item.what_it_does: Validates an inbound dataframe-cache request against the prepared graph/policy, seeds cached node outputs, and computes which downstream nodes the cache fully covers.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. This is ~135 lines of cohesive, self-contained cache-admission logic (key recomputation + 4 distinct ValueError guards, two local closures `_merge_cache_required_columns`/`_required_columns_for_cached_seed`, the cached-seed scan, and the reverse-topo `cache_covers_downstream` fold) physically inlined into the already-785-line orchestrator. None of it touches the per-node execution loop; it only produces three sets (`cached_seed_outputs`, `skip_cache_covered_nodes`, `cache_backed_node_ids`). Its presence inline is the single biggest contributor to _execute_lazy's length and a large share of its cx141.

Both are explicitly thread-able, so the deep nesting (if cache_request -> if key -> with stage -> try/except/else -> if cached_lf, 5-6 deep) is organizational, not essential. (4) _lazy_frame_for_cache raises RuntimeError on multi-port dict (L54-60) INSIDE the try, but try catches ONLY CacheArtifactTooLargeError, so RuntimeError PROPAGATES (fail-loud) — extracted fn must not widen the except. (7/8) CacheArtifactTooLargeError -> warn-and-skip; try/except/ELSE means swap never runs, flag stays False. A naive 'pass int / mutate locally' loses the update and silently DESYNCS the two GC paths — a latent bug. So the refactor is behavior-preserving ONLY via the _GcBatcher/boxed-state route the proposal mentions as an option; the 2-tuple return makes that route mandatory, not optional. Also the listed parameter set is under-specified: it omits cache_backed_node_ids (mutated at L1322, feeds _release_consumed_parents L1005 for later nodes) and execution_facade/_lazy_frame_for_cache/_schema_names_of — these must be threaded or the fn must remain a NESTED closure. (b) _store_and_pin: both call sites have identical fp + 8 slot names + order (store→pin→flag); data differs (merged vs plain) but is passed in; flag stays False on hit since helper is extend/miss-only — exact. item.what_it_does: Maps a node to its ChunkCapability (kind/order/expansion/model-reuse), raising ChunkPlanUnsupportedError for ineligible nodes.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. A 117-line if/elif ladder over `node_type` that re-encodes per-type facts already declared in the `_CHUNK_CAPABILITY_DECLARATIONS` table (status SUPPORTED/CONDITIONAL/UNSUPPORTED). For the SUPPORTED rows (BANDING/OUTPUT/OPTIMISER_APPLY) the body is literally the same `ChunkCapability(kind=MAP_ONLY, preserves_row_order=True)`. The CONDITIONAL rows each repeat the same `raise ChunkPlanUnsupportedError(node_id=..., node_type=node_type.value, ...)` boilerplate around a single guard. The trailing two raises (1220-1231) are unreachable for any declared type because the table is validated complete at import (`validate_chunk_capability_declarations()`), so the fan-in/`not chunk-safe` fallbacks are dead for in-enum types.
item.current_metrics: len=117 cx high (one arm per NodeType); 3 identical SUPPORTED bodies; ~7 near-identical CONDITIONAL raises
item.proposal: Table-drive: (1) for SUPPORTED declarations return the shared MAP_ONLY capability directly from the declaration (the table already says SUPPORTED + MAP_ONLY rule). (2) Keep only the CONDITIONAL node types as explicit cases, but factor the repeated raise into a local `_unsupported(node, reason, **fields)` helper. (3) Delete the trailing `if len(parent_ids) > 1` / generic-raise fallback (1220-1231): every NodeType is in the table, so reaching it is impossible; replace with an `assert_never`-style `raise AssertionError` guarded comment, or rely on the `_CHUNK_CAPABILITY_DECLARATIONS[node_type]` KeyError that already fires first for an unknown type.
item.behavior_preservation: The SUPPORTED rows already construct the exact capability the table implies; pulling it from the table yields the identical ChunkCapability. CONDITIONAL guards keep their exact predicates and error fields. The deleted fallback is provably unreachable because line 1122 `_CHUNK_CAPABILITY_DECLARATIONS[node_type]` raises KeyError before any unknown type could reach 1220, and all known types hit an earlier branch.

verdict.evidence:
Re-read src/haute/chunking.py:1115-1231 (_capability_for_node) plus the declarations table (219-336), validate_chunk_capability_declarations (344-388, called at import 388), ChunkCapability/ChunkCapabilityDeclaration dataclasses (71-91), NodeType enum (_types.py:25-50, 18 members), and the sole caller (chunking.py:767).

ACCURATE CLAIMS:
- SUPPORTED dedup is real. Table has exactly 3 SUPPORTED rows: BANDING(255), OUTPUT(265), OPTIMISER_APPLY(314). Their bodies (1164-1168, 1138-1142, 1183-1187) are byte-identical ChunkCapability(kind=MAP_ONLY, preserves_row_order=True). Collapsing them into one `if declaration.status==SUPPORTED: return ChunkCapability(MAP_ONLY, True)` is provably behavior-preserving.
- Tail (1220-1231) is unreachable for in-enum types. All 18 NodeTypes partition cleanly: 11 UNSUPPORTED -> line 1123; 3 SUPPORTED + 5 CONDITIONAL (DATA_SOURCE/POLARS/MODEL_SCORE/RATING_STEP/SCENARIO_EXPANDER) = 8 -> explicit ladder. None fall through. A non-enum value would die at line 1122 `_CHUNK_CAPABILITY_DECLARATIONS[node_type]` KeyError before reaching the tail. The two tail error strings ("does not yet support fan-in nodes"/"not chunk-safe") are referenced nowhere else (grep) and no test asserts on them, so deletion breaks no existing test.

CAVEATS (why marginal, not sound):
1. The proposal's headline "Delete the trailing fallback (1220-1231)" with "-45 LOC" implies near-total removal, but the tail is a deliberate FAIL-LOUD defense-in-depth guard. If a future dev adds a NodeType to the table as SUPPORTED/CONDITIONAL but forgets the matching ladder branch, today that node hits 1220/1227 and safely raises ChunkPlanUnsupportedError. With the tail deleted and NO terminal raise, the function would fall off the end and return None; that None flows into capabilities[node_id] (777) and capability.row_multiplier (776) -> AttributeError deep in planning. Only the proposal's parenthetical alternative ("assert_never-style raise AssertionError") preserves fail-loud. So the deletion is behavior-preserving ONLY if a terminal AssertionError/assert_never replaces it.
2. est_reduction is inflated. The safe, zero-risk win (SUPPORTED dedup) is ~-8 LOC. The bulk of the claimed -45 comes from the tail, but a correct version must KEEP a terminal raise, recovering few of those LOC. Honest net is ~-10 to -15 LOC.
3. Framing overclaim: the proposal says to "return the shared MAP_ONLY capability directly from the declaration" / "the table already says MAP_ONLY rule" — but ChunkCapabilityDeclaration (84-91) has no ChunkCapability field, only a `_MAP_ONLY_RULE_NAME` rule string. The simplified form must hardcode the capability once in a SUPPORTED branch (still fine, identical object).
4. CONDITIONAL branches kept as-is is correct: DATA_SOURCE has a side effect (_validate_chunkable_source, 1133) and POLARS/SCENARIO_EXPANDER/MODEL_SCORE/RATING_STEP have distinct guards/error fields — none can be table-driven.

Complexity is incidental (SUPPORTED dedup genuinely removable), but the largest claimed savings depend on removing a fail-loud guard whose removal is only safe if replaced by an equivalent terminal raise — and the est_reduction/framing don't reflect that.

Returning `result` directly therefore yields a `.errors` identical to today's 3rd tuple element. Confirmed.

The cache-HIT arm (950-957) reads from the `cached[...]` dict, not `_eager_execute`, so it is untouched. No name collisions; downstream merge/store logic (988-1029, 1060-1071) consumes the same locals.

item.current_metrics: ~6 duplicated lines + 1 duplicated 3-clause guard + duplicated error string
item.proposal: Extract `_usable_ram_bytes(available: int | None = None, *, os_reserve: int | None = None) -> tuple[int, int, int]` returning `(usable, available, reserve)` with the validity guard inside it. item.behavior_preservation: Identical arithmetic and identical guard/exception; `_in_flight_limit_bytes` honours a caller-supplied `budget.os_reserve_bytes`/`available_ram_bytes` by passing them through (same short-circuit it does today). No numeric change.

verdict.est_reduction: -8 LOC; collapses 2 verbatim reserve formulas + 2 identical 3-clause guards + 1 duplicated error string into a single source (drift-proofing).
verdict.repro_path: N/A (read-only audit). Duplication confirmed at src/haute/_execution_admission.py:363-367 vs 550-555; error string "available_ram_bytes must return a positive integer" appears verbatim at lines 364 and 551 (Grep: exactly 2 hits, both in this file).
verdict.evidence:
Complexity is INCIDENTAL, not essential. Re-read both functions in full. _adaptive_default_memory_limit_bytes (361-372): available=available_ram_bytes(); guard(363-364); reserve=min(_resolve_os_reserve_bytes(), max(available//2,1)) (366); usable=max(available-reserve,1) (367); then basis-point math (floor/ceiling) on usable; returns (min(limit,usable), available, reserve). _in_flight_limit_bytes (546-555): available=budget.available_ram_bytes or available_ram_bytes() (547-549); SAME guard(550-551); reserve=budget.os_reserve_bytes or SAME formula (552-554); returns max(available-reserve,1) (==usable). Duplicated: the formula, the usable arithmetic, the 3-clause guard, and the error string (verbatim).

BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING per traced case with proposed _usable_ram_bytes(available=None, *, os_reserve=None) -> (usable, available, reserve):
- Caller A delegates with NO args: both params default None -> always calls patch point + always resolves OS reserve (matches A's unconditional behavior). A keeps its basis-point/floor/ceiling math on the returned usable and returns (min(limit,usable), available, reserve). Ordering preserved: available_ram_bytes() still runs before the _ADAPTIVE_MEMORY_POLICY[profile] lookup because that lookup stays in A after delegation.
- Caller B delegates with _usable_ram_bytes(budget.available_ram_bytes, os_reserve=budget.os_reserve_bytes): the `available is None` and `reserve is None` short-circuits reproduce B's caller-supplied passthrough EXACTLY (same as lines 547-554). B returns usable directly.

This is the one ordering constraint, and the proposal ("guard inside it") satisfies it.
- No numeric change: floor/ceiling/basis-point logic is unique to A and stays in A; the unified helper only produces (usable, available, reserve).

Scope/safety: Grep confirms both functions are module-private with only their two in-file callers (lines 320 and 509). No `_usable_ram_bytes` name collision exists. Caller A calls it with no args then does floor/ceiling/basis-point math on usable; caller B calls it with budget values and returns usable. item.location: src/haute/_execute_lazy.py:1130-1249 (_build_lazy_node) and src/haute/_execute_eager_core (1764-2033) — the contract-check + input-resolution scaffolding
item.what_it_does: Resolve per-edge input frames via _pick_source_frame, run the input-side contract union check (keyed by (source, sourceHandle)), and run the join-dtype check.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL near-duplication across the lazy and eager cores. Both build `incoming_edges`, both compute the per-parent column union for the input contract using the same `(edge.source, edge.sourceHandle)` cache-key scheme, and both call `_assert_simple_join_key_dtypes_compatible(node, input_ids, input_lfs)` under the same `if enforce_contracts`. The lazy version (1178-1204) and eager version (1843-1854) are structurally the same input-contract step written twice with slightly different frame plumbing.
item.current_metrics: ~25 lines of input-contract scaffolding duplicated between the two cores; part of cx141 + cx98
item.proposal: Hoist the input-side contract step into a shared helper `_assert_node_inputs(node, contract, incoming_edges, input_frames, projected_columns, column_cache, columns_of)` used by both cores (the only difference is whether columns come from a projected-cols list or the cache, which the helper can take as parameters). This is a careful extract because the two cores differ in error handling (eager swallows, lazy doesn't) — but the contract assertion itself already raises unconditionally in both, so it is safe to share.
item.behavior_preservation: ContractMismatchError is raised in both paths today regardless of swallow_errors (eager explicitly re-raises ContractMismatchError), so centralising the union+assert does not change which errors propagate. item.est_reduction: -20 LOC net across the two godfunctions; removes a subtle drift surface (multi-port contract keying must stay identical in both cores)

verdict.evidence:
Both cores live in src/haute/_execute_lazy.py: lazy input-contract block _build_lazy_node 1178-1204, eager block _execute_eager_core 1843-1854 (core def at 1553). The GENUINELY shared part is incidental and removable: both key per-edge by (edge.source, edge.sourceHandle) and build frozenset().union(...) of upstream column sets, both gate on `check_here and contract.inputs is not None`, both then call _assert_inputs_satisfy_contract(node, contract, upstream_cols) and, under `if enforce_contracts`, _assert_simple_join_key_dtypes_compatible(node, input_ids, input_lfs). Error-propagation claim is CORRECT: _assert_inputs_satisfy_contract (230-253) raises ContractMismatchError unconditionally and eager re-raises it at 2013-2017 regardless of swallow_errors, so centralising does not change which errors propagate.

BUT the input-resolution differs in essential, silent-wrongness-prone ways the proposal under-specifies: (1) COLUMN SOURCE — lazy per edge prefers projected_cols (the reduced post-_apply_edge_projection set, frozenset(ordered) from line 1059) and only on None falls back to column_cache.get, COMPUTING _columns_of(upstream_lf) and POPULATING the cache on miss (1191-1199); eager reads ONLY column_cache[k], has no projected-cols concept (eager projection is post-execution at 1951-1966, applied at collect time only), and SILENTLY DROPS any key absent via `if k in column_cache` (1849) with NO input_lfs fallback. So on a projected fan-in edge the two unions compute DIFFERENT values: lazy validates the contract against the reduced projected subset, eager against the parent's full output columns (column_cache[(nid,None)]=final_cols, 1967). A naive 'always read from cache' shared helper would silently CHANGE lazy behaviour — masking a real ContractMismatchError when a required input column is projected away. (2) SIDE EFFECT — the lazy block writes column_cache[cache_key] on miss (1197); eager never writes here. (3) MISS POLICY — lazy compute-and-cache vs eager silent-skip. These are 3 behavioural forks a shared helper must parameterise, not a trivial extract. The only pinned test, test_multi_parent_contract_inputs_use_union_of_parent_columns (tests/test_execute_lazy.py:731), uses no edge projection, so the divergence is test-uncovered — the breakage surface is invisible to the suite. The check_here guard wording differs (lazy adds `contract is not None`, eager uses # type: ignore) but is runtime-equivalent since check_here=bool(contract) and _should_check_contract(contract). The proposal also OVER-SCOPES: _assert_simple_join_key_dtypes_compatible is already a shared free function (507) called identically (input_ids, input_lfs) in both cores — it is already deduplicated and needs no hoisting; folding it in couples the dtype check to the contract-union step for no benefit.
verdict.est_reduction: ~-15 to -20 LOC net if done correctly (the union+keying only); not -25, since the dtype helper is already shared and would not shrink
verdict.repro_path: N/A — read-only audit. Divergence demonstrable: a fan-in edge with a projection demand (edge_demands non-None) makes lazy union the reduced frozenset(ordered) (line 1059, used at 1192) while eager unions the full column_cache[(parent,handle)] (1849). No existing test exercises projected fan-in + contract.inputs together, so the difference is unpinned.
verdict.recommended_action: Do NOT extract the proposed broad helper as specified. If pursued, narrow the scope to ONLY the genuinely-identical part: have each core resolve its own per-edge column sets first (lazy keeps its projected_cols-or-cache-with-compute logic; eager keeps its cache-only-skip-missing logic), then call a tiny shared `_union_upstream_columns(col_sets: list[frozenset[str]]) -> frozenset[str]` (the frozenset().union) plus optionally a shared `_input_edge_cache_key(edge)` returning (edge.source, edge.sourceHandle). Leave _assert_simple_join_key_dtypes_compatible alone (already shared). BEFORE any refactor, add a failing-then-passing test that pins the divergence: a projected fan-in edge where the parent's full columns satisfy the input contract but the projected subset does NOT (and vice versa), asserting lazy raises ContractMismatchError on the projected subset while eager validates against full columns — so a future careless merge of the two unions is caught. The broad SIMP-EXEC-09 helper as written is behaviour-preservable only with 3 carefully-wired parameters it under-specifies; modest LOC win vs medium risk on a contract-critical hot path with thin coverage = not worthwhile as proposed.

item.title: Multi-port apiInput node reports timing in seconds while every other node reports milliseconds (≈1000x under-report)
item.location: src/haute/_execute_lazy.py:1902 (multi-port branch of _execute_eager_core) vs the canonical src/haute/_execute_lazy.py:2033
item.failure_scenario: When a node returns a per-port dict (a multi-port apiInput with 2+ emit-true tables), the dict branch sets `timings[nid] = round(t1 - t0, 6)` where `t1 - t0` is in SECONDS, then `continue`s. Every other node path falls through to line 2033 `timings[nid] = round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000, 1)` which is in MILLISECONDS. `EagerResult.timings` is consumed by executor.py:1171/1238 as `timing_ms=timings.get(nid, 0)` and surfaced to the GUI as `NodeResult.timing_ms`. So a multi-port apiInput that actually took 800 ms is reported as `0.8` ms — a ~1000x understatement, and the units silently disagree across node types in the same response. This is the explicit fail-loud-vs-silent-degradation concern: a wrong number shown to the user with no error.

verdict.repro_path: review/03-simplification/repro/execution__BUG-EXEC-01.py
verdict.evidence:
CONFIRMED REAL + NOT a duplicate (catalog.md has 1 execution finding = a resource-leak; zero matches for timing/units/seconds/millisecond/multi-port).

Code-trace (src/haute/_execute_lazy.py, single `for nid in order` loop body starting line 1764):
- L1780  t0 = time.perf_counter()
- L1868  if isinstance(result, dict):   # multi-port apiInput, 2+ emit-true tables
- L1901-1902  t1 = time.perf_counter(); timings[nid] = round(t1 - t0, 6)   # SECONDS
- L1907  continue                       # skips the canonical line below
- L2033  timings[nid] = round((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000, 1)        # MILLISECONDS (every other path)
Grep proves these are the ONLY two `timings[nid] =` writes in the file; the dict branch's `continue` is the last-but-one statement before 2033 (the final loop statement), so it deterministically bypasses the ms conversion. No `*1000` / `/1000` normalization exists for the dict case anywhere.

Consumer (no unit conversion): executor.py:1238 `timing_ms=timings.get(nid, 0)` (also 1171/1194/1202) -> NodeResult.timing_ms (schemas.py:242, plain float) -> routes/pipeline.py:592 NodeTimingInfo(timing_ms=r.timing_ms). For a real (status="ok") multi-port node the seconds value is surfaced verbatim as milliseconds.

Executed repro (uv run python ..., EXIT=0): faithful transcription of the gating + both assignment lines + the consumer line.
- Deterministic fake clock, 800 ms node: multi-port timings[nid]=0.8, single-port=800.0; timing_ms 0.8 vs 800.0; ratio exactly 1000.0x for the SAME real duration. Asserted mp_timing_ms == 0.8 and sp_timing_ms == 800.0.
- Real wall-clock cross-check (~30 ms busy-wait, not a fake-clock artifact): multi-port=0.030009 (seconds), single-port=30.0 (ms); asserted real_sp > real_mp*100.

This is exactly the project's fail-loud-vs-silent-degradation concern: a wrong number (~1000x under-report) shown to the user with no error, and units silently disagree across node types within one response.
verdict.recommended_action: Fix (one-liner): delete L1901-1902 and let the multi-port dict branch fall through to the canonical L2033 (remove the early `continue` at L1907, or convert to ms before continuing: `timings[nid] = round((t1 - t0) * 1000, 1)`). Falling through to 2033 is cleanest since it already recomputes from t0. TDD per CLAUDE.md: add a failing test asserting a multi-port apiInput's reported timing_ms is in the same (ms) unit/order-of-magnitude as a sibling single-port node before fixing; guard against regression of the units-agree invariant. refined_severity=low (claimed severity is correct): genuine silent ~1000x wrong observability value, but bounded — affects only the multi-port apiInput (2+ emit-true tables) timing display, corrupts no data/results, and under-reports rather than false-alarms.

item.title: Preamble compile error is injected only into POLARS/LIVE_SWITCH nodes, but ratingStep/scenarioExpander/explore/dataSource/externalFile builders also consume the preamble — those nodes fail with an opaque NameError instead of the real cause
item.location: src/haute/executor.py:1326 (`preamble_types = {NodeType.POLARS, NodeType.LIVE_SWITCH}` in _eager_execute) vs src/haute/_builders.py:831 (rating_step passes extra_ns=_preamble) and :899 (scenario_expander passes extra_ns=_preamble); preamble also captured by _build_data_source:522, _build_explore:689, _build_external_file:719
item.failure_scenario: If the pipeline preamble fails to compile, `_eager_execute` (executor.py:1294-1306) swallows the PreambleError, sets `preamble_ns = {}`, and records `preamble_error`. It then injects that error message ONLY into nodes whose `nodeType in {POLARS, LIVE_SWITCH}` (line 1326-1331). But `_build_rating_step` and `_build_scenario_expander` execute user code with `extra_ns=_preamble` (the same preamble namespace). With `preamble_ns={}`, a ratingStep/scenarioExpander whose user code references a preamble-defined helper (e.g. `my_factor(...)`) raises `NameError: name 'my_factor' is not defined` deep in `_exec_user_code`, which is swallowed by the eager path and surfaced as that node's error. The user sees a confusing per-node NameError on the ratingStep card with no indication the true root cause is a broken preamble — whereas an adjacent POLARS node would correctly show the preamble error. The injection set is stale relative to the builders that actually bind the preamble.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\execution__BUG-EXEC-02.py
verdict.evidence: Repro drives the REAL haute._eager_execute on synthetic in-memory graphs (broken preamble: `import a_module_that_does_not_exist_zzz` + `def my_factor()`), exit 0. The claim's load-bearing asymmetry ("ratingStep shows opaque NameError WHEREAS an adjacent POLARS node would correctly show the preamble error") is REFUTED by the injection guard at src/haute/executor.py:1330: `if nd and nd.data.nodeType in preamble_types and nid not in errors:` — injection fires ONLY for nodes that did NOT already fail. SCENARIO A (both POLARS and ratingStep reference the broken helper): poly error == rat error == "name 'my_factor' is not defined" (FULLY SYMMETRIC — POLARS is equally opaque, it does NOT show the preamble error). SCENARIO B (POLARS preamble-free, ratingStep uses helper): poly shows "Preamble line 1: No module named 'a_module_that_does_not_exist_zzz'" while rat shows "name 'my_factor' is not defined" — but this asymmetry exists ONLY because the two nodes run DIFFERENT code. The clean preamble error is an INJECTED annotation on a POLARS node that SUCCEEDED (didn't need the preamble); a ratingStep that equally doesn't reference the failed symbol simply succeeds with status="ok". NodeResult.error = errors[nid] verbatim (executor.py:1169), so no special POLARS rewriting exists. Verified facts the claim got right: the 5 builders bind preamble via extra_ns (_builders.py:522/599 dataSource, 689/696 explore, 719/724 externalFile, 818/831 ratingStep, 870/899 scenarioExpander) and preamble_types={POLARS,LIVE_SWITCH} (executor.py:1326) omits them. Existing tests (test_executor.py:2375, 4228-4382) confirm the INTENDED design: injection surfaces the preamble error only on POLARS/LIVE_SWITCH nodes whose code does NOT reference the broken helper. Claim is NOT in catalog.md (checked all 69 numbered findings + refuted section; preamble entries #8/#15/#48 are unrelated) — but novelty is moot given refutation of the failure scenario.
verdict.recommended_action: Reject as filed. The stated failure scenario does not occur: under the like-for-like comparison the claim relies on, a POLARS node referencing the same broken-preamble helper is exactly as opaque (identical NameError) as the ratingStep — the `nid not in errors` guard (executor.py:1330) suppresses injection for any node that already failed, so there is no "adjacent POLARS node correctly shows the preamble error" to contrast against. The only genuine residual is that ratingStep/scenarioExpander/dataSource/explore/externalFile nodes that bind the preamble but do NOT reference the failed symbol miss the advisory "preamble is broken" annotation that POLARS/LIVE_SWITCH receive when they succeed — a low/cosmetic advisory inconsistency that is the INVERSE of (and far milder than) the claimed "opaque NameError hides the real cause" harm. If desired as a polish-only cleanup, add those five NodeTypes to preamble_types so a still-succeeding preamble-consumer also shows the advisory; but this is not the medium-severity error-attribution bug described, and the claimed repro path (ratingStep NameError vs adjacent clean POLARS preamble error) is not reproducible.
verdict.est_reduction: n/a (refuted — no fix warranted; optional 1-line advisory polish only)

item.title: _compute_boundary_check_exceptions builds and returns an exception tuple that no caller uses; _is_boundary_check_exception re-implements the same membership independently — latent drift if one is edited
item.failure_scenario: `_compute_boundary_check_exceptions()` constructs `tuple(exc_types)` (ConfigError, OSError, and optionally MlflowException) but a whole-module read shows the only consumer of boundary-check classification is `_is_boundary_check_exception`, which re-derives the same set via `isinstance(exc, (ConfigError, OSError))` plus its own MlflowException import — it does NOT call `_compute_boundary_check_exceptions`. The risk is silent drift: a future change adding e.g. `TimeoutError` to one function but not the other would make the boundary-check swallow set inconsistent between the (unused) tuple and the (live) predicate, and the discrepancy would not be caught because nothing ties them together. Not a wrong-price bug, but a fail-loud-adjacent maintainability hazard in the exact code that decides which exceptions get silently downgraded to opaque contracts.

verdict.evidence: Repo-wide grep + AST walk of src/haute/_execute_lazy.py: `_compute_boundary_check_exceptions` (def line 130) has ZERO call sites anywhere in src/, tests/, review/ — not exported via __all__, not dynamically dispatched, not tested. The only live boundary-check consumer is `_is_boundary_check_exception` (line 167), called at _execute_lazy.py:207 inside `_effective_contract`. That predicate re-derives the same set independently: `isinstance(exc, (ConfigError, OSError))` + its own `from mlflow.exceptions import MlflowException` (lines 169-177), never consulting the builder's tuple. Executed repro PART A asserts the builder is uncalled in the module AST; PART B shows the two are currently in sync (so nothing forces them to stay so); PART C simulates a one-sided edit adding a new recoverable error class to the builder only -> builder_says_recoverable=True vs predicate_says_recoverable=False, and the REAL `_is_boundary_check_exception(BackendUnreachableError(...))` still returns False, proving builder edits are silently inert. Repro exits 0. NOTABLE: the bug report's own example `TimeoutError` does NOT demonstrate drift — running the script surfaced that TimeoutError subclasses OSError and is already accepted by both classifiers (first run failed at PART C with 'unedited predicate still excludes it'); the divergence manifests only for genuinely-new exception classes, which is the realistic drift scenario. Not present in review/02-findings/catalog.md (no BUG-EXEC-03 / boundary-check match) -> NEW.
verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\execution__BUG-EXEC-03.py
verdict.recommended_action: Collapse the duplicated classification into a single source of truth: rewrite `_is_boundary_check_exception` as `return isinstance(exc, _compute_boundary_check_exceptions())`, OR delete `_compute_boundary_check_exceptions` entirely and keep only the inlined predicate. Either eliminates the dead builder and makes drift structurally impossible. Add a one-line unit test asserting the chosen single classifier accepts ConfigError/OSError(/MlflowException) and rejects KeyError/TypeError/RuntimeError/ImportError so any future membership change is pinned. Prefer unification over leaving dead code, per CLAUDE.md fail-loud guidance.

item.proposal: Decompose into one cohesive private helper per concern, each taking `(step, ...) -> None` and owning its own try/except: `_enrich_passthrough_expression`, `_enrich_target_expression`, `_enrich_expression_chain`, `_enrich_input_sources`, `_enrich_node_detail`, `_enrich_row_lineage`. CORRECT, SOUND parts of the proposal:
- `if True:` at 1697 is an unconditional no-op wrapping BOTH the node-detail try (1698-1768) and the row-lineage try (1771-1815) at the same indent. Python `if True:` introduces no new scope, so de-indenting the body is provably behavior-preserving (names like `detail`, `parent_ids`, `operation_type` stay in the same function scope; `parent_ids` is independently reassigned at 1772 anyway). This single change is safe.
- The repeated `if step.calculation is None: step.calculation = {}` + marker boilerplate (1556,1606,1648,1672,1690 and the setdefault sites) is genuine incidental duplication; per-concern helpers are a reasonable shape.

WHY ONLY MARGINAL / behavior hazards the literal proposal introduces:
1. The "~7 INDEPENDENT concerns" framing is inaccurate. Concerns 2-5 (target-expression parse+eval 1493-1549, expression-chain 1552-1614, input-sources 1617-1674, rename 1677-1694) are NOT independent: they are all nested under the SINGLE guard `if column and (_col_in_schema or _col_in_code):` (1493) and are threaded through shared mutable state with order-dependent reads. Chain (1613) setdefault("error") deliberately must run AFTER eval's overwrite to avoid clobbering the more-specific eval error. A faithful refactor MUST call the helpers in the same order under the same outer predicate; a naive "small loop over independent concerns" would break the read-after-write chain. Decomposition is achievable but only by preserving exact ordering and the shared guard — more constrained than the proposal implies.

It says collapse "~10 ... logger.warning + setdefault('error',...) blocks" into one `_annotate_step_error` and preserves precedence "by keeping setdefault in the shared annotator." But grep of the error sites shows TWO distinct semantics: OVERWRITE via plain assignment at 1510 (parse fail), 1545 (eval fail), 1764 (node-detail fail), and 1481/1485 (passthrough when field is None) vs SETDEFAULT at 1483/1487, 1613/1614, 1673/1674, 1691, 1836/1837. item.what_it_does: "Instance resolution": when a node is an instance whose own code lacks `.with_columns(`, fall back to the original (instanceOf) node's code.

item.proposal: Extract `_resolve_node_code(cfg: dict, node_map: Mapping) -> str` that returns the (possibly instance-resolved) raw code string, and call it at all three sites. This also gives one home for the `isinstance(config, dict)` guard that is repeated alongside it.

verdict.evidence: The proposal's premise is factually wrong: the three sites are NOT mere variable-renames of one idiom. Sites 1 (src/haute/_trace_enrichment.py:1116-1120) and 3 (1440-1444) assign unconditionally: `raw = orig_cfg.get("code","") or ""` / `u_raw = u_orig.get("code","") or ""`. Site 2 (1392-1398) has an EXTRA guard: `orig_code = orig_cfg.get("code","") or ""; if orig_code: raw_code = orig_code`. So Site 2 only adopts the original node's code when it is non-empty; Sites 1/3 overwrite even with empty. Diverging input: an instance node (instanceOf truthy + in node_map) whose own code lacks `.with_columns(`, where the original node's code is empty/missing but the instance's OWN code is non-empty (e.g. a `.filter(...)` dot-chain). Expect cx ~37->~28-30 for the safe subset.
verdict.repro_path: Trace compute_prepared_plan (src/haute/projection.py:2138-2356), Phase B = 2244-2349. (1) Edge-loop+contribution block appears at 2252-2266 (routed_demands), 2294-2308 (edge_join_demands), 2329-2343 (fan_in_demands). (2) Verify ParentDemandResult is @dataclass(frozen=True) at 248 -> reconstructing ParentDemandResult(default=X.default, by_parent=X.by_parent, rule_name=X.rule_name) is observationally identical to assigning X. (3) Verify message literals feed only edge_reasons -> _freeze_plan(2363)/explain(2401), never control flow. (4) Trace the NON-edge-loop arms: my_needed is None at 2268 (calls _raise_if_unbounded_user_code_is_terminal then writes opaque contribution), opaque_demands at 2309-2319, contract_algebra fall-through at 2345-2349.
verdict.evidence:
PARTLY SOUND, PARTLY UNSOUND.

SOUND part: The `_record_parent_contribution` extraction is behavior-preserving for the three edge-loop arms (routed/edge_join/fan_in). The blocks are textually identical except the ProjectionReason `message` literal, which is display-only metadata (it lands in edge_reasons, consumed by _freeze_plan/explain, never by demand math or control flow). The None-vs-fresh-set semantics `None if parent_demand is None else set(parent_demand)` and the contribution reconstruction are reproducible exactly by a helper. Because ParentDemandResult is @dataclass(frozen=True) (line 248), the existing `ParentDemandResult(default=X.default, by_parent=X.by_parent, rule_name=X.rule_name)` is identical to assigning X, so the helper choosing either is safe. The Phase-A split into `_resolve_node_demand` (2159-2242) is a clean structural unit. These are real, low-risk wins.

THREE FACTUAL ERRORS in the proposal: (a) The pattern is written THREE times, not four. Grep for `edge_demands[(parent_id, node_id)]` returns exactly 3 hits (2254, 2296, 2331). The opaque-contract arm (2314) and contract_algebra arm (2345) write `contribution` WITHOUT the edge loop, so a careless application of the helper to those arms would ADD edge_demands/edge_reasons entries that do not currently exist -> behavior change. (b) The behavior_preservation note 'the arms are still tried in the same order with the same continue semantics' glosses over that the arms are NOT a flat chain. (c) est cx 37->18 is unachievable from the safe extractions.

UNSOUND part (the 'collapse routed->edge_join->opaque-contract->fan_in into an ordered list of callables evaluated until one returns non-None'): the ladder is NOT a first_non_None chain. Two essential, order-sensitive guards break the flat-callable model:
  1) Arm `my_needed is None` (2268-2279) sits BETWEEN routed_demands and the edge_join branch. It is keyed on `my_needed is None` (not on a rule returning non-None), calls the side-effecting `_raise_if_unbounded_user_code_is_terminal(...)` which can raise, writes an opaque contribution, and continues. If folded into an ordered-callable chain it would be skipped, and control would reach `set(my_needed)` at 2289 with my_needed=None -> TypeError. This arm MUST remain a distinct early guard.
  2) The edge_join vs fan_in selection is gated by `produced is None or referenced is None` (2282). edge_join_demands is tried only inside that gate; opaque_contract_demands_for_node is the UNCONDITIONAL fallback there (it returns a ParentDemandResult, never None, with no edge loop). fan_in_demands is tried only in the ELSE branch, and depends on `base_contribution = (my_needed - produced) | referenced` (2321) which is only computable when produced/referenced are concrete. So edge_join and fan_in live in mutually exclusive branches and consume branch-local, conditionally-computed args. The helper signatures confirm this: parent_demands_for_node(node, parent_ids, my_needed, seeded_required); edge_join_fan_in_demands_for_node(node, parent_ids, set(my_needed), set(), parent_produced, strict_projection=...) needs parent_produced built at 2283-2285; fan_in_demands_for_node(node, parent_ids, base_contribution, referenced, strict_projection=...). A uniform `result = first_non_None(fns...)` cannot be built without thunks closing over parent_produced/base_contribution/referenced, which forces the same branching to run anyway. Implemented literally as described, the collapse changes behavior (NoneType crash on opaque nodes; wrong rule when produced/referenced are concrete).

CONCLUSION: incidental duplication (the edge loop) is genuinely removable and behavior-preserving; but the rule-SELECTION machinery is ESSENTIAL complexity (mutually-exclusive produced/referenced branches, a side-effecting raise guard on my_needed is None, branch-local arg derivation), and the proposal's flagship metrics depend on collapsing it. Do the helper + Phase-A split; do NOT flatten the ladder.
verdict.recommended_action: Accept ONLY the scoped helper extractions; reject the rule-ladder collapse as written. Specifically: (1) Extract `_record_parent_contribution(node_id, demands, message, *, edge_demands, edge_reasons, contribution)` and apply it to EXACTLY the three edge-loop arms (routed_demands 2252, edge_join_demands 2294, fan_in_demands 2329) — do NOT apply it to the opaque-contract (2309) or contract_algebra (2345) arms, which must keep writing contribution without populating edge_demands. (2) Extract Phase A (2159-2242) into `_resolve_node_demand`. (3) Do NOT collapse the routed/edge_join/opaque/fan_in selection into a first_non_None callable list: preserve the `my_needed is None` early guard (with its _raise_if_unbounded_user_code_is_terminal side effect) and the `produced is None or referenced is None` bifurcation as explicit branches. (4) Per CLAUDE.md TDD: before refactoring, add/confirm tests covering (a) the unprojected-boundary raise path on a terminal unbounded-user-code node, (b) the produced/referenced-None vs concrete bifurcation selecting edge_join vs fan_in respectively, (c) None-vs-set identity (edge_demands entries must be fresh set copies, not aliases of by_parent values), and (d) that opaque/contract_algebra nodes produce NO edge_demands entries. Correct the proposal's '4 times' to '3 times' and downgrade the est cx claim.

item.what_it_does: Single-row evaluation dispatch for a Polars method call: maps `.fill_null/.round/.abs/.clip/.is_null/.cast/.sum/...` etc. onto Python on the already-evaluated receiver value.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: a 25+ arm `if method == 'x': ...` ladder (cx85) where the overwhelming majority of arms are one of three shapes: (a) identity passthrough `return self.evaluate(receiver)` (cast, alias, over, shift, diff, sum, mean, min, max, count, first, last, std, var, median, null_count, n_unique), (b) `val = eval(receiver); if val is None: return None; return f(val)` (abs, log, sqrt, is_null, is_not_null), (c) value+arg combinators (round, clip, fill_null, is_between, is_in). The `.dt.*` and `.str.*` sub-ladders are separate nested ladders.
item.current_metrics: len=216 cx=85 nest=7 params=2
item.proposal: Table-drive: define module-level dicts `_IDENTITY_METHODS = frozenset({...})`, `_UNARY_VALUE_FUNCS = {'abs': abs, 'log': _safe_log, 'sqrt': _safe_sqrt, 'is_null': ..., 'is_not_null': ...}`, and route `.dt`/`.str` via `_DT_ATTRS`/`_STR_METHODS` lookup tables. The `_call` body becomes: resolve method; if in identity set -> evaluate(receiver); elif in unary table -> apply; else fall to the handful of genuinely structural arms (clip/round/fill_null/replace/when/then). The pl.* prefix handling (col/lit/when/horizontal/format) stays as a small head block.
item.behavior_preservation: Each table entry reproduces the exact arm including its None-guard and domain guard (e.g. log only for val>0, sqrt for val>=0) by storing guarded callables; ordering between mutually-exclusive method names is irrelevant since dispatch is keyed by the literal method name, identical to the if-ladder. The receiver/keyword evaluation order for the structural arms (clip/round) is left untouched.

verdict.evidence:
Re-read _call in full (src/haute/_expression_parser.py:1706-1921) plus the non-overriding subclass _BranchTrackingEvaluator (2064-2135, overrides only _eval_clauses/_check_nested_when/_eval_when_from_then_or_otherwise — NOT _call, so when/then/otherwise routing must be preserved). The complexity is largely INCIDENTAL: the ~17 identity arms (cast/alias 1743-1748; over/shift/diff and sum..n_unique 1862-1885) are pure `return self.evaluate(receiver)` and collapse safely to a frozenset membership test — a real, worthwhile, low-risk win and the bulk of the LOC. BUT the proposal as written is NOT provably behavior-preserving; its taxonomy mischaracterizes 4 arms and omits one:
(1) fill_nan (1758-1763) appears NOWHERE in the proposal — not identity, not group (b), and absent from the residual list 'clip/round/fill_null/replace/when/then'. Implemented to spec it falls through to default `evaluate(receiver)`, silently dropping the NaN-replacement branch (1760-1762). This breaks test_fill_nan_eval_replaces (tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py:1431, asserts fill_nan(0) on NaN == 0). Unsound-as-written on its own.
(2) is_null (1834-1836: `return val is None`) and is_not_null (1839-1841: `return val is not None`) are listed under shape (b) ('if val is None: return None; return f(val)'). Shape (b) returns None for null input; these predicates must return True/False for null input. The stated template inverts the null case — the proposal's group definition contradicts its own membership list. Only a fully self-contained callable taking raw val (incl. None) preserves behavior, NOT the described template.
(3) dt (1804-1817) and str (1819-1831) blocks dispatch on `receiver.attr == 'dt'/'str'`, NOT on `method`. The proposal's core correctness claim ('dispatch is keyed by the literal method name, identical to the if-ladder') is false for these: a method-keyed _DT_ATTRS/_STR_METHODS table would route bare `.year()`/`.contains()` (no namespace) — currently default-passthrough returning the base value — into extraction. Plus load-bearing guards must be preserved: getattr(...,None) for year/month/day vs `if hasattr(base_val,'days')` for total_days; isinstance(base_val,str) for str; contains' `pattern in base_val if pattern else False` (falsy pattern -> False) and no-arg -> None.
(4) is_in (1854-1860): no-args path falls through to default `evaluate(receiver)` returning the base value, asserted by test_is_in_no_args (line 2997-3000, expects non-None); listing it as a clean combinator understates this.
None are intrinsically unfixable — a careful implementer storing self-contained guarded callables AND explicitly keeping fill_nan/round/clip/fill_null + the dt/str namespace blocks could be behavior-preserving — but the proposal as specified would introduce at least one test-failing regression (fill_nan) and mis-states the keying invariant. The current arms are already linear and individually commented, so the marginal readability gain over the non-identity arms is small relative to the concentration of subtle guards into callables.
verdict.est_reduction: Realistic safe scope (identity frozenset + abs as one None-guarded entry): _call ~216->~150 LOC, cx ~85->~45. The proposal's claimed ~90 LOC / cx~25 is only reachable by also table-driving dt/str/predicates, which is where the behavior-preservation defects concentrate.
verdict.repro_path: Implement proposal literally (route everything not in identity/unary tables to the listed residual arms clip/round/fill_null/replace/when/then) -> run `python -m pytest tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py -k "fill_nan_eval_replaces or is_null or is_not_null or is_in_no_args"`. test_fill_nan_eval_replaces fails (returns NaN instead of 0); is_null/is_not_null on None return None instead of True/False if shape-(b) template is used verbatim.
verdict.recommended_action: Scope down and proceed under TDD only. Land the safe core: introduce module-level _IDENTITY_METHODS = frozenset({cast,alias,over,shift,diff,sum,mean,min,max,count,first,last,std,var,median,null_count,n_unique}) and route via one membership check; optionally add abs as a single None-guarded unary entry. KEEP as explicit code: fill_nan, fill_null, round, clip, is_between, is_in, is_null/is_not_null (predicates), and the dt/str namespace blocks (they key on receiver.attr and carry distinct guards). If dt/str/predicate tables are still desired, store fully self-contained callables that accept the raw value including None, and key dt/str on the receiver namespace exactly as today — but treat that as a separate, higher-risk change. Gate the whole change on the existing tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py suite (esp. test_fill_nan_eval_replaces, test_is_in_no_args, the is_null/is_not_null, log/sqrt domain-guard, and clip lower_bound/upper_bound cases) staying green; do NOT lower coverage. Do not adopt the proposal as written.

item.what_it_does: When the traced column is a pass-through at the target step, scan upstream steps for the creating step and parse+evaluate ITS expression onto the target step.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: this 67-line inline block re-implements, with its own copy of instance-resolution and its own nested try/except, exactly the upstream-creator search that `_build_input_sources` already does generically (find upstream step where `ref_col in columns_added`, parse its code, evaluate). It also re-derives `u_combined` and duplicates the error-payload dual-write onto expression+calculation.
item.current_metrics: block len=67, nested within the cx104 function; nest depth reaches ~8 here
item.proposal: Replace the inline scan with a call to a small `_upstream_creator_expression(column, step, steps, node_map, preamble_ns)` helper (which can share the upstream-search + instance-resolution from SIMP-2). Drop the bespoke dual error-write in favour of the SIMP-1 annotator.
item.behavior_preservation: The helper performs the same reversed/forward search for the first upstream step that added the column and the same parse_expression/evaluate_expression calls with the same `{**input_values, **output_values}` value map; only target step gets written, exactly as today. Guarded by the same `column and not _col_in_schema and step is target and column in columns_passed` precondition.
item.est_reduction: ~-50 LOC in the hotspot, removes ~3 nesting levels

verdict.evidence:
Re-read the cited inline block src/haute/_trace_enrichment.py:1422-1488 and the sibling _build_input_sources (1034-1193) it claims to duplicate.

CURRENT inline behavior (case-by-case):
- Guard: column truthy AND not _col_in_schema (not added/modified at target) AND step.node_id==steps[-1].node_id (target step) AND column in step.schema_diff.columns_passed (1422-1427).
- Search: `for upstream in steps` is FORWARD over ALL steps (incl. any after target), skip identity (1428-1430). Matches FIRST upstream where `column in upstream.schema_diff.columns_added` — columns_added ONLY, NOT columns_modified (1431). => picks the EARLIEST creator.
- Instance resolution inlined (1440-1444); _wrap_node_code (1445).
- Value map u_combined = {**upstream.input_values, **upstream.output_values} (1448-1451).
- parse_expression -> writes step.expression only if parsed.expression_text truthy (1452-1454); evaluate_expression -> writes step.calculation if ev is not None (1455-1462). Writes ONLY the target step.
- except: logs upstream_expression_failed, builds err_payload {error, error_type, upstream_node_id}, dual-writes to BOTH step.expression and step.calculation (full dict if None else setdefault('error',...)) (1463-1487).
- `break` is OUTSIDE `if u_code:` => breaks on first columns_added match even if creator has no code (1488).

WHERE THE PROPOSAL WOULD CHANGE BEHAVIOR (the searches are NOT identical, contrary to 'exactly re-implements _build_input_sources'):
1. Direction + match-set DIVERGE. _build_input_sources uses `reversed(all_steps[:current_step_index])` and matches columns_added OR columns_modified (1070-1078) => picks the LATEST creator/modifier. The inline block is FORWARD + columns_added-only => EARLIEST creator. For a column added once then modified upstream-of-target, or added/shadowed twice, these select DIFFERENT upstream steps and yield DIFFERENT expression/calculation on the target. The proposal's own wording is hedged ('same reversed/forward search'), so a literal reuse of _build_input_sources's search is a real (edge-case) behavior change. No test guards this.
2. Output contract differs: _build_input_sources returns dict[col->source_info] and RECURSES to max_depth=3 building nested input_sources (1176-1191); the inline block writes parsed expr/calc directly onto the target step and does NOT recurse. A naive reuse would add nested input_sources and change shape.
3. break-on-first-added-even-without-code semantics (1488) is not naturally reproduced by the recursive helper.
4. Error surfacing: 'drop the bespoke dual error-write in favour of the SIMP-1 annotator' alters the payload — the unique `upstream_node_id` key (1475, confirmed not pinned by any test) and the both-fields dual-write. The SIMP-1 annotator does NOT exist (no _annotate_error/_surface_error in src). So this would silently change error output.
5. DEPENDENCIES MISSING: _upstream_creator_expression does not exist; the SIMP-2 instance-resolution helper does not exist (instanceOf resolution is inlined in 3 places: lines 1116, 1392, 1440). This is net-new shared code, not extraction of an existing generic.

WHAT IS GENUINELY INCIDENTAL (supports 'marginal' not 'unsound'): the instance-resolution duplication (3 inline copies) is a clean extract target, and a thin _upstream_creator_expression helper would legitimately flatten ~3 nesting levels out of the cx104 hotspot. So the core idea has merit; the premise of 'exact' equivalence with _build_input_sources is overstated.

TEST EVIDENCE: tests/test_trace_calculation_hero.py:295 test_passthrough_no_expression pins expression=None for a source-added pass-through (consistent with current). tests/test_trace_coverage.py:467 test_column_tracing_passthrough_column checks only column_relevant, not the enrichment payload. No test pins the upstream_node_id error key or the forward/added-only selection — so the risky behaviors are UNGUARDED, which under the project's fail-loudly / no-silent-change rule weighs against calling it 'sound'.

CONCLUSION: Worthwhile dedup exists, but as written the proposal (a) overstates equivalence with _build_input_sources, (b) depends on two non-existent helpers, and (c) its 'reversed/forward' + 'drop dual error-write' framing would change which upstream step is selected and change error surfacing — both unguarded. Sound ONLY if the helper preserves FORWARD + columns_added-only + first-match-break + the exact dual-write error payload (or an annotator proven to emit identical keys incl. upstream_node_id). Not sound unconditionally.
verdict.est_reduction: ~-40 to -50 LOC in the hotspot and ~3 nesting levels removed IF a dedicated _upstream_creator_expression helper is written; NOT achievable by literally reusing _build_input_sources (different direction/match-set/output-contract/recursion). The shared instance-resolution extract additionally removes ~2 of 3 duplicated inlinings.
verdict.repro_path: Behavior-divergence is reachable via a graph where the traced column is added at an early upstream node and modified (or re-added) at a later upstream node, then passes through to the target step: forward+added-only selects the earliest creator's expression, whereas a reversed+added-or-modified search (as in _build_input_sources) selects the later modifier. No existing test exercises this; a new failing test would pin step.expression/step.calculation for such a pipeline.
verdict.recommended_action: Proceed only with a carefully-scoped extraction, not a reuse of _build_input_sources. Specifically: (1) Land SIMP-2 first — extract a shared instance-resolution+code-wrap helper (resolve raw code via instanceOf, then _wrap_node_code) and use it in all 3 sites (1116, 1392, 1440); this alone is the clearly-incidental, safe dedup. (2) For the pass-through block, extract a dedicated _upstream_creator_expression(column, step, steps, node_map, preamble_ns) that PRESERVES the exact current semantics: FORWARD iteration over steps, match columns_added ONLY, first-match break (even when creator has no code), value map {**upstream.input_values, **upstream.output_values}, write only the target step, and NO recursion. (3) Do NOT route error surfacing through a not-yet-existing SIMP-1 annotator unless that annotator provably emits the identical payload including the upstream_node_id key and the dual-write-on-both-fields behavior. (4) BEFORE refactoring, add characterization tests that pin: (a) forward/earliest-creator selection vs a later upstream modifier, (b) the upstream_node_id error key and both-fields dual-write on a parse/eval failure, (c) the no-expression result when the creator is a code-free source. Without these guards the refactor is an unverified behavior change and should be rejected.

verdict.evidence: Split the item in two. PART A (delete dead stubs `_eval_when_chain`@1923 and `_eval_chained_when`@1933; inline `return None` at `_call` arms 1732 `pl.when` and 1903 chained `.when`): SOUND and provably behavior-preserving. Reason: the `.then()`/`.otherwise()` entry at 1907 routes to `_eval_when_from_then_or_otherwise`, which builds clauses STRUCTURALLY via `_collect_eval_clauses` (AST walk) and `_eval_clauses` only ever calls evaluate() on the cond/then/otherwise SUB-nodes, never on the `pl.when(...)` Call node itself, so arms 1732/1903 are unreachable in normal eval. Even if reached (malformed outermost `pl.when(cond)` with no `.then()`), the stub only returns None, so inlining `return None` is byte-identical. The two tests named '...returns None' (test_eval_when_returns_none@2554, test_eval_when_chain_standalone@3116) actually assert end-to-end `.then()` results (`result_value == 1` / `== "pos"`) via the real chain path, NOT the stub return, so they pass after deletion; only their docstring line-number references go stale. The subclass is NOT a single mark-the-branch hook: on a taken `then` it (1) computes `has_nested=_check_nested_when(then_node)` and sets taken state BEFORE `result=self.evaluate(then_node)`, then (2) AFTER that recursive eval, if `has_nested and is_outer`, appends `self.taken_branch or "then"` to `nested_branches` and re-sets taken_branch/index/dimmed (2098-2104). This pre-eval-set + post-eval-append is interleaved with the recursive evaluate() on the same instance and relies on `self._is_outer` being flipped False (2094) so the nested call doesn't clobber outer state. A single callback fired before evaluating `then` cannot perform the post-eval `nested_branches` work, and the signature `(kind,index,total)` lacks then_node/has_nested/result. Golden outputs that must be preserved (captured via _evaluate_conditional_branches): nested-then-taken -> {taken_branch:'then', idx:0, dimmed:[1], nested:['then']}; nested-otherwise-taken (y=2) -> same nested:['then']. item.what_it_does: Each node-type enricher returns a detail dict, wrapped in `try/except Exception` that logs `enrichment_failed` and returns a per-type degraded dict.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: every enricher repeats the identical outer scaffold: `try: <body> except Exception as exc: logger.warning('enrichment_failed', node_type=<t>, error=str(exc), error_type=type(exc).__name__, exc_info=True); return {detail_type:<t>, error: f'... failed: {exc}', error_type:..., <type-specific null fields>}`. item.current_metrics: ~5 functions each carry ~10 lines of identical error scaffold
item.proposal: Introduce a decorator `@_enricher(detail_type, **null_fields)` that wraps the body in the standard try/except and emits the standard degraded dict (merging `null_fields`). Each enricher body shrinks to just the success path. This also guarantees the degraded-dict shape stays consistent across enrichers (today they drift, e.g. some include `pruned_branches`, some not).

verdict.evidence:
The complexity IS incidental for FOUR of the cited functions, but the proposal as written is NOT byte-identical and over-scopes to a fifth that cannot use the decorator.

CODE-TRACE of the cited degraded paths in src/haute/_trace_enrichment.py:
- enrich_banding (629-645): except -> log enrichment_failed(node_type="banding") + return {detail_type:"banding", error:"banding enrichment failed: {exc}", error_type, selected_band:None, rule_index:-1, is_default:False, input_value:None}.
- enrich_model_score (725-740): node_type="model_score"; error:"model score enrichment failed: {exc}"; nulls {prediction_value:None, prediction_column:"", feature_columns:[]}.
- enrich_scenario_expansion (771-785): node_type="scenario_expander"; error:"scenario expansion enrichment failed: {exc}"; nulls {scenario_value:None, scenario_column:""}; success detail_type is also "scenario_expander".
- enrich_live_switch (818-833): node_type="live_switch"; error:"live switch enrichment failed: {exc}"; nulls {active_branch:"", active_scenario:"", pruned_branches:[]}.
These four are genuinely uniform scaffold (try -> body; except Exception -> identical log shape + per-type degraded dict). A decorator can reproduce them — the failure dicts are NOT pinned by any test (grep of tests/test_trace_enrichment.py found no assertion on these error strings/keys; only line 3894 checks the model_score sub-explanation error does NOT bubble to the outer catch), so consolidation is low-risk for these four.

TWO concrete defects in the proposal as written:
1) WRONG-TYPE FUNCTION INCLUDED. The location field and "x5 enrichers" include detect_row_lineage_type (870-936). Its success path returns a bare str ("created"/"selected"/.../"passthrough") and its except path returns a STRING f"error: row lineage enrichment failed: {exc}" (936) — NOT a dict, NO detail_type. Tests assert `result == "created"` etc. (test_trace_enrichment.py:3994-4077). A decorator that "emits the standard degraded dict (merging null_fields)" is type-incompatible with it. Also its log hardcodes node_type="row_lineage" which collides with its real `node_type` parameter, so the @_enricher(detail_type, ...) model does not fit. detect_row_lineage_type must be EXCLUDED; the decorator applies to 4, not 5.
2) SIGNATURE INSUFFICIENT FOR BYTE-IDENTICAL ERROR STRINGS. The proposed signature is @_enricher(detail_type, **null_fields). The error-message prefixes are human-phrased and do NOT equal detail_type: "model score" vs detail_type "model_score"; "scenario expansion" vs "scenario_expander"; "live switch" vs "live_switch". Likewise the log's node_type literal equals detail_type for these four, but the error prefix cannot be derived from detail_type. So a decorator taking only (detail_type, **null_fields) CANNOT reproduce the exact f"... enrichment failed: {exc}" strings — it needs an extra parameter (e.g. error_label). As literally specified it would change the failure `error` text -> not behaviour-preserving.

OTHER NOTES: enrich_rating_step (185, in the module docstring's enricher list) and enrich_optimiser_apply (841) have NO scaffold (they rely on the outer catch in enrich_steps at 1755-1768 / delegate), so the "identical scaffold across the family" framing is already loose; the real scaffold-bearing dict enrichers number 4. Success outputs of all four are untouched by the change (decorator only wraps the except path), so success behaviour is preserved. The proposal's stated benefit (stop degraded-dict drift) is real and these four are safe to dedup. Net: sound idea, but est_reduction is overstated and the contract is not byte-identical until (a) detect_row_lineage_type is dropped from scope and (b) the decorator gains an error-label parameter.
verdict.est_reduction: ~-24 LOC realistic (4 enrichers x ~10 boilerplate lines removed, minus ~16 lines for the decorator/error-label plumbing), NOT the claimed ~-40; detect_row_lineage_type cannot be folded in.
verdict.recommended_action: Accept a CORRECTED, narrower version: introduce @_enricher applied to exactly the 4 dict-returning enrichers (enrich_banding, enrich_model_score, enrich_scenario_expansion, enrich_live_switch). The decorator must take THREE inputs — detail_type, a human error_label (so the f"{label} enrichment failed: {exc}" string is byte-identical), and **null_fields — and must reproduce the existing log call exactly (event "enrichment_failed", node_type=detail_type, error=str(exc), error_type=type(exc).__name__, exc_info=True). EXCLUDE detect_row_lineage_type (string return type, no detail_type, log node_type literal != its param) — leave it as-is. item.title: enrich_steps `_col_in_code` regex matches comparison operators (`>=`,`<=`,`==`,`!=`), so a node that only COMPARES the traced column in a with_columns body is wrongly treated as the column's creating step
item.failure_scenario: For a node whose code is e.g. `df = df.with_columns(flag=pl.when(pl.col('premium') >= 100).then(1).otherwise(0))` and the user traces column `premium` (which this node does NOT create, only reads), `re.search(r'\bpremium\s*=', raw_code)` matches the `premium >` ... actually matches `premium ` followed by the `=` of `>=`/`==`. So `_col_in_code` becomes True and the block at 1493 runs `parse_expression(code, 'premium')` / `evaluate_expression(...)`, attributing an expression/calculation to a step that merely references the column. The waterfall/explanation can then show a bogus 'calculation' for premium at the wrong node, or a spurious parse error marker, instead of treating it as pass-through.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\projection-trace__NEWBUG-1.py
verdict.evidence: Repro exit 0, all assertions pass. Part A: the exact regex re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(column)}\s*=", raw_code) from _trace_enrichment.py:1492 run against all four operators for both reference shapes. Idiomatic pl.col('premium') matches NONE (>=:F, <=:F, ==:F, !=:F); bare premium matches ONLY == (>=:F, <=:F, ==:T, !=:F). The claim's core mechanism ("matches premium followed by the = of >=/<=/!=/==") is FALSE for >=,<=,!=: in premium >= 100 the \s* consumes the space and the next char is >/</!, not the = the regex requires; no match. Only == matches (char after whitespace IS =), and only for a non-idiomatic bare column name. Part B: even in that single matching case (bare premium == 100), driving the REAL parse_expression/evaluate_expression as enrich_steps does (code=_wrap_node_code(raw_code), column='premium') yields parse_expression -> expression_type='opaque', expression_text='', referenced_columns=[] (no bogus calc, no error marker; parse_expression never raises), and evaluate_expression -> result_value=250.0 (the observed pass-through value of premium), expression_type='opaque'. Code-trace: _expression_parser.py:1126-1134 returns OPAQUE EMPTY when no with_columns alias equals the target (the node assigns 'flag', not 'premium'); :1304-1325 falls back to row_values.get(target). Reachability kill-shot: a bare premium inside with_columns raises NameError at Polars execution (verified live), so such a node cannot be successfully traced at all; any executable node references pl.col('premium'), which the regex never matches. NEWBUG-1 is NOT in catalog.md (the _trace_enrichment lines 143-148 are the unrelated Float32 rating-key mirror/twin finding). Neither claimed harm ('bogus calculation' nor 'spurious parse error') is producible.
verdict.recommended_action: Dismiss as not-a-bug. The cited regex does not match >=, <=, or != (the claim's mechanism is wrong: there is a >/</! character between the matched whitespace and the =). It matches only == with a non-idiomatic bare column name, which is unreachable (NameError in Polars, so no successful trace) and, even if forced, degrades safely: parse_expression returns an opaque empty expression for premium and evaluate_expression returns the genuine pass-through value, never a fabricated calculation or a parse-error marker. No code change warranted. Optional cosmetic hardening only: anchor the heuristic to an actual kwarg/alias assignment (with_columns keyword or .alias('premium')) so a bare col == can never set _col_in_code; not required since downstream parse/evaluate already handle the mis-fire and the shape is non-executable.

The architecture map and catalog (#19) confirm duplicate top-level function names produce distinct nodes that can share a name/label. When two steps share `node_name`, the loop patches the FIRST such step's `output_values[col_name]` using the known value derived for a different node, and breaks — silently overwriting a correct/other row value with a value belonging to a same-named sibling. item.what_it_does: Maps an exception raised while running an auto-range job to a job-store terminal transition + a re-raised HTTPException.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The two ~97-line except-ladders (BackgroundJobStopped / ExecutionCancelled / ExecutionMemoryLimitExceeded / HTTPException / BoundedMemoryUnsupported / ValueError / Exception) are byte-for-byte identical except for THREE strings: the log-event names ('frontier_auto_range_*' vs 'frontier_auto_range_streaming_*') and the human prefix in the final 500 branch ('Frontier auto range failed' vs 'Streaming frontier auto range failed'). Verified by normalised diff: only 3 differing lines out of 97. This is the god-file's flagship duplication and the '4 duplicated failure-mapping ladders' the architecture map calls out.
item.current_metrics: ~97 lines x2 (194 LOC); each ladder contributes ~12 to the host function cx
item.proposal: Extract one private helper `_finish_auto_range_job_failure(self, exc, *, job_id, execution_context, label: str, human_label: str) -> NoReturn` that wraps lines 3562-3658 verbatim, with `label` feeding logger.warning/error event names and `human_label` feeding the final message string. Replace each call site with `try: ... except BackgroundJobStoppedError: raise / except Exception as exc: self._finish_auto_range_job_failure(exc, job_id=job_id, execution_context=execution_context, label=..., human_label=...)`. The helper itself keeps the per-exception-type branching once.
item.behavior_preservation: Identical: the helper re-classifies by `type(exc)` exactly as today (memory-limit detection via _is_memory_limit_http_exception, contract_error for 400/422, etc.) and re-raises the same HTTPException with the same status/detail. The only variation (event names, human prefix) is passed as parameters, so log lines and messages are byte-identical per caller. No control-flow merges across the two paths.
item.est_reduction: ~-90 LOC; removes ~12 cx from each host function

verdict.evidence:
Re-read both ladders in full and ran a normalised `diff` of lines 3562-3658 vs 3853-3949: both are exactly 97 lines and identical except for 4 physical lines / 3 semantic differences — (a) logger.warning event `frontier_auto_range_bounded_streaming_unsupported` vs `frontier_auto_range_streaming_bounded_streaming_unsupported`; (b) logger.error event `frontier_auto_range_failed` vs `frontier_auto_range_streaming_failed`; (c) catch-all job message `f"Frontier auto range failed: {exc}"` vs `f"Streaming frontier auto range failed: {exc}"`. The JSON undercounts as "3 differing lines" (4 physical lines differ) but its `label`/`human_label` parameterisation with the `*` wildcard does cover all 4. Note the two 500-branch HTTPException `detail` strings are IDENTICAL ("Frontier auto range failed. Check the server logs for details.") in both ladders, so `human_label` only feeds the job `message`, not the 500 detail — the implementer must NOT parameterise the detail or they would alter it.

COMPLEXITY = INCIDENTAL/removable: the per-type branching (BackgroundJobStoppedError re-raise; ExecutionCancelledError→BackgroundJobStoppedError via cancellation_reason; ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError→_memory_limit_http_exception+memory_limited transition+raise from None; HTTPException with _is_memory_limit_http_exception sub-branch then contract_error-for-400/422-else-error; BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError→422; ValueError→400; catch-all→500) is byte-identical classification logic, correctly belonging in one helper.

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVATION trace: (1) `execution_context` is GUARANTEED non-None at both ladders — set before each `try` at lines 3445-3450 (non-streaming) and 3673-3683 (streaming) — so a helper param typed `ExecutionContext` preserves the unguarded `.metrics_payload()`/`_memory_limit_job_update(execution_context=...)` calls. (2) `_job_elapsed_seconds(self._store.jobs[job_id])`, `_lifecycle.transition`, `_auto_range_jobs.cancellation_reason(job_id)` all reference only `self` + `job_id`, both passed. (3) The helper must re-dispatch via `isinstance(exc, ...)` chains in the SAME order as the `except` clauses (memory-limit, HTTPException-with-memory-subcheck, BoundedMemoryUnsupported, ValueError, catch-all); Python except-ordering ↔ isinstance-ordering is semantically equivalent here since none of the listed types subclass each other except the deliberate HTTPException/memory-limit sub-branch which is preserved. (4) `raise <classified> from exc` reproduces the same status/detail/chaining.

CAVEAT (fix-up, not a redesign): the ladders reference `body.node_id` in TWO branches (BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError logger.warning and the catch-all logger.error). The proposed signature `(self, exc, *, job_id, execution_context, label, human_label)` OMITS `body`/`node_id`; a verbatim extraction would fail to compile or silently drop `node_id` from those two log events, contradicting the "log lines byte-identical per caller" guarantee. The implementer MUST also thread `node_id=body.node_id` (or pass `body`). This is a trivial signature-completeness correction that does not affect soundness of the dedup.
verdict.est_reduction: ~-90 LOC (collapses 194 LOC of two 97-line ladders into ~one 97-line helper + two ~3-line call sites); removes ~12 cyclomatic complexity from each of the two host functions.

verdict.recommended_action: Proceed with the extraction, with two mandatory corrections to the proposal as written: (1) add `node_id=body.node_id` (or pass `body`) to the helper signature — the ladder references `body.node_id` in the BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError and catch-all branches, and the stated signature drops it; (2) keep the 500-branch HTTPException `detail` string hard-coded/identical (do NOT drive it from `human_label`) since both ladders already share the same detail and only the job `message` differs. Re-dispatch inside the helper via isinstance chains in the same order as the current except clauses, return type `NoReturn`. After extraction, run the optimiser-service/frontier auto-range tests to confirm log-event names, job terminal states (memory_limited/contract_error/error), and re-raised HTTP status codes (400/422/500) are unchanged for both the streaming and non-streaming paths; add a test asserting the two distinct logger event names if not already covered.

item.what_it_does: Starts a daemon worker thread and, if thread.start() raises, transitions the job to error, releases the job-set + singleflight registrations, optionally cleans an orphan ratebook handle, and raises a 500.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. Three copies of the same `thread = threading.Thread(target=_X, daemon=True); try: thread.start() except Exception as exc: logger.error(...); self._lifecycle.transition(error); <release N registrations>; [ratebook cleanup]; raise HTTPException(500)` pattern. They differ only in: the worker callable, which job-set is released (_solve_jobs vs _auto_range_jobs), whether a ratebook handle cleanup runs, and the log/message text. The release+cleanup sequence is the part most prone to drift between the three.
item.current_metrics: ~24 + ~30 + ~37 = ~91 LOC across three blocks; the start-failure path is duplicated 3x
item.proposal: Extract `_spawn_worker_or_fail(self, worker: Callable[[], None], *, job_id, job_set, setup_singleflight_key, event: str, human_label: str, on_start_failure_cleanup: Callable[[], None] | None = None) -> None` that builds the thread, starts it, and on failure runs the shared transition+release sequence (releasing the passed `job_set`, _graph_node_setup_jobs and the singleflight) then raises the standard 500. Callers pass a small lambda for the ratebook-handle cleanup. The thread-body closures stay where they are.
item.behavior_preservation: Same releases in the same order on the same failure condition; the ratebook-cleanup callback is only supplied by the two ratebook-capable callers, preserving the `mode == 'ratebook' and handle.kind == _RATEBOOK_FACTORS_HANDLE_KIND` guard. Success path is untouched (thread already running owns its own finally/release).
item.est_reduction: ~-55 LOC; removes one full failure-branch from each of the 3 launchers

verdict.evidence:
Re-read all three start-failure blocks in full (2640-2663, 4050-4079, 5009-5045) plus their enclosing launchers, the worker-body finallys, SingleFlightRegistry.release (_background_jobs.py:165) and ExecutionContext.release_admission (_execution_context.py:687). The underlying complexity is INCIDENTAL (a shared helper is feasible), but the proposal AS SPECIFIED is NOT behaviour-preserving because its difference-enumeration is incomplete and its signature omits real divergent axes. Confirmed differences across the three failure paths:

(A) execution_context.release_admission() — THE decisive gap. Block1: none (the context is created INSIDE the worker callee _run_solve_setup_and_launch:2693, not in launcher scope, so nothing to release). Block2 (4054-4056): releases admission via `execution_context = prepared.get("execution_context"); if isinstance(...): release_admission()` placed BEFORE logger.error. Block3 (5012-5045): execution_context is in scope (ctx.execution_context) yet the start-failure path deliberately does NOT release it (only the worker-body finally at 4983 does). So the axis is none / release-before-log / none — three behaviours. The proposal never parameterises this; its only hook is on_start_failure_cleanup which it explicitly reserves for the ratebook lambda, and its described flow runs the callback AFTER the transition+release sequence. A faithful helper therefore needs an extra pre-log callback with ordering control; a naive one would drop Block2's release (leaks a memory admission reservation) or add a release to Blocks 1/3 (behaviour change / Block1 has no context object). The proposal's claim "Same releases in the same order" is false on this axis.

(B) elapsed_seconds differs and is NOT equivalent: Block1 = _job_elapsed_seconds(self._store.require_job(job_id)) (reads start_time from store, floors at 0, fallback) where `start_time` is not even a local; Blocks2/3 = time.monotonic() - start_time (local). Feeds the error-transition elapsed_seconds surfaced to clients/metrics. Not in the proposed signature.

(C) log node_id source differs: Block1/2 use body.node_id; Block3 uses node_id (=ctx.node_id). Not in signature. Block1 also adds a `job_id=job_id` structured-log kwarg that 2/3 omit.

(D) singleflight guard differs: Block1 releases unconditionally (no `is not None`); Blocks2/3 guard `if setup_singleflight_key is not None`. This one is BENIGN — release(key,*,job_id) does `_active_by_key.get(key)` so a None key no-ops — so a unified always-call-with-maybe-None is safe. The proposal does not call this out but it doesn't break.

The proposal's stated enumeration ("differ only in: worker callable, which job-set, whether ratebook cleanup runs, log/message text") omits (A), (B), (C) and (D). (A)/(B) are load-bearing (memory-admission leak / observable elapsed value); (C) is observability. A correct helper is writable but needs ~3 more params/lambdas than proposed (pre-log admission callback w/ ordering, elapsed strategy, node_id, optional log kwarg), which erodes the readability/-55 LOC win.
