item.what_it_does: Calls a memoised loader and emits a hit/miss log line by diffing lru_cache_info() before vs after the call.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. Both functions repeat the identical pattern: `info_before = loader.cache_info(); result = loader(...); info_after = loader.cache_info(); if info_after.misses > info_before.misses: log miss else log hit; return copy.deepcopy(result)`. The before/after cache_info diff to detect a hit is a hand-rolled idiom duplicated across the two loaders (and is itself fragile under concurrent calls).
item.current_metrics: ~10 LOC of cache-diff boilerplate x2
item.proposal: Extract `_load_cached_with_logging(cached_fn, args, *, on_miss, on_hit) -> dict` (or a small decorator) that performs the cache_info diff and deepcopy once. Each public loader becomes a 2-3 line call. Alternatively drop the hit/miss log distinction entirely (it is debug/info only) and just `return copy.deepcopy(cached_fn(...))`, removing the diff machinery.
item.behavior_preservation: Returns the same deep-copied artifact; the same log events fire on the same miss/hit outcome for single-threaded call sequences (the only sequencing the current code already assumes). Cache semantics (key = path+digest / resolved triple) are untouched.
item.est_reduction: ~-12 LOC

verdict.evidence:
The proposal's core premise — that the two loaders "repeat the IDENTICAL pattern: if info_after.misses > info_before.misses: log miss else log hit" — is FACTUALLY WRONG for the MLflow loader. Code-trace of src/haute/_optimiser_io.py:

(A) load_optimiser_artifact (51-74): digest=content_hash(Path(path)) [raises FileNotFoundError BEFORE any cache touch; side-effect file read]; diffs MISSES (info_after.misses>info_before.misses); has an explicit if/else: miss -> logger.INFO "optimiser_artifact_loaded" path+mode; hit -> logger.DEBUG "optimiser_artifact_cache_hit". The cached body (_load_artifact_cached, 32-48) emits NO log. Then return copy.deepcopy.

(B) load_mlflow_optimiser_artifact (118-157): resolve_mlflow_source(...) [raises ValueError on bad source_type/missing run_id/registered_model; side-effects]; diffs HITS (info_after.hits>info_before.hits), NOT misses; has NO else branch — it logs ONLY a hit (logger.DEBUG "mlflow_optimiser_cache_hit"). The miss/info log "mlflow_optimiser_artifact_loaded" lives INSIDE the cached body (_load_mlflow_cached, 109-114), where it fires only on an actual download and has access to the parsed mode. Then return copy.deepcopy.

So the two functions differ in: counter diffed (misses vs hits), presence of an else (A yes / B no), and WHERE the miss-log lives (A: wrapper / B: inside the memoised body). A single helper _load_cached_with_logging(cached_fn, args, *, on_miss, on_hit) that diffs one counter and calls on_miss/on_hit cannot reproduce B without either (i) moving B's miss-log out of the cached body into the wrapper (a real call-site/behaviour change — currently it is emitted from within the memoised function, only on download), or (ii) making the helper configurable enough (which counter; optional no-op on_miss) that the dedup payoff largely evaporates. Hence "each loader becomes a 2-3 line call" is NOT cleanly achievable; B's miss-log is body-resident.

The alternative variant ("drop the hit/miss log distinction entirely and just return copy.deepcopy(cached_fn(...))") is NOT behaviour-preserving: it deletes four log events (optimiser_artifact_loaded info, optimiser_artifact_cache_hit debug, mlflow_optimiser_artifact_loaded info, mlflow_optimiser_cache_hit debug). This directly CONTRADICTS the proposal's own behavior_preservation claim ("the same log events fire on the same miss/hit outcome"). The most operationally useful line — mlflow_optimiser_artifact_loaded, which records run_id+mode at the moment of a real MLflow download — would be silently removed.

No test guards any of this. Grep over tests/: the four log event names appear ONLY in src/_optimiser_io.py; no caplog/structlog capture in test_optimiser_io.py. The enforced contract (test_optimiser_io.py, test_lru_cache_contracts.py TestLoadOptimiserArtifactMemoisationContract / TestLoadMlflowOptimiserArtifactMemoisationContract) pins ONLY: return values, deep-copy isolation (mutating result must not corrupt cache), cache currsize (1 for repeat, 2 for distinct keys), and download/open call counts. So dropping the logs would PASS CI silently — exactly the "incorrect change that's hard to notice" CLAUDE.md warns against. The deepcopy and content-hash-key semantics ARE behaviour-preserved by both variants (untouched), but the logging is not.

Legitimate kernel: the cache_info before/after diff is a genuine hand-rolled, concurrency-fragile hit/miss detector (incidental complexity), and A's local if/else could be tidied. But the "two identical patterns -> one helper" dedup framing rests on a misread, and the LOC-winning variant changes observable behaviour with zero test coverage.
verdict.est_reduction: Claimed ~-12 LOC. Realistic: ~-3 to -5 LOC if done faithfully (A-only tidy, or a per-function helper preserving B's body-resident miss-log and hits-diff). The ~-12 figure is only reachable via the log-deleting variant, which is not behaviour-preserving.
verdict.repro_path: Read src/haute/_optimiser_io.py:51-74 (function A, misses-diff + if/else, body emits no log) vs 84-115 + 118-157 (function B, hits-diff, no else, miss-log at 109-114 INSIDE the cached body). Grep tests/ for the four log event names -> matches only in src. No caplog/structlog capture in test_optimiser_io.py. Contracts in tests/test_lru_cache_contracts.py:740-915 assert return-equality, deepcopy isolation, currsize, and download/open counts only — never the log events.
verdict.recommended_action: Do NOT adopt as a symmetric "dedup of two identical patterns" — the premise is wrong (B diffs hits not misses, has no else, and emits its miss-log from inside the cached body). Reject the log-dropping variant outright: it deletes info/debug observability (incl. the MLflow download provenance line) with no test catching it, contradicting the proposal's own behaviour-preservation claim. If a cleanup is still wanted: (1) FIRST add structlog/caplog tests pinning all four events on the correct miss/hit outcome for both loaders; (2) THEN, if desired, refactor — but keep B's miss-log inside _load_mlflow_cached and keep B's hits-diff for the wrapper hit-log, or unify only A's local if/else. Treat as a low-value, behaviour-sensitive tidy, not a free dedup; not worth the churn unless the logging tests are added first.

item.what_it_does: Validates a job's stored frontier/constraint metadata and raises HTTPException(500) with a fixed message when it is missing or malformed.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The literal `raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Job frontier constraint names are invalid")` appears 4x and `"...constraints are invalid"` 2x, each guarding a near-identical isinstance/membership check. The repeated string + status is copy-paste validation scaffolding.
item.current_metrics: ~6 duplicated 500-raise guards; route file 1802 LOC
item.proposal: Introduce a small `_require(value, predicate, detail, status=500)` (or per-field `_require_frontier_constraint_names(job) -> list[str]`) helper that raises the standard HTTPException when the predicate fails, and reuse the existing _INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL constant pattern for the message. Collapses each guard to one line and removes the duplicated literals.
item.behavior_preservation: Same status code and detail string raised under the same condition; purely textual consolidation with no change to which inputs pass/fail.
item.est_reduction: ~-15 LOC

verdict.est_reduction: ~-4 to -6 LOC realistically (not the claimed -15); the in-loop guards at 544-546 / 611-613 cannot collapse to one line.
verdict.repro_path: N/A (read-only audit). Behaviour locked by tests in C:\Users\prici\haute\tests\test_optimiser_routes.py: test_frontier_point_constraints_override_invalid_constraint_names_list (~13786), ..._non_string_in_names (~13802), ..._invalid_config (~13522), ..._invalid_name (~13537). Run: python -m pytest tests/test_optimiser_routes.py -k frontier_point_constraints_override
verdict.evidence:
Re-read the cited code in full. Two functions are involved: _frontier_point_result_dict (optimiser.py:535-589) and _frontier_point_constraints_override (592-631). The six guards are real copy-paste: lines 539/545/609/613 raise HTTPException(500, "Job frontier constraint names are invalid"); lines 599/604 raise HTTPException(500, "Job optimiser constraints are invalid"). De-duplicating these two literal strings is a legitimate (small) DRY win, so the underlying idea is not unsound. BUT the proposal as written has three defects that make it not a clean "sound":

(1) MIS-CITED LINES. The proposal lists "1312/1319" as part of the same frontier/constraint dedup. Lines 1312/1319 are in a DIFFERENT function (apply path) and raise DIFFERENT messages: "Job summary is missing" (1312) and "Job summary is incomplete" (1319). They are not duplicates of the frontier-constraint literals; folding them into _require_frontier_constraint_names would be wrong. The citation is incorrect.

(2) "Reuse the _INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL constant pattern for the message" is behaviour-changing if taken literally. _INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL (=_helpers.py:180 "Operation failed. Check the server logs for details.") is GENERIC. The six guards raise SPECIFIC details. Tests assert "constraint names" in exc.value.detail.lower() (test_..._invalid_constraint_names_list, ..._non_string_in_names) — substituting the generic value breaks them and changes the API contract. Only "use a named constant" (carrying the same text) is safe; "reuse _INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL" (its value) is not. Verified no test does an == on the full string (grep of test file), so a constant with identical text passes; the generic value does not.

(3) LOGGING SIDE-EFFECT mismatch. The proposal points at the existing helper pattern, but every raise_* helper in _helpers.py (raise_node_not_found 187, raise_validation_error 208, etc.) calls logger.warning(...) BEFORE raising. The six inline raises here do NOT log. A _require helper modelled on that family would add a structured-log emission per failure — an observable behaviour change, contradicting the "purely textual / no behaviour change" claim. A faithful helper must be non-logging.

Case-trace of behaviour that must be preserved: all six raises keep status 500; in _frontier_point_result_dict, 538-539 (constraint_names not a list) fires BEFORE the loop, 544-545 fires on the FIRST non-str name inside the loop (short-circuit, before constraints[name] is set); converged check (548-549) stays 400. In _frontier_point_constraints_override, ordering is config-constraints validation (598-604) -> constraint_names list check (608-609) -> per-name loop with non-str check (612-613), missing-spec 500 (616), threshold-count 500 (621), missing threshold_field 500 (627). A generic _require(value,predicate,detail) placed inline preserves ordering; but the proposed per-field variant _require_frontier_constraint_names(job)->list[str] cannot cleanly own the interleaved per-element non-str check without either eagerly validating up front (changing which exception fires first when multiple fields are bad) or leaving the in-loop check in place (then it only covers 2 of 6 sites). Hence the -15 LOC / "each guard to one line" estimate is optimistic; realistic saving is ~4-6 LOC.

Net: incidental (removable) complexity, but the proposal is imprecise and partly behaviour-changing as specified (wrong line cites; _INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL value would fail tests; logging-helper pattern adds a side effect). Sound ONLY if narrowed to: introduce two non-logging module constants (or one non-logging _require) carrying the EXACT current detail strings, leave 1312/1319 untouched, and do not log. That qualifies as marginal, not sound.
verdict.recommended_action: Accept a NARROWED version only. Implement as two module-level constants (e.g. _FRONTIER_CONSTRAINT_NAMES_INVALID = "Job frontier constraint names are invalid", _OPTIMISER_CONSTRAINTS_INVALID = "Job optimiser constraints are invalid") referenced at 539/545/609/613 and 599/604, OR a tiny NON-LOGGING helper _require(value, predicate, detail, status=500). Do NOT touch lines 1312/1319 (unrelated "Job summary" messages). Do NOT substitute the generic _INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL value and do NOT model the helper on the logging raise_* family. Keep raise ordering and the in-loop short-circuit identical. Re-run tests/test_optimiser_routes.py -k "frontier_point" to confirm the substring assertions still pass. Expected ~4-6 LOC, low risk.

item.what_it_does: Turns a BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError into a 422 with a '<stage> cannot run in bounded streaming mode: {exc}' detail, a warning log, and a job/setup failure record.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. Five separate handlers (_run_solve_setup_and_launch, _run_frontier_auto_range_job, _run_streaming_frontier_auto_range_job, _execute_pipeline, _build_grid) each repeat the same warning + 422 detail + record-failure shape, differing only in the stage noun ('Optimiser setup' / 'Frontier auto range' / 'Pipeline' / 'Grid construction') and the log-event name.
item.current_metrics: ~12 LOC x5 = ~60 LOC
item.proposal: Extract `_record_bounded_streaming_unsupported(self, exc, *, job_id, execution_context, stage_noun, event) -> HTTPException` returning the 422 to raise (or raising directly). Each handler becomes `except BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError as exc: raise self._record_bounded_streaming_unsupported(...)`. For the orchestrator copies this can fold into SIMP-1's helper.
item.behavior_preservation: Same 422 status, same detail format, same warning event payload (node_id, error, job_id), same record-failure call. Only the stage noun and event name vary and are passed in.
item.est_reduction: ~-40 LOC

verdict.evidence:
The proposal's premise — that the five BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError handlers "differ only in the stage noun and the log-event name" — is false. Code-tracing all five sites in src/haute/routes/_optimiser_service.py shows they diverge on FIVE behavioural axes, and the proposed single helper `_record_bounded_streaming_unsupported(self, exc, *, job_id, execution_context, stage_noun, event) -> HTTPException` (raised by the caller) would CHANGE behaviour at multiple sites:

(A) RAISE vs NO-RAISE. Site (1) `_run_solve_setup_and_launch` @2838-2863 is a TERMINAL handler that records `contract_error` and does NOT re-raise (control falls to the `finally` at 2887 and the method returns). Sites (2) @3624, (3) @3915, (4) @4323, (5) @4785 all `raise HTTPException(422) from exc`. The proposed form `except ...: raise self._record_bounded_streaming_unsupported(...)` injects a `raise` into site (1), which would start propagating a 422 out of the launch path it currently swallows. That is a behaviour change / bug, not a dedup.

(B) WARNING PAYLOAD DIFFERS. Sites (1)@2843, (2)@3610, (3)@3901 log `node_id, error, job_id`. Sites (4)@4315 and (5)@4777 log only `node_id, error` — NO job_id. A unified helper taking `job_id` would add a job_id field to the Pipeline and Grid warnings that is currently absent. The proposal's promise of "same warning payload (node_id, error, job_id)" is only true for 3 of 5 sites.

(C) node_id SOURCE DIFFERS and is OMITTED from the proposed signature. Sites (1)-(4) use `body.node_id`; site (5) `_build_grid` @4777 uses bare `node_id`. The proposed signature has no node_id parameter at all, so it cannot reproduce either value in the warning.

(D) THREE DISTINCT RECORD-FAILURE MECHANISMS, not one shape. (1) builds an inline `fields` dict guarding execution_metrics on `execution_context is not None`, then `transition(to="contract_error", message=detail, fields=...)`. (2)/(3) use `_http_error_job_update(...)` (defs @334) which calls `execution_context.metrics_payload(...)` UNCONDITIONALLY (would AttributeError if execution_context is None) and `transition` with NO message kwarg (message rides in the dict). (4)/(5) use `_record_http_setup_failure` (@3362) → `_record_setup_failure` (@3335) with `setdefault` execution_metrics. Collapsing these changes the execution_context-None contract.

(E) elapsed_seconds SOURCE DIFFERS. (1) = `time.monotonic() - start_time` (monotonic delta from local timer @2571). (2)/(3) = `_job_elapsed_seconds(self._store.jobs[job_id])` (@528, stored wall timing, 0.0 fallback). (4)/(5) pass no elapsed_seconds (None). Not interchangeable.

The duplication is also overstated: sites 4/5 ALREADY share `_record_http_setup_failure`, and sites 2/3 ALREADY share `_http_error_job_update`. The only genuinely repeated text per site is the ~2-3 lines `detail = f"<noun> cannot run in bounded streaming mode: {exc}"` + the `logger.warning(...)`. Real dedup potential is ~10-15 LOC, not 40, and even that cannot collapse into ONE unified helper as specified without breaking (A)-(C). Verdict: essential per-site differences + the proposed helper changes behaviour at sites (1),(4),(5) → unsound.
verdict.est_reduction: Claimed ~-40 LOC is inflated. A behaviour-preserving variant (a tiny helper that only formats the detail string + emits the warning, threading node_id, and leaving each site to do its own record-failure and raise/no-raise) saves at most ~10-15 LOC. The proposed single unified helper as specified saves ~40 only by changing behaviour, so its real safe reduction is ~0.
verdict.refined_severity: unsound-as-specified; at most a marginal ~10-15 LOC micro-dedup is salvageable
verdict.recommended_action: REJECT the proposal as written. The single `_record_bounded_streaming_unsupported(...)->HTTPException` helper would (a) inject a re-raise into site (1) `_run_solve_setup_and_launch` which must NOT raise, (b) add a `job_id` field to the Pipeline (4) and Grid (5) warning logs that is currently absent, and (c) cannot reproduce site (5)'s bare-`node_id` warning value because the signature omits node_id. The five sites also use three different record-failure mechanisms (inline fields+message / `_http_error_job_update` / `_record_http_setup_failure`) with different execution_context-None and elapsed_seconds semantics — these are essential differences. If any cleanup is wanted, limit it to a small `_bounded_streaming_detail(stage_noun, exc)` string formatter (and at most a thin warning emitter that takes node_id AND an explicit `include_job_id`/`job_id` so the 3-vs-2-field split is preserved), leaving raise/no-raise, the record-failure call, and elapsed_seconds at each call site unchanged. Do not fold into SIMP-1's helper without first reconciling the raise/no-raise and payload differences.
verdict.repro_path: Trace in src/haute/routes/_optimiser_service.py: handler (1) @2838-2863 (no raise; inline fields; time.monotonic()-start_time; logs job_id; body.node_id), (2) @3605-3624 (raises; _http_error_job_update; _job_elapsed_seconds; logs job_id; body.node_id), (3) @3896-3915 (same as 2; event name only differs), (4) @4310-4323 (raises; _record_http_setup_failure; NO job_id in warning; body.node_id), (5) @4772-4785 (raises; _record_http_setup_failure; NO job_id in warning; bare node_id). Helpers: _http_error_job_update @334 (unconditional metrics_payload), _record_http_setup_failure @3362, _record_setup_failure @3335, _job_elapsed_seconds @528, start_time @2571.

item.what_it_does: Coerces a stored start_time into a float (falling back to time.monotonic()) and computes elapsed seconds for status updates.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The 5-line `raw = job.get('start_time'); start_time = float(raw) if isinstance(raw, int|float) and not isinstance(raw, bool) else time.monotonic()` idiom is duplicated verbatim in at least two launchers, and `_job_elapsed_seconds(self._store.jobs[job_id])` is repeated ~20 times (the same expression flagged for the unlocked-.jobs hazard in catalog #32).
item.current_metrics: start_time coercion ~5 LOC x2; elapsed expression x~20
item.proposal: Add `_job_start_time(self, job_id, default=None) -> float` for the coercion, and a `_job_elapsed(self, job_id) -> float` thin wrapper that reads the job once and calls _job_elapsed_seconds. Replacing the raw subscript also gives a single chokepoint to later harden the catalog #32 unlocked-read (a behaviour-neutral structural win, not the fix itself).
item.behavior_preservation: Same float coercion rules (bool excluded, non-numeric -> monotonic now) and same elapsed value; reads the same job dict. No semantic change, just one definition.
item.est_reduction: ~-25 LOC

verdict.evidence:
Re-read all cited code in full. TWO halves with different verdicts.

(1) `_job_elapsed(self, job_id)` over the 21 `self._store.jobs[job_id]` sites — SOUND dedup. Grep confirms EXACTLY 21 occurrences of the verbatim 1-arg form `_job_elapsed_seconds(self._store.jobs[job_id])` (lines 3478,3496,3523,3556,3574,3586,3599,3619,3633,3651,3696,3740,3811,3821,3847,3865,3877,3890,3910,3924,3942); the two-arg-subscript grep found NONE, so all 21 rely on the module helper's `fallback=0.0` default. A thin wrapper `def _job_elapsed(self, job_id): return _job_elapsed_seconds(self._store.jobs[job_id])` is byte-for-byte behaviour-preserving: same unlocked `dict.__getitem__` (no lock, no `_evict_stale`, KeyError-on-missing), same module function (`_optimiser_service.py:528-534`), same default. The OTHER call-site flavours are correctly OUT of scope and must NOT be folded in: line 2655 uses `require_job(job_id)` (locked+evicted, raises HTTP404 not KeyError); 3100/3226/3257 pass an already-fetched local `job`; 2201/2255 are in MODULE functions (no `self`) using `store.jobs.get(job_id,{})`/`store.jobs.get(job_id,job_snapshot)` WITH a `fallback` arg; 3138 passes `job,elapsed_seconds`. `require_job`/`get_job` differ from the raw subscript in lock acquisition, stale-eviction, and missing-key behaviour (HTTPException/None vs KeyError) — confirmed at `_job_store.py:360-468,533-541` — so the wrapper is only neutral if it keeps the raw subscript.

(2) `_job_start_time(self, job_id, default=None)` over the 2 coercion sites (2683-2687, 4843-4847) — NOT cleanly behaviour-preserving AS SPECIFIED. The 5-line idiom is byte-identical at both, but the RAW source differs: site A (2682) reads from an already-fetched `job = require_job(job_id)` (present-guaranteed, just locked); site B (4841) reads from `existing_job = get_job(job_id) or {}` (missing job -> {} -> monotonic fallback). A helper that fetches internally by `job_id` must pick ONE accessor: `require_job` would turn site B's missing-job->monotonic into a 404 (behaviour CHANGE); `get_job() or {}` adds a redundant second locked fetch at site A. Truly neutral form is a module helper taking the dict (`_job_start_time(job, default)`) — not the `self,job_id` signature proposed. Saves only ~5 LOC.

CATALOG #32 tension (decisive for 'marginal'): repro `review/02-findings/repro/routes__optimiser-worker-raw-jobs-keyerror.py` PROVES the raw subscript is a live bug — under concurrent TTL eviction `store.jobs[job_id]` raises KeyError as an ARGUMENT before `lifecycle.transition` runs, masking the genuine exception in `except` branches and leaving the job stuck 'running' with no terminal_reason. The proposal is explicitly behaviour-PRESERVING ('reads the same job dict... not the fix itself'), so it PERPETUATES this bug, now hidden behind the innocuous-looking `self._job_elapsed(job_id)` — a readability MINUS (the unlocked-read hazard becomes invisible to future readers) that partly offsets the dedup win. Acceptable as pure structural prep ONLY if #32's real fix (switch the chokepoint to `get_job(...,{})`) lands separately under its own dev/reviewer+test pair.
verdict.est_reduction: ~-20 LOC realistic (21 elapsed sites collapse to one-liners: ~-18 to -20; start_time half nets only ~-3 to -5 and as-specified needs a signature change). Below the claimed -25 once the start_time wrinkle is handled.
verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\02-findings\repro\routes__optimiser-worker-raw-jobs-keyerror.py
verdict.recommended_action: Accept ONLY the `_job_elapsed(self, job_id)` half (21 verbatim sites -> sound, behaviour-preserving dedup; wrapper MUST keep `_job_elapsed_seconds(self._store.jobs[job_id])` to stay neutral). For the start_time half, either (a) drop it, or (b) implement it as a module helper taking the already-fetched dict (`_job_start_time(job, default)`) rather than the proposed `self,job_id` signature, to avoid the site-A re-fetch / site-B 404 divergence. STRONGLY recommend sequencing the catalog #32 fix (change the new chokepoint to `self._store.jobs.get(job_id, {})`) immediately after, with the existing repro promoted to a failing pytest, so the dedup is not left as a tidier facade over a proven KeyError-masking bug. Do NOT fold the require_job / local-job / fallback-bearing / module-function call sites into the wrapper — their accessor and argument semantics differ.

item.title: Rating table with empty (or unusable) entries is silently dropped — promised outputColumn never materialises, violating the fail-loud mandate
item.location: src/haute/_rating.py:517-518 (and 542, 568) `return lf` guards in _apply_rating_table, reached via _apply_rating_step_outputs:791-795 because output_col is still appended to out_cols
item.failure_scenario: A ratingStep table that passes config validation but produces no lookup rows is silently skipped, and the rate column it was supposed to add never appears. Verified reachable via the real config path: `normalise_rating_tables` (_rating_step_config._normalise_entry_rows:148-170) validates per-row value/factor presence but does NOT reject an empty `entries: []`. So a table {factors:['age'], entries:[], outputColumn:'age_factor'} survives normalisation, then `_apply_rating_table` hits `if not factors or not entries or not output_col: return lf` and returns the frame unchanged. `_apply_rating_step_outputs` still appends 'age_factor' to out_cols. Repro (run): `_apply_rating_step_outputs(lf, [{'factors':['age'],'entries':[],'outputColumn':'age_factor'}], []).collect()` materialises with NO error and NO age_factor column (shape unchanged). If this is the only table with no combinedOutputs, the entire rating step is a silent no-op and downstream pricing/scoring that reads age_factor sees it missing (or binds a stale upstream same-named column) — a silently wrong price. The sibling guards (entries lacking a 'value' key; a declared factor absent from every entry) are defended by normalise_rating_tables for the config path but remain live for any direct _apply_rating_table caller, e.g. trace enrichment. Contrast with the loud RatingTableMissError the same function raises for ordinary lookup misses — a config that yields zero usable entries should fail at least as loudly.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\optimiser__BUG-1.py
verdict.evidence: Executed repro EXIT=0, all checks OK, on real haute functions. PART A: normalise_rating_tables({tables:[{factors:['age'],entries:[],outputColumn:'age_factor'}]}) returns the table verbatim [{'factors': ['age'], 'entries': [], 'outputColumn': 'age_factor'}] -- NOT rejected (root cause _rating_step_config.py:270-274 `if entries == []: result['entries']=[]; return result` short-circuits _normalise_entry_rows). PART B (headline): _apply_rating_step_outputs(pl.DataFrame({'age':[25,40]}), [empty_table], []).collect() -> result columns ['age'], shape (2,1) UNCHANGED, NO error, age_factor absent (guard _rating.py:517-518 `if not factors or not entries or not output_col: return lf`). Stale-binding check: input with pre-existing age_factor=[99.0,99.0] -> output age_factor still [99.0,99.0] (stale upstream value silently preserved -> silently wrong price). PART D: direct _apply_rating_table callers hit guards :542 (no 'value' key) and :568 (declared factor absent) -> age_factor silently dropped. PART E CONTRAST: an ordinary lookup miss in the SAME function raises RatingTableMissError loudly ('Rating table age_factor ... 2 of 2 row(s) had no match'), proving the inconsistency the bug asserts. Refinement: the combinedOutputs sub-path is NOT silent -- it raises ColumnNotFoundError on the phantom out_cols entry (out_cols still appended at _rating.py:793-795); the genuinely silent path is the no-combinedOutputs case.
verdict.recommended_action: Fix (fail-loud): reject a rating table that yields zero usable lookup rows instead of returning lf silently. In _rating._apply_rating_table, when output_col is declared but factors/entries are empty (or entries lack 'value', or a declared factor is absent from every entry), raise a clear config error naming the outputColumn -- mirroring RatingTableMissError's loudness. Equivalently/additionally, tighten _rating_step_config._normalise_entries_for_table to reject `entries == []` for a table that declares factors+outputColumn (the early-return at lines 270-274 currently bypasses _normalise_entry_rows validation). Per repo TDD policy, first add a failing test: a ratingStep config with {factors:['age'],entries:[],outputColumn:'age_factor'} (and the no-'value' / missing-factor variants) must fail loudly rather than materialise without age_factor; include a regression test that a stale upstream same-named column is never silently passed through as the rate.
verdict.est_reduction: n/a (verifier: this is a new-bug confirmation, not a simplification/LOC-reduction item)

item.title: Streaming auto-range progress is pinned at 0.30 for the entire chunk phase; the in-loop refresh writes a constant and never advances toward the 0.85 'combining' milestone
item.failure_scenario: After emitting progress 0.30 at 3735, the per-chunk refresh inside the loop (`if chunk_index % 10 == 0: atomic_update({... 'progress': 0.30 ...})`) re-writes the same 0.30 value, so a long streaming auto-range over many chunks shows a frozen 30% bar until it jumps to 0.85 at 3816. item.title: _apply_rating_table deduplicates lookup rows on RAW factor values BEFORE canonicalisation, so the B14 'left join cannot fan out' invariant is enforced against pre-canonical keys
item.location: src/haute/_rating.py:572 (unique(subset=factors, keep='last')) executes before 583 (_rating_key_expr canonicalisation) and 602 (join on canonicalised columns)
item.failure_scenario: The comment at 571-572 asserts the dedup guarantees the left join cannot fan out rows, but the dedup runs on the lookup's raw factor column while the join key is the canonicalised (Utf8) form produced at 583. Today no live fan-out is reproducible: String factor columns canonicalise verbatim (so any post-canonical duplicate is already a pre-canonical duplicate and is deduped), and the Float int-like collapse (25.0->'25') maps only values that were already equal pre-canonical. I attempted several mixed-type entry constructions (str/int/float for one factor) and all collapsed to a single row — no fan-out observed. The defect is therefore latent: the ordering makes the no-fan-out guarantee depend on a property of _rating_key_expr (no two distinct pre-canonical values share a canonical key on the SAME dtype) that is true today but is neither asserted nor obvious, and would silently start duplicating rows (inflating the frame, multiplying premium) if the canonicaliser ever gained a many-to-one rule on a homogeneous column. Robust fix: dedup AFTER canonicalisation (move the unique() below 583), so the invariant the comment claims is actually the one enforced.

item.what_it_does: Locate the AST expression node whose alias == target_column among all with_columns/select calls (last match wins, plus no-alias auto-name fallback).
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The identical 'for wc_call,lineno in wc_calls: exprs=_extract_expressions_from_with_columns(...); for expr_node,alias,ln in exprs: if alias==target: best_match=...' loop is copy-pasted in 4 functions (verified: 4 call sites of _extract_expressions_from_with_columns, 6 wc_calls loops), and _parse_expression_impl bolts on 3 extra sequential fallback blocks (:1087-1124) that re-walk the same wc_calls re-implementing the alias/auto-name match a second and third time. _extract_expressions_from_with_columns already resolves Starred, list-variables and auto-names, so the three fallback blocks are largely redundant with it.
item.current_metrics: _parse_expression_impl len=163 cx=32 nest=8; the 4 duplicated loops total ~60 lines
item.proposal: Extract one helper `_find_target_expr(wc_calls, symbol_table, target_column) -> tuple[ast.AST, int|None] | None` that runs the canonical last-match-wins scan (including the no-alias auto-name pass) once, and call it from all four functions. Fold the three ad-hoc fallback blocks in _parse_expression_impl into that single helper so there is exactly one definition of 'how a target column is located'. kind=extract+dedup.
item.behavior_preservation: The helper reproduces the exact 'last match wins' precedence (overwrite best_match on every alias hit) and the same no-alias _infer_auto_name fallback order already used in _compute_result_impl; the deleted fallback blocks only matched aliases through list-variables, which _extract_expressions_from_with_columns already returns, so the resolved node set is identical across nulls/empties/missing-target (all paths still end at best_match is None -> opaque/observed-value).
item.est_reduction: ~70 LOC; _parse_expression_impl cx 32 -> ~14

verdict.evidence:
The proposal bundles a sound dedup with a NON behavior-preserving change. Traced all four sites + the helper.

SOUND parts: (1) The canonical last-match-wins loop `for wc_call,_ in wc_calls: exprs=_extract_expressions_from_with_columns(...); for en,al,ln in exprs: if al==target: best=...` is byte-identical in _parse_expression_impl (1081-1085), _evaluate_conditional_branches (1466-1470), _compute_result_impl (1562-1566); these 3 can share a helper. (2) Fallback block 1 (1091-1109, list-variable alias re-scan) is DEAD CODE: _extract_expressions_from_with_columns already resolves Name->ast.List via _strip_alias (helper lines 948-954), so block 1 never adds a match. Verified empirically: removing only block 1 across a case grid yields 0 divergences.

UNSOUND part (the headline 'fold the three fallback blocks into the helper'): Fallback block 2 (1111-1124, no-alias auto-name) is NOT redundant. It iterates `wc_call.args` DIRECTLY and calls _strip_alias(arg)/_infer_auto_name(expr_node) on the UNRESOLVED arg node. For a bare `ast.Name` single-expression variable, _strip_alias returns (Name,None) and _infer_auto_name(Name)=None -> no match -> opaque. The helper instead RESOLVES the Name to its expr (line 956) and returns (resolved_expr, None); a helper-driven no-alias pass then runs _infer_auto_name on the RESOLVED node and matches. So folding block 2 into the helper BROADENS matching. Confirmed 3 public-API regressions via parse_expression():
  - `expr = pl.col("x") + 1\ndf = df.with_columns(expr)` target "x": current=opaque/"" -> proposed=arithmetic "x + 1"
  - `e = pl.col("X")\ndf = df.with_columns(e)` target "X": current=opaque -> proposed=arithmetic
  - `e = pl.col("a") + pl.col("b")\ndf = df.with_columns(e)` target "a": current=opaque -> proposed=arithmetic
The proposal's stated behavior_preservation ("the resolved node set is identical across nulls/empties/missing-target") is therefore FALSE. The only relevant test, tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py:2386 test_variable_single_no_alias (`expr = pl.col("x") + 1; df.with_columns(expr)`), asserts only `expr is not None`, so it does NOT pin opaque and would NOT catch the flip — a silent observable change, exactly the class this audit guards against and the project's "no hidden behaviour change" rule forbids.

Additional: the 4th site _parse_expression_chain_impl (2186-2196) is NOT the same scan — it builds all_defs (not last-match-wins) and unconditionally applies _infer_auto_name to every None-alias expr (2189-2190). It cannot share the proposed `_find_target_expr` helper's return shape/semantics, so "call it from all four functions" is inaccurate.

Baseline: 698 parser tests pass (tests/test_expression_parser*.py).
verdict.est_reduction: Real, but smaller and narrower than claimed. Safe scope (extract canonical helper for the 3 identical sites + delete dead block 1) saves ~25-30 LOC and drops _parse_expression_impl cx modestly (not 32->14; block 2 and the cf/control-flow branches remain). The advertised ~70 LOC / cx 32->14 is only reachable by also folding block 2, which is the behaviour-changing part.
verdict.recommended_action: Reject as written (not behaviour-preserving). If still desired, REWRITE narrowly: (1) extract `_find_target_expr` doing ONLY the canonical last-match-wins scan and call it from _parse_expression_impl/_evaluate_conditional_branches/_compute_result_impl (NOT the chain impl); (2) delete dead fallback block 1 (1091-1109); (3) LEAVE block 2's direct-args _strip_alias/_infer_auto_name semantics exactly as-is (do not source its input from the helper). Before any merge, first land a characterization test pinning the current opaque output for `expr = pl.col("x") + 1; df.with_columns(expr)` (target "x"); if the team decides the broader resolution is actually desirable, that must be a separate, intentional behaviour-change PR with updated assertions, not folded into a "simplification".

item.what_it_does: Walk backwards up a pl.when().then()...otherwise() method chain collecting [{cond,then}...] + optional {otherwise}.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The two methods are the same algorithm duplicated across two classes: identical otherwise/then/alias/when handling, identical 'receiver must be a when() call' guard, identical 'stop at pl' termination, identical clauses.reverse(). They differ only in the trivial otherwise-default sentinel placement. Two copies must be kept in lockstep by hand.
item.current_metrics: _collect_when_clauses ~63L (within _call's cx85 cluster); _collect_eval_clauses ~40L
item.proposal: Hoist a single module-level free function `_collect_when_then_chain(node) -> list[dict]` returning the [{cond,then}...,{otherwise}] structure and call it from both classes. The converter and evaluator already consume the same dict shape, so only the per-clause text/value rendering needs to stay class-specific. kind=dedup.
item.behavior_preservation: Both current copies produce the same clause list for the same chain (same break conditions, same reverse, same otherwise handling); extracting the shared walk leaves the divergent rendering (convert vs evaluate) in place, so when/then/otherwise selection, nested-when detection and otherwise-None defaults are unchanged.
item.est_reduction: ~40 LOC removed

verdict.est_reduction: ~30 LOC net removed (eliminates a fully duplicated ~33L walk; new shared free function ~30L; also drops converter's redundant 628-631 rebuild loop). Proposal's "~40 LOC" is slightly optimistic but directionally right.
verdict.repro_path: .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest tests/test_expression_parser_chain.py tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py -k "when or clause or Chain or otherwise or nested" -q  => 126 passed
verdict.evidence: Re-read both methods in full: _ExprConverter._collect_when_clauses (src/haute/_expression_parser.py:572-635) and _ExprEvaluator._collect_eval_clauses (1938-1978). Normalized (whitespace/comment-stripped) textual diff of the two while-loop bodies shows them BYTE-IDENTICAL except for four behaviorally-inert differences, each traced: (1) assignment order `method=current.func.attr; func_attr=current.func` + redundant `assert isinstance(func_attr,ast.Attribute)` in converter vs `func_attr=current.func; method=func_attr.attr` in evaluator — same result; the loop guard at 581/1945 already proves current.func is ast.Attribute so the assert never fires and `.attr` is safe either order. (2) `then` no-preceding-when: converter `else: break`, evaluator bare `break` after the inner if — both reach break iff receiver isn't a when() call (the inner if always breaks/continues, so trailing break == converter's else). (3) `when` method: converter explicit `if method=="when": break`, evaluator omits and falls to final break — identical (both break). (4) otherwise sentinel `(ast.Constant(value=None))` vs `ast.Constant(value=None)` — parens cosmetic, identical. Both tails do clauses.reverse() then append {"otherwise":...} ONLY when the value `is not None`, producing the SAME list [{cond,then}...,{otherwise}]; converter's 628-631 element-by-element copy is a no-op rebuild. CRITICAL behavior-preservation checks: (a) Neither walk references `self` — they read only the `node` arg, local `current/clauses/otherwise_*`, and the `ast` module — so hoisting to a module-level `_collect_when_then_chain(node)` is clean and cannot drop side effects. (b) cond can be None (603/1963 `if when_call.args else None`); both consumers guard it identically and independently: converter `_format_when_clauses` :642 `self.convert(clause["cond"]) if clause["cond"] else "?"`, evaluator `_eval_clauses` :1983 `self.evaluate(clause["cond"]) if clause["cond"] else False`. The divergent per-clause RENDERING (convert vs evaluate, including _BranchTrackingEvaluator._eval_clauses override at 2075) correctly stays class-specific — only the shared walk is extracted. (c) `_collect_eval_clauses` is defined once on _ExprEvaluator (1938) and inherited by _BranchTrackingEvaluator (override at 2131 calls self._collect_eval_clauses) — refactor must keep a thin delegating method or have both sites call the free function; straightforward. Edge paths (alias-in-chain, then-without-when break, deeply-nested when, otherwise defaults) are covered by dedicated tests (test_expression_parser_coverage.py:2279,2416,2857) — 126 pass. Complexity is genuinely INCIDENTAL verbatim duplication, not essential.
verdict.recommended_action: Accept. Hoist module-level `_collect_when_then_chain(node: ast.AST) -> list[dict]` returning [{cond,then}...,{otherwise}] (otherwise appended only when `is not None`). Replace _ExprConverter._collect_when_clauses body and _ExprEvaluator._collect_eval_clauses body with a call to it; drop the converter's redundant 628-631 copy loop and dead `assert`. Keep a thin _collect_eval_clauses method (or call the free function directly from both _eval_when_from_then_or_otherwise overrides) so _BranchTrackingEvaluator inheritance is preserved. Leave _format_when_clauses / _eval_clauses (and the _BranchTrackingEvaluator override) untouched. Re-run the 126 when/clause tests as the gate.

That is provably wrong: a with-block body is INDENTATION-delimited, whereas _statement_end_index (src/haute/_code_extraction.py:471-478) advances by parenthesis depth only. A `with open('m.pkl','rb') as f:` header has balanced parens, so _statement_end_index returns the index of the NEXT line and never skips the indented body. The current in_with/base_indent machinery (lines 604-621) exists precisely for this and is ESSENTIAL, not incidental. Two concrete body shapes diverge under the proposed form: (1) legacy multi-statement with-body whose first body line is not `obj=...` (e.g. `model_bytes = f.read()`): current returns 'df = df.with_columns(pred=obj.predict())'; proposed leaks 'model_bytes = f.read()\n    obj = pickle.loads(model_bytes)\ndf = ...' into user code. (2) with-body containing a blank line then a 2nd indented stmt (`aux = obj.meta`): current skips both; proposed leaks 'aux = obj.meta' into user code. Both violate the function's own docstring contract ("with open(...) blocks ... still treated as load boilerplate wherever they appear (legacy multi-step loads)") and would corrupt the saved code box / re-emit a non-standalone file. The canonical single-statement pickle case (tests/test_parser_helpers.py:1902, tests/test_code_extraction_roundtrip.py:434) survives ONLY by coincidence because its body line starts with `obj = ` and gets rescued by the obj-arm — masking the bug in the existing suite. item.what_it_does: Render a literal AST Constant (or pl.lit(literal)) to display text and record numeric/value constants.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. _pl_lit duplicates the entire None/True/False/str/int-float/repr ladder of _constant, then adds a Name('None'/'True'/'False') variant. The same five-case formatting is written twice; _pl_lit additionally appends to self.constants for the cases _constant does too.
item.current_metrics: _pl_lit ~34L largely overlapping _constant ~14L
item.proposal: Have _pl_lit delegate: when the single arg is an ast.Constant, route it through a shared `_render_literal(value, record=True) -> str` helper that both _constant and _pl_lit call; keep _pl_lit's extra Name('None'/'True'/'False') and variable-fallthrough handling as a thin pre-step. kind=dedup.
item.behavior_preservation: The shared helper reproduces the exact case order (None/True/False before str before int/float before repr) and the same self.constants.append targets, so emitted text and recorded constants are identical for every literal kind; the Name-keyword and variable paths in _pl_lit are untouched.
item.est_reduction: ~18 LOC

verdict.evidence:
The proposal's core premise is factually wrong about the current code. It claims _pl_lit "additionally appends to self.constants for the cases _constant does too" and that a shared _render_literal(value, record=True) helper would reproduce "the same self.constants.append targets." It would not — the append targets DIFFER for 5 of 6 literal kinds.

Case-by-case trace of the ast.Constant arg:
- None: _constant (264-265) returns "None", NO append. _pl_lit (483-485) append(None) + return "None".
- True: _constant (266-267) NO append. _pl_lit (486-488) append(True).
- False: _constant (268-269) NO append. _pl_lit (489-491) append(False).
- str: _constant (270-271) NO append. _pl_lit (492-494) append(val).
- int/float: BOTH append (273 / 496). <- the ONLY agreeing case.
- repr-fallback (e.g. bytes): _constant (275) NO append. _pl_lit (498-499) append(val).

So _constant records ONLY numeric literals; _pl_lit records EVERY literal. A single `record` boolean cannot reconcile these:
- record=True called from _constant would start appending bare True/None/"s"/bytes that it currently never records, perturbing ParsedExpression.constants (e.g. invariants like `assert expr.constants == []` at tests/test_expression_parser.py:49 and every downstream consumer at _expression_parser.py:653,1153,1319,1405).
- record=False (i.e. _constant's logic) reused by _pl_lit would stop pl.lit(True/False/None/"hello"/b"data") from recording, directly FAILING the pinned tests test_pl_lit_true (tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py:509-512), test_pl_lit_false (514-517), test_pl_lit_none_constant (519-522), test_pl_lit_string (524-527), test_pl_lit_bytes_repr (534-538), and TestPlLitNameTrue (2346-2359).

Either setting of the single proposed `record=True` flag changes behavior for one caller — it is a behavior-changing bug, not a behavior-preserving dedup. The proposal does not specify the more granular signature (e.g. record_all vs record_scalars_only) that a correct merge would require; it explicitly says record=True. The complexity here is ESSENTIAL: the two functions implement genuinely different recording contracts ("numeric only" vs "all literals"), so the duplicated text encodes a real semantic difference. Only the int/float branch is safely shared (a ~1-line overlap), far short of the claimed ~18 LOC.
verdict.repro_path: Implement _render_literal(value, record=True) per the spec, route _constant and _pl_lit through it, then run: pytest tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py -k "PlLit" -q. With record=True the str/None/bool/bytes branches break the == [] invariant elsewhere; with _constant's numeric-only logic, test_pl_lit_true/false/none_constant/string/bytes_repr fail because the constants are no longer recorded.
verdict.est_reduction: ~1 LOC genuinely safe (shared int/float branch only); the claimed ~18 LOC is not achievable without changing side effects or introducing a two-mode flag the proposal does not specify

The two ladders are not side-effect-equivalent (_constant records numeric only; _pl_lit records all literals), and the proposed record=True helper would break pinned tests for one caller whichever way the flag is set. item.what_it_does: Recursively detect whether an AST subtree contains a pl.when()/.then()/.otherwise() chain (nested conditional).
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL (with a caveat). Two near-identical recursive detectors live in two classes; they differ ONLY in whether a bare `.when` attribute (receiver not pl) counts as nested. The duplication risks the two drifting; the difference is subtle and undocumented.
item.current_metrics: 2 x ~13L recursive functions
item.proposal: Promote to ONE module-level `_contains_nested_when(node, *, bare_when_counts: bool) -> bool` and have both callers pass the flag matching their current behavior; document why each needs its variant (or unify if a test proves they can agree). kind=dedup.
item.behavior_preservation: Parameterising the single differing predicate (bare `.when` membership) with a flag set per-call reproduces each caller's exact truth table; nested-when detection used for sub_expression extraction and branch tracking is therefore unchanged.
item.est_reduction: ~13 LOC; removes a silent-drift hazard

verdict.est_reduction: ~9-11 net LOC (proposal's ~13 is slightly optimistic; two methods of 13L+14L collapse to one ~16-18L module-level fn + 2 call-site edits). Real value is eliminating the silent-drift hazard, not LOC.
verdict.repro_path: .venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pytest tests/test_expression_parser.py tests/test_trace_hero_tdd.py tests/test_trace_calculation_hero.py tests/test_expression_parser_coverage.py -q (485+ green). Divergence + behavior-preservation demonstrated by AST comparison harness (see evidence).
verdict.evidence:
Complexity is INCIDENTAL, not essential: _has_nested_when (671-683, _ExprConverter) and _check_nested_when (2116-2129, _BranchTrackingEvaluator) are the same recursive algorithm differing in EXACTLY ONE predicate. Truth table per ast.Call node with func F:
(1) F is Attribute, attr in {then,otherwise}: both True.
(2) F is Attribute, attr==when, receiver is Name 'pl': both True (in _has_nested_when via either the dead is_pl_call line 674 OR the attr-in-{...,when} line 677; in _check_nested_when via lines 2122-2124).
(3) F is Attribute, attr==when, receiver NOT pl ("bare .when"): _has_nested_when -> True (line 677); _check_nested_when -> does NOT return, falls through to recurse on F.value (line 2125). THIS IS THE ONLY DIFFERENCE.
(4) F is Attribute, other attr: both recurse F.value.
(5) F not Attribute: both recurse node.args.
(6) node not Call: both False.

Verified by execution (AST harness on literal, col, full nested when/then/otherwise, multi-when chain, arith+when, expr.when(...), foo.bar.when(...), pl.col('a').when(...)): the two originals diverge ONLY on the three bare-.when samples (has=True, check=False); they AGREE everywhere else. The proposed unified _contains_nested_when(node, *, bare_when_counts): with bare_when_counts=True it equals _has_nested_when on every sample; with bare_when_counts=False it equals _check_nested_when on every sample. So the flag-parameterized module-level form is provably BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING for both call sites (line 645 -> bare_when_counts=True; line 2088 -> bare_when_counts=False). The is_pl_call(node,'when') at line 674 is provably DEAD (subsumed by the attr-in-{then,otherwise,when} test on line 677), so module-level promotion does not need self; _is_pl_call (also used at 349/353/357/366) stays as a method untouched. No instance state read by either function.

WHY MARGINAL (two caveats):
(a) The proposal offers an UNSOUND alternative: "unify if a test proves they can agree." The two detectors GENUINELY DISAGREE on bare-.when nodes (proven above). Collapsing to a single behavior would change one call site's truth table -> that path is a bug. Only the strict flag-preserving refactor is acceptable; the implementer must NOT actually unify the semantics.
(b) Reachability of the divergent case is unproven: in a valid polars chain, .when's receiver is always a .then(...) Call, so _check_nested_when would hit .then on recursion and agree anyway; the bare-.when-on-Name case appears unreachable from real expressions. This makes the practical bug-risk low, but precisely because reachability isn't proven the flag MUST faithfully reproduce the divergence rather than 'simplify it away'. Risk='medium' in the item is fair. Separately note both functions share an UNRELATED limitation (arith_with_when -> False for both, because the outer node is a BinOp, not a Call) — out of scope here, do not 'fix' it under this item.
verdict.recommended_action: ACCEPT as a strict flag-parameterized dedup; REJECT the "unify to one behavior" sub-option. Implement module-level `def _contains_nested_when(node: ast.AST, *, bare_when_counts: bool) -> bool` whose body mirrors _check_nested_when but adds `if bare_when_counts: return True` inside the attr=='when' non-pl branch BEFORE falling through to the recursive return. Replace line 645 with `_contains_nested_when(clause["then"], bare_when_counts=True)` and line 2088 with `_contains_nested_when(then_node, bare_when_counts=False)`. Drop the dead is_pl_call call at 674 (keep the _is_pl_call method). Add a docstring sentence documenting WHY each call site needs its flag value (converter counts bare `.when` as nested for sub-expression extraction; branch-tracker requires a pl receiver and otherwise recurses). TDD: before refactor, add a characterization test asserting the divergent truth values on `expr.when(...)` for both call paths so any future drift/over-unification is caught. Run the 4 test files above to confirm green.

item.title: _substitute_names_in_ast calls ast.copy_location with arguments reversed, so substituted nodes get no source position (and the original node is clobbered)
item.failure_scenario: ast.copy_location(new_node, old_node) copies position FROM the second arg INTO the first and returns the first. Every call here is written ast.copy_location(node, new_node) — i.e. it copies the freshly-built node's MISSING lineno/col_offset onto the ORIGINAL node and returns the original (with location), while the returned new substituted node (new_left/new_node_c/...) is never given a position. Verified: after the wrong-order call the new node has no lineno attribute. Today this is latent because the only consumers of the substituted AST (_ExprConverter/_ExprEvaluator) never read lineno, and ParsedExpression.source_line is taken from the original with_columns call node, not from substituted nodes. But it is an outright misuse of the API: any future feature that reports a source position from a reassignment-chain-substituted expression (e.g. better error locations in the trace, or ast.unparse round-tripping that relies on positions) will read a missing/garbage position, and the mutation of the original node's location is an unintended side effect on a shared AST.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\parser__NEWBUG-01.py
verdict.evidence: All 7 calls confirmed reversed at src/haute/_expression_parser.py:1220,1227,1251,1258,1270,1277,1284 -- written ast.copy_location(node, new_node); correct signature is copy_location(new_node, old_node) (verified via inspect.getsource: it copies position FROM the 2nd arg INTO the 1st and returns the 1st). Repro imports the REAL _substitute_names_in_ast and drives the BinOp path via a reassignment chain (expr = pl.col('base'); result = expr * pl.col('factor')). CONFIRMED claim (a): the returned/substituted BinOp has NO lineno/col_offset attrs (hasattr(result,'lineno')==False) and end_lineno/end_col_offset==None; compile(ast.Expression(body=result)) raises TypeError: required field "lineno" missing from expr -- so any future consumer that reads a source span from, compiles, or fix_missing_locations() the substituted AST will break. Side-effect on the shared original node is real but the bug text mis-describes WHICH attrs: in CPython 3.11 copy_location skips None-valued lineno/col_offset (so original.lineno stays 1, NOT clobbered), but the end_ branch copies even None, so original.end_lineno 1->None and end_col_offset 23->None ARE clobbered. Repro exits 0 (claim reproduced). Latent today (verified): only .lineno reads in the module are the _find_* extractors at lines 920-978 operating on the ORIGINAL tree; _ExprConverter (line 138)/_ExprEvaluator (line 1588) never read positions; ParsedExpression.source_line (line 42) is taken from the with_columns call node, not substituted nodes; no fix_missing_locations call exists. NOT in catalog: the 9 parser findings in review/02-findings/catalog.md (lines 83-525) contain no reference to copy_location / _substitute_names_in_ast / reassignment-chain positions -- this is new.
verdict.recommended_action: Fix all 7 calls to ast.copy_location(new_node, node) (swap args) so substituted nodes inherit the original position and the shared original node is not mutated. Per repo TDD policy, first add a failing unit test asserting a reassignment-chain-substituted node has a valid lineno (e.g. compile()/fix_missing_locations succeeds) and that the input node's end_lineno/end_col_offset are unchanged, then apply the swap. Severity low: no current behavioral impact (no consumer reads positions from substituted nodes), but it is an outright API misuse and a latent correctness/maintenance trap.
verdict.est_reduction: N/A (bug fix, not a simplification; ~7 one-line arg swaps)

item.title: _eval_clauses treats Polars 'and'/'&' incorrectly: BoolOp 'and' returns the last truthy operand's VALUE while a Compare returns bool, so a when-cond using `a & b` vs `a and b` can pick a different branch than Polars
item.location: src/haute/_expression_parser.py:1672-1686 (_boolop) reached from when-condition evaluation in _eval_clauses :1980-1988 / _BranchTrackingEvaluator._eval_clauses :2075-2114
item.failure_scenario: _ExprEvaluator._boolop implements Python `and`/`or` short-circuit semantics returning the last operand value (e.g. evaluates `pl.col('a') & pl.col('b')` only if parsed as BoolOp). But Polars conditions are written with bitwise & / | (BinOp BitAnd/BitOr), which _binop maps via operator.and_/operator.or_ — a BITWISE op on Python ints/bools, not logical. For boolean row values that coincide (0/1) the truthiness usually agrees, but for non-bool integer factor columns combined with & (a common Polars idiom for masks) `2 & 1 == 0` (falsey) whereas Polars boolean-context treats the predicate differently, so the branch-taken decision (taken_branch/dimmed_branches shown in the trace) can diverge from the executor. This is display-only (catalog #23/#29 note the evaluator is trace-only) but is a distinct divergence mechanism from the horizontal-func gaps already catalogued (#47): it is in branch SELECTION, affecting which when-clause the waterfall highlights, not just a leaf value.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\parser__NEWBUG-02.py
verdict.evidence: Executed repro (uv run python, polars 1.39.2, exit 0, all 7 assertions PASS) refutes the claimed REACHABLE branch-SELECTION divergence on all three scenarios the claim invokes. SCENARIO A (the EXACT claim: non-bool int columns a=2,b=1, `pl.col('a') & pl.col('b')` in when()): the Polars EXECUTOR RAISES `SchemaError: invalid series dtype: expected Boolean, got i64 ... .when([(col("a")) & (col("b"))])` -> there is NO executor branch to diverge from; the claim's premise "Polars boolean-context treats the predicate differently" is FALSE (Polars hard-rejects non-Boolean when() predicates rather than coercing). The LEAF bitwise value even AGREES: polars `2 & 1 == 0` == evaluator operator.and_(2,1) == 0. SCENARIO B (the `_boolop` mechanism the bug is named after, `a and b`): constructing `pl.col('a') and pl.col('b')` RAISES `TypeError: the truth value of an Expr is ambiguous` at construction (Expr.__bool__) -> no executable Polars source can contain it, so _boolop's last-operand-value path (confirmed real: `2 and 3` -> 3) is UNREACHABLE from any executor expression and cannot diverge against it. SCENARIO C (the actual legitimate idiom, Boolean columns `pl.col('fa') & pl.col('fb')` and `|`): evaluator bitwise operator.and_/or_ AGREES with Polars boolean &/| on the FULL truth table for branch selection (all 4 combos each, both & and |; True&False==False etc. coincide). Net: no expression that Polars will actually execute produces a different taken_branch in the trace evaluator than in the executor. CATALOG: mechanism absent from review/02-findings/catalog.md (8 high + 29 medium; parser entries #19-23; #23 is the unrelated catch-all-masking finding), but novelty is moot given refutation. The claim conflates the correct bitwise leaf value of `2 & 1` with a boolean-context reinterpretation Polars does not perform.
verdict.recommended_action: Do not add to catalog. REFUTED. The claimed distinct "branch-SELECTION divergence" is not real: Polars raises (SchemaError on non-bool i64 when-predicate; TypeError when constructing `a and b`) for both forms the claim relies on, so the trace can only ever render beside a pipeline that itself errored at execution -- there is no self-consistent waterfall highlighting a wrong branch. For the legitimate Boolean-column `&`/`|` idiom, the evaluator's bitwise ops already agree with Polars on branch selection. The only genuinely-real sub-fact (the _boolop returns-last-operand mechanism) is dead code w.r.t. this claim because it is unreachable from valid Polars, and any general "trace evaluator is more permissive than Polars / catch-all masks divergence" concern is already covered by catalog #23 -- no separate action.

item.title: _strip_docstring mis-detects the docstring terminator when a single-quoted (''') docstring body contains a literal triple-double-quote, or vice versa, silently swallowing real user code as 'docstring'
item.location: src/haute/_ast_helpers.py:203-231 (_strip_docstring), specifically the close test `if opening_quote in stripped` at :215
item.failure_scenario: _strip_docstring is a line/string heuristic (not AST-based, unlike the rest of _code_extraction which deliberately moved to AST for exactly this reason). On a multi-line docstring it records opening_quote (''' or """) and then closes on the first later line where `opening_quote in stripped`. If the docstring was opened with """ but a body line contains ''' (or any line merely CONTAINS the 3-char sequence, e.g. inside an expression or comment after the docstring), the terminator test can fire early or late. More concretely, because the close test uses substring containment on .strip(), a body line like `text = ''' inline'''` inside a """...""" docstring will not close it (good), but a user whose FIRST real statement after a single-line-looking docstring contains the opposite quote can be misclassified. Since extract_user_code runs _strip_docstring on every node body before boilerplate matching, a misdetected docstring boundary drops or keeps the wrong leading lines, corrupting the persisted code box on round-trip with no error. The AST path (_parse_user_code/ast.get_docstring) is available and would be exact.

verdict.evidence: Ran review/03-simplification/repro/parser__NEWBUG-03.py (uv run python, EXIT=1 = NO divergence). For 10 valid-Python function bodies, _strip_docstring output is IDENTICAL to the AST ground truth (ast.get_docstring + docstring node end_lineno) on every mechanism the claim names: e.g. mixed-quote-after ("""...""" doc then `marker = ''' literal '''`) -> both keep ["marker = ''' opposite-quote literal '''", 'return marker']; embedded-opposite ('''...''' doc whose body holds """ runs, then `"""userval"""`) -> both keep ['"""userval"""', 'return 0']; substring-after ("""...""" doc then `sep = '"""' + tail`) -> both keep the sep line. WHY: (1) close test at _ast_helpers.py:215 keys on the SAME opening_quote, so an opposite-quote run never closes it (claim concedes this); (2) a same-quote triple run can NEVER sit inside a docstring body of valid Python (it would terminate the literal), so early-close is impossible; (3) the real terminator line always contains opening_quote, so late-close is impossible; (4) once docstring_done=True (line 221 fast-path or 217), later statements are appended verbatim. UPSTREAM GUARANTEE: parser.py:144 does ast.parse(source) (raises on invalid Python) and _extract_function_bodies (_ast_helpers.py:251-276) slices bodies from validated AST nodes, so _strip_docstring only ever receives valid-Python text -- the one case I authored that broke (`sep = "row """ ...`) was invalid Python I mistakenly wrote, not a reachable vector. NOT A DUPLICATE: catalog.md _ast_helpers entries (lines ~222 func-name collision, ~231 async-def gap, ~516 _extract_preamble) do not cover _strip_docstring.
verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\parser__NEWBUG-03.py
verdict.recommended_action: Dismiss NEWBUG-03 as not-a-bug. The substring-containment close test cannot misfire on valid Python (the only input this function receives, guaranteed by ast.parse upstream at parser.py:144): an opposite-quote run never matches opening_quote, and a same-quote run cannot legally appear inside a same-quote docstring body. No code is swallowed and no round-trip corruption occurs; all 10 cases match ast.get_docstring exactly. Optional non-bug refactor to the AST path would be cosmetic only, not a correctness fix; weigh against the existing tested heuristic. Not present in catalog and should NOT be added as a real finding.
verdict.est_reduction: none

item.what_it_does: Each builder emits either a no-code template body or, when config['code'] is present, a hand-written function whose body is `<imports/load_expr>` + indented user code + `return df`.
item.current_metrics: ~6 builders x ~12-25 lines of duplicated assembly; _gen_model_score=64L, _gen_rating_step=55L, _gen_transform=48L, _gen_data_source=27L
item.proposal:
Extract one helper `_emit_function(decorator: str, func_name: str, description: str, params: str, *, body_lines: list[str]) -> str` that builds the `@dec
def f(params) -> pl.LazyFrame:
    """desc"""
<body>` envelope once. Then each builder computes only (decorator, pre_body_lines) and calls `_emit_function(..., body_lines=[*pre_body, *(_wrap_user_code(code,['df']) if code else [default_return])])`. The existing module-level template constants (_BANDING_*, _RATING_STEP, etc.) become the no-code default bodies fed to the same helper, collapsing the template-constant vs inline-f-string split flagged in the catalog.
item.behavior_preservation: The envelope text (decorator newline, def line, triple-quoted docstring, trailing newline) is produced verbatim today by every branch; centralising the exact same concatenation cannot change a byte. _wrap_user_code already owns the indent+`return df` logic, so reusing it is identical. The no-code templates already produce the same envelope via str.format, so routing them through the helper preserves output. ast.parse gate at emit time backstops any drift.
item.est_reduction: ~120-150 LOC removed; per-builder length roughly halved

verdict.evidence:
Re-read all six builders (src/haute/_codegen_builders.py:542-1038) plus helpers (_wrap_user_code:457, _wrap_external_code:444, _data_source_parts:308, _common_node_fields:185, _build_params:124, _first_source:203, _sanitize_description:131) and the template constants (_MODEL_SCORE:275, _RATING_STEP:360, _SCENARIO_EXPANDER:391, _EXPLORE:419, etc.).

COMPLEXITY = INCIDENTAL (removable). Every branch emits the identical envelope `@dec\ndef f(params) -> pl.LazyFrame:\n    \"\"\"{desc}\"\"\"\n<body>`. Only the decorator, the optional pre-body load lines, and the no-code default body differ per type. So a single `_emit_function(decorator, func, desc, params, body_lines=...)` is a legitimate dedup. `description` is the SAME `_sanitize_description` output fed to both the template (str.format kwarg) and the f-string, and `_wrap_user_code(code,['df'])` already owns indent+`return df` — reusing both preserves the docstring round-trip and the user-body shape.

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING semantically, but the proposal's headline claim ("centralising the exact same concatenation cannot change a byte") is PROVABLY FALSE for _gen_model_score. The no-code template renders the load call on ONE line — `_MODEL_SCORE` line 282: `df = score_from_config({first_param}, config={config_path_repr}, base_dir=base)` — while the code branch (lines 656-659) renders it across FOUR lines (open paren, args indented 8 spaces, `base_dir=base,`, close paren). These pre-body lines are NOT byte-identical across the two branches. To stay strictly byte-for-byte the helper must take a BRANCH-CONDITIONAL pre_body (one rendering when code is absent, another when present), which shrinks the model_score saving the proposal advertises. The same wrinkle (pre_body depends on whether `code` is truthy, not just on node type) applies to _gen_scenario_expander (393-395 vs 837-841), _gen_explore (419-423 vs 902-907) and _gen_transform (1024-1029 vs 1032-1037): the no-code bodies are `return {first}` with NO `df = {first}` seed, whereas the code bodies emit `df = {first}` then the wrapped user code. So `pre_body` is `(code present)`-dependent for 4 of the 6 builders, not purely type-level as the formula `body_lines=[*pre_body, *(wrap if code else [default])]` implies.

If an implementer instead used a SINGLE shared pre_body for model_score (collapsing the 4-line call to 1 line), it is still SEMANTICALLY safe: re-extraction `_match_model_score` (src/haute/_code_extraction.py:536-545) walks parentheses to find the closing `)` and explicitly handles single- OR multi-line `score_from_config(...)` (docstring line 532); `_match_rating_step` (553-564) does likewise; and the marker gate at line 891 (`"score_from_config(" in stripped`) fires for either form. The byte-identity safety net `tests/test_codegen_roundtrip_property.py` asserts only `codegen(parse(codegen(g)))` self-stability (file docstring lines 6-8), NOT equality to pre-refactor bytes, and its corpus covers DATA_SOURCE(185), MODEL_SCORE(264), RATING_STEP(308), POLARS/explore(409-473) with adversarial descriptions (quotes, triple-quotes, braces, backslashes, unicode, newlines — lines 61-70). So neither a branch-conditional nor a collapsed implementation breaks any test or regresses the round-trip.

Pre-envelope guards are untouched and must stay: _gen_explore `len(source_names)!=1` ParseError (882-889); _gen_transform 0-source / >1-source ConfigErrors (1008-1023). The proposal keeps per-builder computation of decorator+pre_body, so these survive. `_strip_generated_boilerplate_from_code` (with per-kind `kind=`/`param_names=`) stays in each builder unchanged.

Net: sound direction, low real risk, genuine readability win (template-constant vs inline-f-string split collapses), but the "zero byte change" claim is wrong for model_score and pre_body is branch-dependent for 4/6 builders — caveats that must be honoured in implementation, hence marginal not sound.

verdict.evidence:
Re-read graph_to_code_multi (886-1263) in full plus helpers (_build_id_to_func 544, _build_node_sources 597, _build_node_source_ids 609, _generate_pipeline_lines 667, build_edge_join_boundary_target_roles in _edge_join.py 329) and the GraphEdge model (_types.py 611: handles are non-empty-str-or-None, empty string rejected by validator).

The proposal's CENTRAL premise is factually wrong: it claims the validation is implemented "TWICE inline (1013-1043 for targets, 1044-1068 for sources)... re-implemented a THIRD time as _resolve_submodel_endpoint" and instructs to "delete the two inline in__/out__ loops at 1013-1068 in favour of" a single validate-and-return-child_id helper. But the in__ loop (1013-1043) is NOT pure validation — it MUTATES sm_node_sources/sm_node_source_ids (1039-1042: setdefault(child_id) then dedup-append src_name = root_id_to_func.get(edge.source, ...)). Those dicts are then passed to _generate_pipeline_lines at 1090/1092 to generate the SUBMODEL file. This is the sole producer of cross-boundary parent-input wiring into the submodel function.

Empirically verified: a graph with root node "RootSource" -> submodel via targetHandle "in__child_a" emits modules/sm1.py containing `def ChildA(RootSource: pl.LazyFrame)` with body `df = RootSource`. Delete the in__ loop in favour of a pure resolver and that parameter + body line vanish — a SILENT miswiring / data-loss regression (precisely the failure class CLAUDE.md forbids). The in__ loop also (a) populates submodel_child_ids[sm_node_id] at 1012, which _resolve_submodel_endpoint READS at 1139, so it is a prerequisite not a duplicate; and (b) dedups (`if src_name not in existing`) whereas the root walk at 1182 appends unconditionally — different output semantics, so a single shared builder cannot serve both.

Accurate decomposition: there is ONE mutation+validation (in__ loop), ONE pure validation (out__ loop 1044-1068, which IS a true duplicate of _resolve_submodel_endpoint's out__ path and could fold into it), and ONE pure resolver (_resolve_submodel_endpoint). Error-field divergence I checked (inline `handle=handle` vs resolver `handle=handle or None`; inline `submodel=sm_name` vs resolver `node_id.removeprefix("submodel__")`) turns out equivalent given the model invariant (handle never "") and sm_node_id=f"submodel__{sm_name}", so consolidating the out__ loop alone is behaviour-preserving.

The two ROOT walks (1156-1183 sources; 1195-1235 connects) DO share identical endpoint resolution + func-name lookup, but produce different structures (walk 1 filters `actual_tgt not in root_node_ids` -> root_node_sources/_ids; walk 2 unfiltered -> root_connect_pairs incl. source_port/target_port + submodel_edge_join_target_roles lookup at 1232). They cannot collapse to ONE walk but CAN each become _build_root_node_sources(...) / _build_root_connect_pairs(...) named helpers — that part is sound. Likewise extracting _generate_submodel_files(...) is fine PROVIDED the in__ mutation stays inside it.

Net: the structural decomposition into ~4 named helpers is worthwhile and behaviour-preserving IF (1) the in__ loop's source-injection mutation is preserved verbatim inside _generate_submodel_files (only the out__ pure-validation loop may be replaced by the shared resolver), and (2) the no-submodel branch is NOT forced onto a "shared" builder that drops its no-dedup connect semantics. As written ("delete the two inline loops", "three validation copies", no-submodel branch calls shared builders) the proposal would drop the cross-boundary submodel-input wiring => UNSOUND for that specific instruction. Hence marginal: real cleanup available, but the proposal mischaracterises essential mutating logic as redundant validation and must be re-scoped before implementation. Existing net (TestItem20SubmodelCrossBoundaryHandleValidation: 8 passed) locks the RAISE behaviour but I found NO test asserting the in__ source-injection appears in the emitted submodel file body — so a naive implementation of this proposal could pass CI while silently regressing; a guard test must be added first.
verdict.est_reduction: Overstated. Real, safe reduction ~ cx 71 -> ~25-30 (orchestrator) by extracting 4 helpers + folding ONLY the out__ pure-validation loop into the resolver; ~30-40 LOC net, not ~80. The claimed ~80 LOC via "dedup of 3 validation copies + 2 edge walks" double-counts: the in__ loop and the two root walks are not removable duplicates.

verdict.recommended_action: Re-scope before implementing. (1) Extract _generate_submodel_files(...) but KEEP the in__ loop's mutation (sm_node_sources/_ids injection + dedup + submodel_child_ids population) verbatim inside it; only replace the out__ pure-validation loop (1044-1068) with the shared _resolve_submodel_endpoint out__ path.
