verdict.evidence:
Re-read src/haute/modelling/_rustystats.py:435-467 in full. Current structure: (1) attr loop over 5 pairs read via float(getattr(model, attr)); (2) method loop over 4 pairs read via float(getattr(model, method)()); (3) a converged block stats["converged"]=1.0 if model.converged else 0.0. Each is independently wrapped in try/except logging logger.warning("fit_stat_failed", attr=<source name>, error=str(exc)).

COMPLEXITY IS INCIDENTAL: the only thing differing between the two loops is whether the resolved attribute is called; that is "how to read the value," which a per-row extractor lambda captures cleanly. The three blocks (2 loops + converged) collapse to one loop + one data table. This is a legitimate, textbook table-drive refactor — removable, not essential.

BEHAVIOR PRESERVATION — traced every case: attribute-vs-method read moved verbatim into lambdas (float(m.deviance) vs float(m.aic())); float() coercion preserved; converged 1.0/0.0 mapping preserved; per-stat try/except so one failure does not abort the rest is preserved; iteration order preserved (5 attrs, 4 methods, converged) and dict insertion order keeps stats identical. Happy path covered by tests/test_rustystats_algorithm.py:426-436 (deviance/aic/bic present, converged==1.0) and tests/test_training_job_no_glm_cv.py:249.

TWO CAVEATS keeping this from "sound":
1) Log-fidelity trap. For 3 stats the SOURCE name differs from the LABEL: nobs->n_obs, df_resid->df_residual, llf->log_likelihood. Current code logs attr=<source name>. The proposal's headline _FIT_STATS example uses 2-tuples ("deviance", lambda...) with NO source-name field, so a unified loop would log attr=<label>, silently changing these 3 warning fields. The proposal's own note recognizes this and says to carry the original attr string as a third tuple element — but that contradicts the 2-tuple example, so the proposal is internally inconsistent. Byte-identical logs hold ONLY if the implementer uses the 3-tuple (attr,label,extract) form. No test asserts the attr= field on the failure path, so this is unverified by the suite.
2) Inaccurate status-quo description. The proposal repeatedly describes current reads as float(getattr(model, x)[()]) with a numpy-scalar [()] index; the actual code has NO [()] — it is plain float(getattr(model, attr)). A faithful verbatim move must copy float(model.deviance) WITHOUT [()]; if an implementer trusts the proposal's prose and adds [()], it would break (floats are not subscriptable). The error is in the description, not the target shape, but it raises implementation risk.

Net: right shape, behavior-preserving IFF the corrective 3-tuple note is followed and the bogus [()] is ignored.

Ignore the proposal's spurious float(getattr(model,x)[()]) description — the real reads have no [()] and must stay that way. Before merging, add a failure-path test (e.g. a stub model raising on .llf / .df_resid) asserting the logged attr= equals the SOURCE name, since no current test guards log fidelity. With those two conditions met, the refactor is safe and worthwhile; without the 3-tuple form it silently changes 3 log fields and should be rejected.

item.why_complex: ESSENTIAL-but-extractable. The read+predict+metrics triplet (read partition -> to_numpy target -> algo.predict -> optional weight -> compute_metrics) appears twice (1135-1147 and 1156-1172) with identical structure. item.proposal: Extract `_partition_metrics(data_path, partition, glm_columns, features, algo, model, *, stage_name, execution_context) -> tuple[metrics, y_true, y_pred, w]` (or a small dataclass) that performs read -> y_true -> predict -> weight -> compute_metrics. Call it for the diagnostics partition (reusing y_true/y_pred/w for the downstream plots) and again for validation when `diagnostics_set=='holdout' and has_validation`. The diagnostics-set selection (holdout>validation>train) stays inline.

The diagnostics partition's y_true/y_pred/w must still be returned and reused by the subsequent double_lift/AvE/residuals/lorenz/PDP calls (they currently read these locals) — the helper returns them rather than recomputing. `del val_df` and gc semantics for the validation read are preserved inside/after the helper. metrics-vs-holdout_metrics binding order (holdout_metrics=metrics BEFORE metrics is rebound) is retained.

verdict.evidence:
Re-read _compute_metrics in full (src/haute/modelling/_training_job.py:1068-1289), _read_partition (1042-1066), compute_metrics (src/haute/modelling/_metrics.py:102+), and _mem_checkpoint (src/haute/modelling/_algorithms.py:94-112).

KERNEL OF TRUTH: The two read+predict+metrics blocks share a ~6-line skeleton (read partition -> diag_df[target].to_numpy() -> algo.predict(model, df, features) -> diag_df[weight].to_numpy() if self.weight else None -> compute_metrics(..., variance_power=vp)). Triplet A = lines 1127-1147; triplet B = 1156-1172. Real incidental duplication exists.

BUT the proposal as specified is NOT behavior-preserving — three asymmetries it glosses over:

(1) _mem_checkpoint side effect: the diagnostics read emits `_mem_checkpoint(f"read {diagnostics_set} partition for diagnostics ({len(diag_df):,} rows)")` at line 1134, BETWEEN read and y_true extraction. The validation read (1156-1173) emits NO checkpoint. _mem_checkpoint is NOT a no-op: it writes a flushed+fsync'd line to a persistent crash-survival mem log (_algorithms.py:94-112) that this memory-critical subsystem maintains deliberately for OOM forensics. The proposal's signature `_partition_metrics(data_path, partition, glm_columns, features, algo, model, *, stage_name, execution_context)` contains NO checkpoint-label parameter. So a helper doing the shared skeleton would either DROP the diagnostics checkpoint or ADD a spurious one to the validation path — an observable behavior change (different mem-log output).

(2) Frame lifetime asymmetry: diag_df is reused for ~125 downstream lines — compute_ave_per_feature (1180), shap_summary (1195), _build_pool (1201), compute_pdp (1227) — and deleted only at line 1262 (then gc.collect() at 1263). val_df is deleted IMMEDIATELY at line 1173. A single helper must therefore branch keep-vs-del on the frame; not symmetric "read->predict->metrics".

(3) Return arity asymmetry: the diagnostics call must return FOUR live values (diag_df itself PLUS y_true/y_pred/w, all consumed downstream — note diag_df the DataFrame, not just the numpy arrays, escapes for SHAP/pool/PDP), while the validation call returns just `metrics` and discards everything else.

FACTUAL SLIP in proposal: it claims to preserve "del val_df and gc semantics for the validation read" — but there is NO gc.collect() after the validation read (line 1173 is bare `del val_df`); the only gc.collect() is at 1263 after `del diag_df`. Signals the author did not precisely trace.

CORRECTLY preserved by any reasonable extraction: columns=glm_columns on both reads (projection pushdown unchanged), distinct stage_names (`training_{diagnostics_set}_diagnostics_materialise` vs `training_validation_metrics_materialise`), holdout_metrics=metrics binding BEFORE metrics is rebound (1153 vs 1166), and the holdout>validation>train selection staying inline.

NET: real but small duplication; however the helper must take conditional params (checkpoint label/emit, keep-vs-del frame) to be faithful, which dilutes the readability win, and as literally written the proposal changes the mem-log side-effect behavior. Medium risk in a hot path explicitly engineered for "each partition read at most once".

If pursued, amend so the helper either (a) returns (metrics, df, y_true, y_pred, w) and the CALLER keeps emitting its own checkpoint + manages del/gc (so the helper is pure read->predict->metrics with no logging/lifetime concerns), or (b) takes explicit `checkpoint_label: str | None` and `release_frame: bool` params. item.title: render_loss_curve_svg X-axis tick labels cast iteration ticks with int(tick), truncating non-integer 'nice' tick values to wrong labels (e.g. 2.5 -> '2')
item.location: src/haute/modelling/_charts.py:401-408 (x-axis label loop: `for tick in _nice_ticks(x_min, x_max, 6): ... f'{int(tick)}'`)
item.failure_scenario: _nice_ticks(x_min, x_max, 6) can legitimately return fractional tick positions (it rounds the STEP to a nice 1/2/5*magnitude but starts at floor(min/step)*step, and for small iteration ranges the step can be < 1, e.g. for a 0..3 range it produces 0,0.5,1.0,... or for a subsampled range like 7..19 it can yield 7.5, 10, 12.5). The x label loop renders `int(tick)`, which truncates toward zero: 2.5 and 2.9 both print '2', 12.5 prints '12'. Two adjacent gridline labels can therefore collide or be numerically wrong, mislabelling the iteration axis on the model card's loss curve. Unlike the y-axis (which uses `_format_tick`), the x-axis is the only place a raw `int()` truncation is applied to a `_nice_ticks` output. Affects every loss curve whose iteration span makes _nice_ticks choose a sub-integer or *.5 step (short training runs, or any run after >300-point subsampling narrows the rendered domain).

item.location: src/haute/modelling/_model_card.py:105 (metrics) vs 234-237 (params); contrast with the math.isfinite guard used for metric_rows
item.failure_scenario: metric_rows (line 105) guard each value with `math.isfinite(v)` -> 'N/A', but this assumes every metrics value is a float. compute_metrics can inject a non-metric entry `non_finite_rows_filtered` (a float count) which is fine, but glm_fit_statistics values surfaced into metrics (via the AIC/BIC/deviance path in _mlflow_log, and into the card's metrics dict) are floats too. The real asymmetry: a metric value that is a numpy float (np.float64) passes math.isfinite, but a metric that failed and was stored as a non-float (e.g. None from a degraded GLM stat) raises TypeError inside math.isfinite, aborting model-card generation — which is then swallowed by the `try/except` at _mlflow_log.py:362-373 ('model_card_generation_failed'), so the card is silently dropped from the run. The card generation is best-effort and never fails the run, but the operator loses the entire HTML card (every chart) because one metric value was a non-float, with only a WARNING. This is a fail-loud-mandate gap: a single bad metric value silently removes the whole diagnostics artifact.

verdict.evidence: Repro (modelling__NEWBUG-CARD-NONFINITE-PARAM.py) output: "(B) REACHABILITY: compute_metrics (sole producer) yields ONLY floats ([...,'non_finite_rows_filtered',...]); the filed non-float production path is NOT reachable." Code-trace: the `metrics` dict reaching generate_model_card is assigned SOLELY from compute_metrics() at _training_job.py:1141/1166 (aliased 1153); grep confirms NO metrics[...]=, .update, or .setdefault mutation anywhere in _training_job.py. Every metric fn in _metrics.py is `-> float` and wraps output in float(...); non_finite_rows_filtered = float(n_filtered) (_metrics.py:144). GLM fit stats (aic/bic/deviance/null_deviance) are logged ONLY as top-level MLflow metrics via mlflow.log_metric at _mlflow_log.py:344-346 — they are NEVER merged into the metrics dict, contradicting the filed claim that "glm_fit_statistics values surfaced into the card's metrics dict" and that "the metric finiteness guard is bypassed for holdout/glm-derived metrics." Mechanism part (A) is real but latent: math.isfinite(None) raises TypeError and generate_model_card has no per-value guard (line 105), so IF a non-float were passed the whole card aborts and is swallowed at _mlflow_log.py:362-373 — but no production path delivers a non-float. (C) secondary cosmetic claim confirmed: NaN/Inf param renders raw 'nan'/'inf' via str(v) at line 235 while NaN/Inf metric renders 'N/A' — display-only, never aborts, params are hyperparameters not NaN/Inf in practice. Not present in review/02-findings/catalog.md.
verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\modelling__NEWBUG-CARD-NONFINITE-PARAM.py
verdict.est_reduction: none (no behavioral bug to fix; production metrics dict is provably dict[str,float])
verdict.recommended_action: Reject as filed. The load-bearing production failure path (a non-float / degraded GLM stat reaching line 105 and silently dropping the card) does not exist: compute_metrics is the sole producer of the metrics dict and only ever yields floats, and GLM fit stats are logged as separate MLflow metrics, never merged into the card's metrics dict. What remains is (1) a latent input-robustness gap at the generate_model_card boundary (no per-value type guard) and (2) a cosmetic param-vs-metric NaN/Inf formatting asymmetry. If any hardening is desired (defensive only, not a real bug), it would be a one-line change to guard the metrics comprehension with isinstance/try (e.g. `f"{v:.4f}" if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and math.isfinite(v) else "N/A"`) and optionally apply the same N/A treatment to non-finite params — but per the codebase's no-unnecessary-fallback mandate this is arguably noise. Do not add to catalog as a confirmed bug.

item.title: render_ave_feature_svg decides whether to rotate x labels using `len(str(lab)) > 5` on the RAW labels, but _render_dual_axis_chart then truncates each label to 15 chars; long categorical levels that share a 15-char prefix render as indistinguishable rotated labels with no disambiguation
item.location: src/haute/modelling/_charts.py:510-524 (render_ave_feature_svg: any_long = any(len(str(lab)) > 5 ...)) and 209-224 (_render_dual_axis_chart truncates to 15 / rotates)

The actuary reading the per-feature Actual-vs-Expected chart on the model card cannot tell which bin is which, and may misattribute a mis-calibration to the wrong level. The rotate decision (>5 chars) and the truncation width (15) are independent magic numbers that don't coordinate, so the truncation silently destroys label uniqueness. Distinct from the catalogued chart issues (none cover AvE label collisions).

item.what_it_does: After execution, builds per-node timings/memory/status/columns/warnings payloads restricted to the target node's relevant ancestors.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: five near-identical dict/list comprehensions each re-iterate results.items() and re-apply the same `nid in node_map and nid in relevant` predicate. The repetition (not the filtering) is the cost; the filtering itself is essential.
item.current_metrics: preview_node whole fn len=216 cx=38 nest=2; this block ~34 lines of 6 parallel comprehensions
item.proposal: Extract a small helper that computes the ordered list of (nid, NodeResult) pairs once: `relevant_results = [(nid, r) for nid, r in results.items() if nid in node_map and nid in relevant]`, then build timings/memory/node_columns/node_available_columns/node_schema_warnings/node_statuses from that single filtered sequence. This also removes the inconsistency where node_statuses currently skips the `nid in node_map` guard (see BUG-1).
item.behavior_preservation: All six outputs iterate the same dict in the same insertion order and apply the same membership predicate; factoring the predicate out once yields identical keys/values. node_statuses gains the node_map guard, but `relevant = ancestors(... set(node_map.keys()))` so every relevant id is already in node_map -> output is byte-identical on every input.
item.est_reduction: ~18 LOC; cx -5 on preview_node

verdict.evidence: Re-read pipeline.py:569-621 plus the predicate's transitive deps (_topo.ancestors L105-117, _graph_utils.build_parents_of L19-28, executor._result_order_for_target L788-802, executor results-build L1082-1256). The complexity is INCIDENTAL: six parallel comprehensions over results.items() re-apply the identical `nid in node_map and nid in relevant` predicate; the predicate (filtering) is essential and the proposal preserves it, only factoring the re-iteration out once. BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING on every traced case: (1) Order — building `relevant_results = [(nid,r) for nid,r in results.items() if nid in node_map and nid in relevant]` then deriving the two lists (timings/memory) and four dicts (node_columns/node_available_columns/node_schema_warnings/node_statuses) from it yields identical insertion order, since a comprehension over an ordered list preserves the order of results.items(). (2) The node_statuses guard addition — current node_statuses (L608) omits `nid in node_map`. Adding it is a provable no-op because node_statuses iterates results.items(), and results.keys() ⊆ result_order ⊆ topo `order` ⊆ node_map.keys(): executor.py:1206 does `node_map[nid].data` unconditionally on the happy path (would KeyError otherwise), and result_order is a filtered subset of `order` (_result_order_for_target returns `[nid for nid in order if nid in needed]`). (3) else-branch `relevant=set(results.keys())` (L585-586) is unchanged and feeds the same sequence (and is effectively unreachable: L507 rejects node_id∉node_map). (4) Block stays inside the same try; except paths at L650+ unchanged; all six comprehensions are pure (no side effects). item.what_it_does: On an HTTPException during prep, transitions the job to memory_limited / contract_error / error with a fields payload derived from the status code.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: a 3-arm if/elif/else where the 507 and 4xx arms are textually identical except for the `to=` reason; the third arm is a strict subset. The status->reason mapping and the optional error_code/error_detail capture are the only varying parts.
item.current_metrics: start() len=176 cx high; this handler ~36 lines
item.proposal: Table-drive: `reason = 'memory_limited' if code==507 else 'contract_error' if 400<=code<500 else 'error'`. Build a base `fields={'error': str(exc.detail)}`; when reason != 'error', also add error_detail/error_code/http_status_code. One `self._lifecycle.transition(job_id, to=reason, message=str(exc.detail), fields=fields)` call. Fold the separate ExecutionAdmissionError/ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError arm (533-541) into the same helper since _memory_limit_http_exception already yields a 507 (also fixes BUG-3).
item.behavior_preservation: Same reason chosen for every status code, same message, same fields keys for each branch; error_code is still `detail.get('error_code')` only when detail is a dict. Output records are identical for all three current branches.
item.est_reduction: ~22 LOC; cx -4

verdict.evidence:
Re-read src/haute/routes/_train_service.py:533-591 in full plus collaborators (JobLifecycle.transition _job_lifecycle.py:105-168; _memory_limit_http_exception _train_service.py:91-94 -> HTTPException(507, detail=exc.to_payload()); ExecutionAdmissionError.to_payload _execution_admission.py:268-284 returns a dict with error_code='memory_limit').

PART A — the 3-arm HTTPException handler (542-578) IS incidentally complex and the table-drive over JUST these three arms is behavior-preserving:
- reason dispatch: `'memory_limited' if code==507 else 'contract_error' if 400<=code<500 else 'error'` reproduces the if(507)/elif(400<=c<500)/else exactly; 507 is tested first so no 4xx/507 overlap.
- 507 arm + 4xx arm: current fields = {error:str(detail), error_detail:detail, error_code: detail.get('error_code') if dict else None, http_status_code: exc.status_code}; else arm: fields = {error:str(detail)} only. Proposed base {error:str(detail)} plus the three extra keys when reason!='error' matches. CAVEAT (real hazard): http_status_code MUST be wired to exc.status_code, NOT a hardcoded 507 — the 4xx arm has a VARIABLE status (422/400/409 etc.); a naive table that hardcodes 507 would silently corrupt http_status_code for contract_error jobs.
- bare `raise` (line 578) preserved => same exception/traceback. OK.

PART B — the proposal OVER-REACHES by folding the admission-error arm (533-541), and that fold is NOT behavior-preserving:
- Current 533-541: http_exc=_memory_limit_http_exception(exc) (507, detail=dict); records fields={'error': str(http_exc.detail)} ONLY — NO error_detail/error_code/http_status_code; re-raises `raise http_exc from None` (line 541, explicit cause suppression).
- Folding it through the 507-style handler ADDS three keys (error_detail, error_code='memory_limit', http_status_code=507) to the persisted job record — an OBSERVABLE change to stored job state for the admission/memory-limit prep path.
- It also changes `raise http_exc from None` -> bare `raise`, altering exception chaining, and (depending on how the fold is written) risks re-raising the original non-HTTP ExecutionAdmissionError instead of the constructed 507 HTTPException => a 507->500 status regression at the route boundary.
- The proposal itself says 'also fixes BUG-3' — i.e. it deliberately CHANGES behavior, which contradicts its own behavior_preservation claim ('Output records are identical for all three current branches'). That claim is true only for the three HTTPException branches and silently omits the admission branch.

Test reality: tests/test_training_memory_safety.py:269-273 asserts error_detail.error_code=='memory_limit' and http_status_code==507 for a memory_limited job, but that test exercises _launch_background (the background thread), NOT TrainService.start — it does not constrain start()'s arms. No test pins start()'s admission-arm fields-only shape, so the field drift introduced by the fold would NOT be caught by the suite (dangerous silent change, against the project's 'fail loudly' rule).

Conclusion: the simplification of the THREE HTTPException arms is sound; bundling BUG-3 (the admission-arm fold) into a 'behavior-preserving' simplification is unsound and changes persisted records + exception chaining.
verdict.est_reduction: ~12-15 LOC for the safe part (consolidating the 3 HTTPException arms); the additional ~7 LOC the proposal attributes to folding 533-541 should NOT be taken as part of a behavior-preserving simplification. cx -3 realistic (not -4).
verdict.recommended_action: Split the item. (1) SIMPLIFICATION: table-drive ONLY the 3-arm HTTPException handler (542-578): reason = 'memory_limited' if code==507 else 'contract_error' if 400<=code<500 else 'error'; fields = {'error': str(exc.detail)} and, when reason!='error', add error_detail=exc.detail, error_code=(exc.detail.get('error_code') if isinstance(exc.detail, dict) else None), http_status_code=exc.status_code (MUST be exc.status_code, not a constant — guards the variable-code 4xx arm); keep the bare `raise`. Add a regression test asserting http_status_code==422 (or another non-507 4xx) for a contract_error job to lock the variable-status behavior. (2) Do NOT fold lines 533-541 here. Handle BUG-3 (admission arm missing error_detail/error_code/http_status_code, and `raise ... from None` semantics) as its own bugfix, TDD-style with a failing test that pins the desired admission-arm record shape and the 507 status at the route boundary, so the field/chaining change is explicit and caught by tests.
verdict.repro_path: tests/test_training_memory_safety.py:269-273 (shows the memory_limited field contract, via _launch_background); src/haute/routes/_train_service.py:533-541 (admission arm: fields-only + raise http_exc from None) vs 542-578 (HTTPException arms: full fields + bare raise).

item.what_it_does: Removes the temp parquet on every failure path before re-raising.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: the exact two-line guard `if os.path.exists(tmp_parquet): os.unlink(tmp_parquet)` is copy-pasted 4 times in _execute_and_sink and twice more in _launch_background. The four except arms also share the shape transition(to=...)+raise.
item.current_metrics: _execute_and_sink len=227 cx=30; ~8 duplicated cleanup lines
item.proposal: Add a module-level `_safe_unlink(path: str)` (single `with suppress(FileNotFoundError): os.unlink(path)`), and call it once. Better: wrap the body so the temp file is unlinked in a single `except Exception` cleanup that re-derives the terminal reason via the same status->reason table as SIMP-2, rather than four arms each repeating the unlink. The unconditional `del/gc/_malloc_trim` already lives in the happy path; only the unlink needs centralising.
item.behavior_preservation: os.unlink under an exists-check is exactly FileNotFoundError-suppressed unlink; suppress() preserves the 'best-effort delete' semantics. Each except arm keeps its own transition reason and HTTP mapping, so error surfaces are unchanged.
item.est_reduction: ~10 LOC; cx -3

verdict.evidence:
The proposal bundles two distinct ideas with opposite soundness.

(A) NARROW `_safe_unlink` DEDUP — SOUND but small. The guard `if os.path.exists(tmp_parquet): os.unlink(tmp_parquet)` appears 6x: _execute_and_sink lines 967-968, 981-982, 996-997, 1000-1001 and _launch_background 1229-1230, 1236-1237. `tmp_parquet` is always a bound str (created at line 833 before the try), so no None/empty case. `with suppress(FileNotFoundError): os.unlink(path)` is behavior-preserving for a private mkstemp temp file: it deletes iff present and swallows FileNotFoundError — the only error the exists-check guarded — and is in fact strictly MORE correct (closes the TOCTOU hole the exists-check leaves open). All 6 sites want identical 'best-effort delete this temp file' semantics, so one helper fits. This part is safe.

(B) THE 'BETTER' VARIANT (collapse the four except arms 966-1012 into one `except Exception` + 'the same status->reason table as SIMP-2') — UNSOUND, on three independent grounds:
  1. The referenced table DOES NOT EXIST for this function. transition(to=...) takes the terminal reason DIRECTLY (_job_lifecycle.py:125 `update['terminal_reason']=to`). There is no status->reason map in _train_service.py; the only mapping (TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS) goes the OPPOSITE direction (reason->status) and lives in a DIFFERENT subsystem (_optimiser_service.py:342). Each arm chooses its reason from the exception TYPE, not from a status. The premise is fabricated.
  2. The four arms are ESSENTIAL — they diverge on every axis: (arm1 ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError) warn-log `pipeline_exec_memory_limited`, transition memory_limited, raise NEW 507 via _memory_limit_http_exception(exc) `from None`; (arm2 BoundedMemoryUnsupportedError) warn-log `pipeline_bounded_streaming_unsupported`, transition contract_error, raise NEW 422 with the DETAILED message `from None`; (arm3 HTTPException) NO log, NO transition (already done at the raise site, e.g. 909-915 — collapsing would double-write and could clobber a more specific reason via the precedence check at _job_lifecycle.py:154), bare re-raise of the ORIGINAL exc; (arm4 Exception) error-log `pipeline_exec_failed`, transition error with `error_msg=f'Pipeline execution failed: {exc}'`, but raise NEW 500 whose detail is a GENERIC string deliberately different from the transition message (log-only info-disclosure boundary) and WITHOUT `from None` (chains exc). A single arm cannot reproduce this without rebuilding the same 4-way isinstance dispatch — no real simplification, high risk of silently flipping an HTTP status / dropping a log event / breaking the disclosure boundary or the no-transition re-raise.
  3. Catch ORDER is load-bearing (memory/bounded subclasses before bare HTTPException before Exception); a naive collapse risks misclassification.

So the defensible work is ONLY the tiny `_safe_unlink` helper; the proposal's headline reduction and 'low risk' are largely predicated on the four-arm collapse, which is unsound. Hence marginal, not sound. Note: `suppress` is not currently imported (grep confirms only a comment at line 462), so the helper also needs `from contextlib import suppress`.
verdict.est_reduction: ~6 net LOC (6 two-line guards -> 6 one-line calls + ~2-line helper + 1 import); cx -1 to -2 split across _execute_and_sink and _launch_background. NOT the claimed cx -3 / ~10 LOC, because that figure assumes the unsound four-arm collapse.
verdict.repro_path: Trace src/haute/routes/_train_service.py: tmp_parquet bound at 833; four except arms 966-1012 each unlink then diverge (log event, terminal_reason, NEW-vs-original exception, HTTP status, from-None chaining, arm3 does NO transition); _launch_background finally 1229-1230 and thread-start failure 1236-1237 unlink the consumed parquet. _job_lifecycle.py:124-125 shows transition writes reason directly (no status->reason derivation); reverse map TERMINAL_REASON_TO_STATUS is in _optimiser_service.py:342 (different subsystem). _train_service.py has no `suppress` import (grep).
verdict.recommended_action: ACCEPT ONLY the narrow dedup: add module-level `_safe_unlink(path: str)` = `with suppress(FileNotFoundError): os.unlink(path)` plus `from contextlib import suppress`, and replace all 6 exists-check+unlink guards with `_safe_unlink(tmp_parquet)`. REJECT the 'better' variant: do NOT collapse the four except arms — they encode distinct terminal reasons, log events, HTTP status codes (507/422/passthrough/500), the deliberate no-transition re-raise (arm3), the generic-detail-vs-detailed-message disclosure boundary (arm4), and from-None chaining. TDD: before refactor add a test asserting each arm still produces its exact (status_code, terminal_reason, logged event) and that the temp file is gone, so any future collapse regression is caught.

item.what_it_does: Translates a path-resolution ValueError into HTTPException(400) for embedded-null vs HTTPException(403) for project-root escape.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: the identical idiom `status_code = 400 if 'embedded null byte' in str(exc) else 403; raise HTTPException(status_code, detail=str(exc)) from None` is duplicated in three call sites across two route modules.
item.current_metrics: 3 copies x ~3 lines
item.proposal: Extract a shared `path_value_error_to_http(exc: ValueError) -> HTTPException` into routes/_helpers.py and call `raise path_value_error_to_http(exc) from None` at all three sites. Keys the 400-vs-403 decision on the same substring in one place.
item.behavior_preservation: The substring test, status codes, detail string, and `from None` chaining are reproduced verbatim in the helper; callers raise the returned exception identically.
item.est_reduction: ~6 LOC net; removes a 3-way drift hazard

verdict.evidence:
Re-read all three cited sites in full. The idiom `status_code = 400 if "embedded null byte" in str(exc) else 403; raise HTTPException(status_code=status_code, detail=str(exc)) from None` is byte-for-byte identical at src/haute/routes/pipeline.py:155-156 (_validate_runtime_input_paths), pipeline.py:177-178 (_validate_sink_output_path), and json_cache.py:158-159 (_resolve_data_path). A repo-wide grep finds EXACTLY these three occurrences in src/ — no missed site, so the extraction fully removes the drift hazard. Complexity is INCIDENTAL: a single substring decision duplicated three times, not three genuinely distinct behaviors.

Behavior-preservation: the only non-obvious concern is whether moving construction into a helper that RETURNS (not raises) the HTTPException and then doing `raise path_value_error_to_http(exc) from None` at the call site preserves the `from None` traceback semantics vs the original inline `raise HTTPException(...) from None`. I proved equivalence by executing both forms under .venv python for both branches:
- 400 case ("Path contains an embedded null byte"): orig and proposed both give status=400, detail='Path contains an embedded null byte', __suppress_context__=True, __cause__=None.
- 403 case ("Cannot access paths outside the project root"): both give status=403, same detail, __suppress_context__=True, __cause__=None.
Because the helper returns rather than raises, it attaches no __context__ of its own; the caller's `from None` sets __suppress_context__=True identically. Substring test, status codes, detail string, and chaining are all reproduced exactly.

The driving ValueError messages originate in src/haute/_path_resolution.py ("embedded null byte" L20; "resolves outside the project root" L92/L133), inspected identically by the helper. The proposal CORRECTLY excludes _resolve_config_path (json_cache.py:175-176), whose different unconditional-403 idiom (no substring test) must NOT be folded into the shared helper — doing so would change its behavior to emit 400 on null bytes. Extraction target routes/_helpers.py already hosts a sibling "HTTP error helpers" section (raise_node_not_found / raise_node_type_error) with HTTPException imported, so this is idiomatic. Existing direct tests at tests/test_pipeline_runtime_path_validation.py (lines 43,65,99: assert 403/400 + detail substrings) exercise the public callers and remain green unchanged.
verdict.est_reduction: ~6 LOC net (3 x ~2-line except bodies collapse to one helper); eliminates a 3-way drift hazard
verdict.repro_path: .venv\Scripts\python.exe executed inline trace comparing `raise HTTPException(...) from None` vs `raise helper(exc) from None` for both null-byte (400) and escape (403) messages; identical status_code/detail/__suppress_context__=True/__cause__=None in all four runs.
verdict.recommended_action: Accept. Extract `path_value_error_to_http(exc: ValueError) -> HTTPException` into src/haute/routes/_helpers.py beside the existing HTTP error helpers, keying the 400-vs-403 decision on `"embedded null byte" in str(exc)` and returning `HTTPException(status_code=..., detail=str(exc))`. Replace the three except bodies with `raise path_value_error_to_http(exc) from None`. Do NOT touch _resolve_config_path (json_cache.py:175-176). item.what_it_does: After the debounce window, classifies pending watch events, resolves them to pipeline files, reparses, and broadcasts graph_update/parse_error.

item.what_it_does: Scans column stats and emits up to five data-quality issues (missing, constant, negatives, zero-heavy) with severity/label/detail.

Compute `null_ratio = c.null_count/row_count if row_count else 0` once in a tiny local. Keep the cross-category coupling (mostly_null -> danger severity; zero_heavy_names excluded from constant) as explicit inputs to the descriptors.
item.behavior_preservation: Same predicates, same sort keys (including the `.lower()` tie-breaks and negative-count ordering), same severity selection and label/detail strings, same append order -> identical ExploreDataQualitySummary. The only change is where the shared filter/sort lives.

The proposal's core claim — that cx=33 is INCIDENTAL and stems from "repeating the sort-filter-append shape" — is largely false on a decision-point trace. The four build-and-append blocks contribute only ~4 `if <list>:` decisions plus 1 inline severity ternary. The bulk of cx=33 lives in ESSENTIAL predicates/sort-keys: zero_heavy comprehension+lambda (~7 short-circuits: two `and`, three `(z or 0)`, lambda `or`), constant comprehension (5 `and`s incl. the unique `distinct_count is not None` guard), missing (`if>0` + lambda ternary + separate `mostly_null` recompute with `and`), negatives (`(neg or 0)` x3). Module-level complexity is conserved; the "33->12" figure is a where-the-decision-is-counted artifact, not real logic reduction. The four categories are NOT a uniform table: detail strategies differ (missing emits worst-one `worst.name`; negatives emits top-one with `:,` count; constant & zero_heavy emit all-names via _names_text), severity differs (missing conditional on sibling `mostly_null_columns`; others fixed), and there is genuine cross-category coupling — `zero_heavy_names` (a LATER category) feeds the `constant` filter, and `mostly_null_columns` feeds `missing` severity. OPTIONAL `_strip_heavy` COMPANION (unsound as written). The JSON proposes `_strip_heavy(job)` for "the two dict-comprehensions (lines 195, 527)". item.what_it_does: Builds one batched aggregation expression list per column, then reads the collected row back into ExploreColumnStat objects.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: the build loop (422-448) and the readback loop (456-500) are two parallel dtype-dispatch ladders (is_numeric / _supports_min_max / _has_categorical_value_counts) that must stay in lockstep; the alias strings (`f'min::{name}'` etc.) are spelled out twice. ESSENTIAL: the single-collect batching is a deliberate perf choice.
item.current_metrics: len=104; two parallel per-column ladders
item.proposal: Introduce a per-statistic descriptor table (alias-suffix, build-expr lambda, parse lambda, dtype-applicability predicate). Both loops iterate the same descriptor list, so the alias and the dtype gate are defined once and cannot drift between aggregate and parse. The categorical-value-counts branch already has single-source helpers; extend that pattern to min/max and the numeric quantile/mean/std/zero/negative set.
item.behavior_preservation: Same aggregation expressions produced in the same order, same alias keys read back, same int()/_format_* coercions -> identical ExploreColumnStat fields. Purely relocates the alias/gate definitions.
item.est_reduction: ~20 LOC; eliminates a build-vs-parse drift class

verdict.evidence:
Re-read _build_frame_stats in full (src/haute/routes/_explore_service.py:408-511) plus every dtype-gate and parse helper (_is_unhashable_dtype:93, _format_display_value:112, _format_numeric_profile_value:126, _supports_min_max:142, _has_categorical_value_counts:154, _min_max_column_expr:170, _categorical_value_counts_{alias,expr}:324-336, _parse_categorical_value_counts:339) and the ExploreColumnStat model (schemas.py:392-412).

DTYPE DISPATCH IS ESSENTIAL (different dtypes genuinely support different aggregations); the proposal correctly targets only the INCIDENTAL duplication of alias strings + gate predicates across the build loop (422-448) and readback loop (456-500). That duplication is real, and _has_categorical_value_counts (docstring at 154-167 explicitly calls itself the single source of truth for the categorical branch) already demonstrates the exact single-source pattern the proposal wants to extend. So the direction is valid.

BUT the two ladders are NOT cleanly isomorphic, and the headline claim 'the alias and dtype gate are defined once and cannot drift' is FALSE for the unique/distinct_count pair — the most asymmetric line in the function:
- BUILD emits `unique::{name}` only when `not _is_unhashable_dtype` (427).
- READBACK runs UNCONDITIONALLY (461-465): `distinct_count = None` if unhashable else `int(aggregate_row["unique::"])`, and feeds a MANDATORY constructor positional (`distinct_count: int | None`, no default). A descriptor whose single applicability predicate gates BOTH loops cannot model this: distinct_count must still be produced (as None) when the build expr is absent. It would remain a hand-written special case OUTSIDE any table, so the '~20 LOC eliminated' is optimistic — the single most drift-prone pair is not covered. Realistic net is ~10-15 LOC, partly offset by the descriptor declarations themselves.

Two further asymmetries a flat descriptor must carry as exceptions: (a) min/max derive TWO aliases from ONE shared sub-expression `_min_max_column_expr(name,dtype)` which casts text/bool to String (170-181) — not a 1-alias→1-expr row; (b) the numeric block uses TWO parse fns (_format_numeric_profile_value for the 5 floats, int() for zero/negative).

RISK (rated medium, accurate): both loops gate categorical as `elif _has_categorical_value_counts` (445/486), i.e. mutually exclusive with the numeric `if dtype.is_numeric()`. The exclusion currently holds only because _has_categorical_value_counts already contains `not dtype.is_numeric()` (164); the `elif` makes that exclusion textually local. Flattening into a descriptor iteration removes that locality, so a careless author writing the categorical predicate as `_supports_categorical_value_counts` would reintroduce exactly the silent dtype-gate drift this audit guards against. This UNDERCUTS the 'cannot drift' selling point rather than supporting it.

BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING? Yes, IF authored carefully: aggregation values are read by named alias via `.row(0, named=True)` (454), so expression ORDER in `select` is value-irrelevant (only a diff/cosmetic concern); Pydantic assigns fields by name with defaults filling absent ones, so `**profile_stats` dict-build order is irrelevant; the per-column emission order (null, unique, min, max, p25, median, mean, p75, std, zero, negative, categorical) and the exact coercions (_format_display_value / _format_numeric_profile_value / int / _parse_categorical_value_counts) can all be reproduced. So no behavior MUST change. But this is NOT a mechanical/obviously-safe transform — it requires correctly re-encoding the distinct_count None-substitution, the shared min/max cast, the dual parse fns, and the numeric/categorical mutual exclusion. Substantial regression coverage exists (test_explore_routes.py and ~20 other suites touch distinct_count/min_value/zero_count/categorical_values), which makes correctness VERIFIABLE but does not remove the authoring hazard.

Net: genuine-but-modest DRY win on a perf-sensitive batched path; the central 'gate defined once' claim does not hold for distinct_count; medium risk concentrated in the numeric/categorical exclusion invariant; the code is already reasonably DRY via the named-alias helpers. Marginal, not sound.
verdict.est_reduction: ~10-15 LOC net (proposal's ~20 is optimistic: distinct_count, the dual min/max alias from a shared cast expr, and the two numeric parse fns remain special cases outside any descriptor table, and the table declarations add lines back)
verdict.recommended_action: Do not adopt as a blanket table-drive. If pursued, scope it narrowly to the part that actually fits: a descriptor list covering ONLY the min/max pair (sharing _min_max_column_expr) and the 7-stat numeric block (carrying its per-stat parse fn), iterated by both loops so those aliases+gates are defined once. Keep null_count and distinct_count as the explicit hand-written constructor args they are today (distinct_count's unconditional None-substitution does not fit the gate-both-loops model). Critically, preserve the numeric-vs-categorical mutual exclusion explicitly (do not rely on _has_categorical_value_counts's internal `not is_numeric` as the sole guard once the `elif` locality is gone). Gate the change behind full re-run of test_explore_routes.py and the dtype-branch suites; require a new test asserting every dtype kind (numeric/temporal/bool/text/object/struct/nested) still yields identical ExploreColumnStat fields before/after. Given the modest payoff and the medium drift risk, lower priority than the cleaner table-drive candidates.
verdict.repro_path: N/A (read-only audit; no behavioral defect in current code — current _build_frame_stats is correct as written)

item.what_it_does: Builds the supersession cache key and the ValueError->HTTPException ladder for preview and for trace.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: preview and trace each hand-roll a supersession key as a flat tuple of alternating literal-name/value pairs, and each has a long `except ValueError` ladder matching message prefixes to status codes. The two key builders share the `_supersession_key` prefix and the same alternating-pair convention.
item.current_metrics: two ~20-line key builders; two ~25-line exception ladders
item.proposal: (a) Replace the alternating literal/value tuples with a single helper `_kv_key(prefix_tuple, **fields)` that sorts/serialises named fields, so a new key field can't be added to the value list but forgotten in the label list. (b) Drive the trace ValueError ladder from an ordered list of (prefix, status, log_event) tuples scanned by a small matcher; the generic 500 stays the default. Preview's ValueError handling is simpler and can reuse the same matcher with its own table.
item.behavior_preservation: The serialised key includes the same components in a stable order (fingerprint already canonical), so cache identity is unchanged; the prefix-matching table reproduces the same status codes and log events in the same precedence order.
item.est_reduction: ~20 LOC; cx -4 across the two handlers

verdict.repro_path: Read pipeline.py:189-249 (key builders) and 402-492 (trace handler + ValueError ladder) and 495-711 (preview handler + typed-exception ladder); _supersession.py (key used only as dict Hashable, so identity == tuple __eq__/__hash__); _cache.py:400-437 (graph_fingerprint canonical); errors.py/executor.py:161 (PreviewProjectionError is ValueError but caught BY TYPE; ConfigError/ParseError/ContractMismatchError are HauteError, not ValueError); _trace_correlation.py:564 and trace.py:366,494 (exact ValueError messages); tests/test_pipeline_route_supersession.py:423,488,1203 (distinctness asserted via HTTP 200/200, NOT tuple shape).
verdict.evidence:
PART (a) _kv_key — SOUND IN PRINCIPLE, ONE CAVEAT. The supersession key is consumed only as a dict key in SupersessionCoordinator (_retain_state/_states: dict[Hashable,...]); nothing inspects its internal shape, and the two distinctness tests assert behaviour via HTTP status (200/200), not the literal tuple. So restructuring is permissible iff equality/distinctness is byte-for-byte preserved. The alternating literal-label/value convention IS an incidental footgun (add a value, forget its label) and centralising it has genuine value. CAVEAT: the preview key ends in `*requested_columns` (an ORDER-SENSITIVE list); currently ['a','b'] and ['b','a'] yield DISTINCT keys. The proposal says _kv_key 'sorts/serialises named fields'. That must mean sort FIELD NAMES (fine); if an implementer sorts the list VALUES, ['a','b']==['b','a'] would collide — a behaviour change. The proposal's own note ('same components in a stable order') implies field-name ordering, so it is preservable, but the wording is loose. Verdict on (a): worthwhile, low-risk, with an explicit 'do not sort list values' constraint.

PART (b) table-drive the ladders — PARTLY UNSOUND (premise false for preview) + MARGINAL for trace. (1) FACTUAL ERROR: the proposal claims 'Preview's ValueError handling is simpler and can reuse the same matcher.' Preview (lines 495-711) has NO `except ValueError` and NO `.startswith` anywhere (grep confirms the ONLY message-prefix ladder in the file is trace at 477-489). Preview dispatches by EXCEPTION TYPE with heterogeneous control flow that a (prefix,status,log_event) matcher cannot reproduce: ConfigError/ParseError/ContractMismatchError RETURN a 200 PreviewNodeResponse(status='error',...) (not raise); ExecutionAdmissionError/ExecutionMemoryLimitExceededError -> 507; BlockingWorkTimeoutError calls preview_token.cancel() + add_done_callback(release_admission) + nulls preview_context; TimeoutError cancels token; PreviewProjectionError(ValueError) -> raise 400 BY TYPE. Forcing these into a message-matcher would change return-vs-raise and drop side effects = bug. So the preview half of (b) is unsound. (2) TRACE half is only marginal: a faithful table cannot be the stated 3-tuple (prefix,status,log_event). Two of three arms require prefix AND a second substring — `startswith('row_index ') AND 'out of range' in detail` and `startswith('Target node ') AND 'not found in graph' in detail` (source msgs confirmed: '_trace_correlation.py:565' and 'trace.py:366'). The author deliberately uses the dual condition as a defensive classifier. The matched arms also log at WARNING and forward the REAL detail to the client, whereas the default logs at ERROR and returns generic _INTERNAL_ERROR_DETAIL. A faithful table therefore needs ~6 attributes per row (prefix, optional-substring, status, log_event, log_level, forward_detail) for just 3 rows + a matcher fn — roughly the same LOC as the explicit if-chain and LESS readable (the explicit ladder shows the exact condition inline, top-to-bottom). The '~20 LOC / cx-4' saving is overstated; realistic net for trace alone is near zero. Default-last ordering (500 fallthrough) is load-bearing and must be retained as the matcher's default arm.

NET: (a) is a sound, worthwhile micro-simplification with one must-not-sort-list-values caveat; (b) is built on a false premise for preview and yields negligible, possibly-negative readability gain for trace. Composite = marginal: cherry-pick (a), drop (b) (or at most extract a trace-only matcher, accepting it does not meaningfully shrink the code).

item.what_it_does: Suppresses the RAM-downsample warning when the user's explicit row_limit is the binding constraint.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: the predicate `user_limit and isinstance(user_limit,(int,float)) and int(user_limit)>0 and row_limit==int(user_limit)` re-parses user_limit exactly the way _clamp_row_limit already did one line earlier; the parsed value is thrown away and recomputed.
item.current_metrics: ~9-line inline conditional duplicating _clamp_row_limit's parse
item.proposal: Have `_clamp_row_limit` return both the clamped limit and a `user_bound: bool` flag (or a small dataclass), or add a `_parse_user_row_limit(user_limit) -> int|None` used by both. The suppression test becomes `if ram_warning and parsed_user_limit is not None and row_limit == parsed_user_limit`. Removes the triple-isinstance re-derivation.
item.behavior_preservation: The clamping arithmetic and the suppression condition evaluate to the same result for every input (including None/0/negative/non-numeric), so the warning is cleared in exactly the same cases; also fixes the bool edge if the parser rejects bool (see BUG-2).
item.est_reduction: ~6 LOC; cx -2

verdict.evidence:
The complexity IS incidental: the suppression predicate at _train_service.py:463-468 (`ram_warning and user_limit and isinstance(user_limit,(int,float)) and int(user_limit)>0 and row_limit==int(user_limit)`) mechanically re-parses user_limit exactly as _clamp_row_limit (167-176) did one line earlier at :459. Extracting `_parse_user_row_limit(user_limit)->int|None` and writing `if ram_warning and parsed is not None and row_limit==parsed` is a legitimate dedup.

Pure-dedup behavior trace (parser mirroring current parse, i.e. ACCEPTS bool since bool is an int subclass) — all cases evaluate identically: None/0 -> user_limit falsy -> parsed=None -> no suppress (matches); negative -> int<=0 -> parsed=None (matches; cf test_negative_user_limit at test_modelling_routes.py:899); non-numeric "abc" -> isinstance False -> parsed=None (matches test:911); 500.7 -> int=500 -> suppress iff row_limit==500 (matches test:914); valid int identical; row_limit is None with parsed set -> `None==parsed` is False, matching the explicit `row_limit is not None` guard. So the _train_service.py suppression refactor is provably behavior-preserving IF the parser accepts bool.

HOWEVER the proposal's own behavior_preservation field is self-contradictory: it claims identical results for "every input (including None/0/negative/non-numeric)" AND "fixes the bool edge if the parser rejects bool (see BUG-2)." These cannot both be true. If the parser REJECTS bool and _clamp_row_limit is refactored onto it, then `_clamp_row_limit(1000, True)` changes from 1 -> 1000 — a real, UNTESTED clamp behavior change (no bool test exists for _clamp_row_limit; Grep found none locking True/False). That is exactly the silent change the audit guards against. If the parser ACCEPTS bool, the refactor is clean but there is no bool fix to deliver. So one of the two stated properties is false; the bool fix must NOT be smuggled into a 'simplification'.

Scope gap: the predicate is TRIPLICATED, not single — identical at _train_service.py:463-468 AND modelling.py:181-186 (only row_limit/safe_limit names differ; both verified textually), plus the parse inside _clamp_row_limit used at BOTH _train_service.py:459 and modelling.py:176. The cited est_reduction ~6 LOC counts one site only; a correct dedup adopting the helper at both suppression sites removes ~10-12 LOC across two files, and any bool-semantics change in the shared helper now affects both clamp call sites — wider blast radius than 'risk: low' implies.
verdict.est_reduction: ~10-12 LOC across two files (not ~6) if both suppression sites (_train_service.py + modelling.py) adopt the shared helper; cx -2 per site. cosmetic dedup, no runtime gain.
verdict.repro_path: Trace _clamp_row_limit (src/haute/routes/_train_service.py:167-176) then the suppression at :458-471; compare to the identical suppression at src/haute/routes/modelling.py:178-189 and its clamp call at :176. Bool edge: in a REPL, isinstance(True,(int,float)) is True and int(True)==1, so current _clamp_row_limit(1000, True) returns 1; a bool-rejecting parser would return 1000 with no test catching it (tests/test_modelling_routes.py TestClampRowLimit:890-919 has no bool case).
verdict.recommended_action: Accept ONLY as a pure dedup that PRESERVES current parse semantics (parser accepts bool), and apply it to BOTH suppression sites (_train_service.py:463-468 and modelling.py:181-186) so the duplication is actually removed rather than half-removed. Do NOT bundle the 'fix the bool edge' change — the proposal's full-behavior-preservation claim is false the moment the parser rejects bool. If bool rejection is desired, do it separately under BUG-2 with a failing test first that locks _clamp_row_limit(1000, True) and the end-to-end warning behavior, per the repo's TDD-bugfix rule. As written (dedup + smuggled bool fix + single-site scope), it is marginal, not sound.

item.what_it_does: Maps watch events to discovered/known pipeline files keyed by resolved absolute path.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL: three places independently build `{str(path.resolve()): path}` dicts and the `key = str(p.resolve())` idiom recurs ~6 times in _flush. The resolved-path string is the de-facto identity but isn't named.
item.current_metrics: ~6 inline `str(p.resolve())` recomputations + 2 dict-builders of the same shape
item.proposal: Introduce `_resolved_key(p: Path) -> str` and `_by_resolved_path(paths) -> dict[str,Path]` and use them in _discovered_pipeline_paths, _known_pipeline_paths, and the _flush loops. Centralises the 'resolved path is identity' rule.
item.behavior_preservation: Identical string keys and dict contents; only the construction is named once. No change to which files are selected/broadcast.
item.est_reduction: ~8 LOC; readability

verdict.evidence:
Complexity is genuinely INCIDENTAL (pure recomputation of a string key), so not unsound. Split the proposal into its two helpers:

PART 1 `_resolved_key(p)=str(p.resolve())` — SOUND & behavior-preserving. Every cited inline site is literally str(<x>.resolve()): L154, L565, L600, L629, L661 use str(p.resolve())/str(path.resolve()); L605/L610/L616 use str(pipeline_path.resolve()). _resolved_key is pure (no hidden state); substitution yields byte-identical keys and raises identically. The except-path reconstruction at L661 (fp_key=str(p.resolve())) and self-write key at L565 are preserved. Clear win; names the de-facto identity rule.

PART 2 `_by_resolved_path(paths)={str(p.resolve()):p}` — only PARTIALLY applies; the proposal's claim of 'two dict-builders of the same shape' (really three lines L154/L160/L161) is overstated:
- L160 {str(path.resolve()):path for path in _ensure_pipeline_index().values()} — matches exactly. OK.
- L150-154 builds the dict ONLY after a continue-filter (suffix!='.py' or name.startswith('__')). A bare _by_resolved_path(discover_pipelines()) would INCLUDE filtered files = behavior change. Preservable only as _by_resolved_path(p for p in discover_pipelines() if p.suffix=='.py' and not p.name.startswith('__')) — filter MUST be retained, so it is not the 'same shape'.
- L161 paths.update({key: Path(key) for key in _last_broadcast_fp}) is NOT _by_resolved_path shape: value is Path(key) and key is an ALREADY-resolved string (no .resolve() re-applied). Rewriting as _by_resolved_path([Path(k) for k in _last_broadcast_fp]) would RE-call .resolve() on each reconstructed Path — a change in construction intent (idempotent for existing files, but not the same operation). L161 must be left untouched.

L605/L610/L616 are NOT {key:path} builders (values are tuples), so only Part 1 applies there — correctly scoped by the proposal. Tests (tests/test_server.py:1364) assert exact {str(pipeline.resolve()): pipeline} and still pass under both helpers. Net: Part 1 fully sound; Part 2 saves ~2 LOC over 1.5 of the 3 claimed builders and L161 is intentionally excluded, so real reduction is smaller than '~8 LOC'.
verdict.est_reduction: ~5 LOC realistic (Part 1: ~6-7 inline call-sites named once; Part 2: ~2 LOC across L154/L160 only). Proposal's ~8 LOC is optimistic because L161 cannot be folded into _by_resolved_path and L154 must keep its filter.
verdict.repro_path: Trace src/haute/server.py:148-162 (builders) and 560-662 (_flush key recomputations); cross-check _last_broadcast_fp population at L637 (keys are str(p.resolve())) which makes L161 a re-key, not a resolve; tests/test_server.py:1349-1364 pins exact dict shape.
verdict.recommended_action: Adopt _resolved_key(p)->str as proposed across L154,L565,L600,L605,L610,L616,L629,L661 (provably identical). Apply _by_resolved_path ONLY to L160, and optionally L154 while RETAINING the .py/dunder filter. Explicitly EXCLUDE L161 ({key: Path(key)} over _last_broadcast_fp is an intentional re-key of already-resolved strings, not a resolve-builder — folding it in would re-resolve and is not 'same shape'). Reword the proposal to '1.5 builders + ~7 inline recomputations' rather than 'three builders of the same shape'.

item.title: preview_node node_statuses comprehension drops the `nid in node_map` guard its 4 sibling comprehensions enforce
item.failure_scenario: node_statuses = {nid: r.status for nid, r in results.items() if nid in relevant} omits the `nid in node_map` clause present in all five sibling comprehensions. Today it is masked because `relevant = ancestors(body.node_id, pruned, set(node_map.keys()))` can only contain ids already in node_map, so node_statuses keys are a subset of node_map. But the invariant is unstated and fragile: if `relevant` is ever seeded from a wider set (e.g. the `else: relevant = set(results.keys())` branch at line 586 when node_id is falsy, where results may include synthetic/aggregate ids not in node_map), node_statuses would expose ids the other maps suppress, producing a PreviewNodeResponse whose node_statuses keys disagree with node_columns/timings. Pure consistency hazard, not currently reachable with a non-empty node_id.

verdict.evidence: CODE CLAIM IS ACCURATE: src/haute/routes/pipeline.py:608 `node_statuses = {nid: r.status for nid, r in results.items() if nid in relevant}` omits the `nid in node_map` clause that all 5 siblings (lines 595/605/610/615/620) carry. BUT THE DEFECT IS UNREACHABLE, proven by two code-traced invariants: (1) DECISIVE executor result-key contract — in src/haute/executor.py execute_graph(), `results` is built only by `for nid in result_order:` (line 1165) and the body unconditionally indexes node_map[nid] at lines 1110, 1148, 1206; result_order is bounded by graph topo `order` and ancestors(target, edges, set(node_map)) (lines 788-802, 1082-1098). item.title: JSON row_limit:true (bool) is accepted as a numeric limit and downsamples training to 1 row
item.failure_scenario: config['row_limit'] comes from user JSON. _clamp_row_limit does `if user_limit and isinstance(user_limit,(int,float))`. In Python `isinstance(True,int)` is True and `int(True)==1`, so a config with `row_limit: true` yields clamped=1 -> row_limit=min(current,1)=1 -> _seeded_training_sample(lf, 1) trains the model on a single random row, silently, with no validation error. `row_limit: false` is falsy and harmless, but `true` (or any bool reaching this path) corrupts the training set. The shared script-export path (build_train_params) would not reproduce this, so live vs exported training could differ.

verdict.evidence: Executed review/03-simplification/repro/routes__BUG-2.py against the REAL production functions haute.routes._train_service._clamp_row_limit and _seeded_training_sample (exit 0, all asserts held). Output: "_clamp_row_limit(None, True) = 1 (type=int)"; "rows the model is trained on = 1 (source had 100)"; control "_clamp_row_limit(None, False) = None; rows trained = 100". Root cause exactly as claimed: _train_service.py:172 `if user_limit and isinstance(user_limit,(int,float))` -> isinstance(True,int) is True and int(True)==1, so clamped=1; consumed at :888 `if row_limit:` (True/1 is truthy) -> _seeded_training_sample(lf,1). No guard rejects it: _validate_config (:644) checks only target/algorithm/GLM family-link; validate_v2_schema (_api_input_schema.py) is NEVER called on the training config and contains no row_limit rule; config['row_limit'] is free-form node.data.config. The suppression block (:463-468) reuses the identical isinstance test (int(True)==1==row_limit) so the RAM downsample warning is also suppressed, making it quieter. Export-divergence sub-claim holds: build_train_params (src/haute/modelling/_train_config.py) has ZERO row_limit references, so exported scripts won't reproduce 1-row training. Note: row_limit:false is falsy -> _clamp returns the original limit AND the `if row_limit:` guard never fires (harmless), confirming only bool True is harmful.
verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\routes__BUG-2.py
verdict.recommended_action: Tighten _clamp_row_limit (and the mirrored suppression test at :463-468) to exclude bool, e.g. `isinstance(user_limit, int) and not isinstance(user_limit, bool)` (drop float too, or coerce explicitly). Per the project's fail-loud guidance, prefer raising a 400/ValueError when row_limit is present but not a positive int rather than silently coercing. Best: validate config['row_limit'] in _validate_config (the fast upfront path) so a malformed value is rejected before any job starts. Add a failing-first regression test asserting that config={'row_limit': True} either raises or leaves the row count unchanged (NOT 1), plus a test that the live route and build_train_params/script-export agree on the applied limit.

item.title: _friendly_error classifies any non-CatBoost exception whose message mentions 'catboost' as a CatBoost error, and File/OSError ordering can mislabel
item.failure_scenario: The branch `if 'CatBoost' in exc_type or 'catboost' in msg.lower()` fires on substring of the message, not just the exception type. A FileNotFoundError or generic RuntimeError whose message merely references a catboost artifact path (e.g. "could not open /models/catboost_model.cbm") is reported to the user as a 'CatBoost error: ...' rather than 'File not found: ...', sending the user to fix the wrong thing. FileNotFoundError is handled earlier (304) so that specific case is safe, but any OSError subclass raised after a catboost-pathed message, or a wrapped third-party error mentioning catboost, is mis-narrated. Display-only (the job still fails), but the actionable message is wrong.

(correct), proving the mislabel is driven by the message substring, not the type. Claim's stated-safe case verified: FileNotFoundError is caught at line 304 -> "File not found: ..." (safe). Note FileNotFoundError and PermissionError are both OSError subclasses, but only FileNotFoundError is handled before line 308. So a single closure keyed on `_st` (load_mlflow if _st in (run,registered) else load_optimiser_artifact(remapped)) with the shared tail IS behaviour-preserving — but ONLY if the two firing GATES are retained: MLflow fires for ANY _st in (run,registered); file fires ONLY when _st=='file' and remap present and _remap_artifact hit, otherwise the branch returns None to fall through to the base builder (which loads the ORIGINAL artifact_path and runs ConfigError validation). Those gates are essential, not incidental; a flat single closure that always fires would break the file remap-miss / no-remap fall-through. Real saving is ~20-30 LOC, not the claimed 40-55.

The proposal's PREFERRED 'Better still' variant is UNSOUND on two traced cases:
(1) Bundle-remap cannot be expressed via _resolve_runtime_graph_paths. That resolver only rewrites the config key 'path' for _RUNTIME_PATH_NODE_TYPES and resolves relative paths against graph.source_file; optimiserApply is keyed on 'artifact_path' and the remap is content-addressed (_remap_artifact builds f"{node_id}__{Path(raw_path).name}" and looks it up in the artifact_paths bundle dict). Test test_ratebook_apply_file_remap_* (tests/test_deploy_internals.py:1687-1737) passes artifact_paths={"opt__ratebook.json": ...} with config path "artifacts/ratebook.json" and NO source_file — the source-file-relative rewrite would never find the bundled artifact, breaking the test.
(2) Dropping the MLflow override changes guard semantics. Deploy override fires MLflow on bare _st in (run,registered); base builder's _has_mlflow ADDITIONALLY requires run_id (run) or registered_model (registered) and returns _passthrough_fn otherwise. A misconfigured run/registered node currently routes to load_mlflow_optimiser_artifact and fails loudly inside resolve_mlflow_source; under the base builder it becomes a SILENT passthrough — a regression that directly violates the repo's 'fail loudly, no incorrect-and-hard-to-notice fallback' rule (CLAUDE.md). The MLflow case is NOT a no-op to drop.

Therefore: real but small incidental dedup exists (core single-closure merge); the headline 'better' proposal would change behaviour. Marginal.
verdict.est_reduction: ~20-30 LOC (core single-closure merge keyed on _st, retaining both firing gates); NOT the claimed 40-55. cx of _intercept down ~3-4, not 6-8. The 'Better still' variant nets near-zero after adding the new artifact_path remap plumbing it would require.
verdict.repro_path: tests/test_deploy_internals.py::test_ratebook_apply_file_remap_routes_through_configured_input (and siblings :1739-1752) pin file-remap resolution via artifact_paths bundle dict; test_optimiser_apply_mlflow_source (:1754) pins MLflow runtime download. Trace gates at _scorer.py:531 (file: _st=='file' and remap and remap-hit) and :562 (MLflow: _st in (run,registered)) vs base _has_mlflow guard at _builders.py:992-994.
verdict.recommended_action: Adopt ONLY the conservative core merge: replace the two parallel closures with one closure whose body is `artifact = load_mlflow_optimiser_artifact(...) if _st in ('run','registered') else load_optimiser_artifact(_path)` followed by the shared _select_optimiser_apply_input + _dispatch_apply, while KEEPING the two outer gates exactly (file branch still computes the remapped path and returns None on remap-miss/no-remap to fall through; MLflow branch still fires on bare _st in (run,registered)). REJECT the 'Better still' variant: do NOT route file-remap through _resolve_runtime_graph_paths (wrong resolution mechanism, breaks bundle remap test) and do NOT drop the MLflow override (converts a loud misconfig failure into a silent passthrough, violating the fail-loudly rule). Gate any change behind running the test_optimiser_apply_* / test_ratebook_apply_* suite.

item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. One 265-line nested function is an if-ladder over six node types (apiInput, externalFile, optimiserApply, modelScore, dataSource), each defining 1-3 inner closures with long default-argument capture lists. It closes over ~8 enclosing-scope names (input_set, input_lf, remap, node_by_id, parents_of, execution_context, model_score_temp_paths, retained_lazy_frames), which is why it is inlined; but the per-node logic is otherwise independent and individually testable.
item.current_metrics: 265L, cx27, nesting 3; ~10 inner closures
item.proposal: Extract one module-level builder per node type — `_intercept_api_input(node, input_set, input_lf)`, `_intercept_external_file(node, remap)`, `_intercept_optimiser_apply(node, remap)`, `_intercept_model_score(node, remap, ctx...)`, `_intercept_static_data_source(node, remap, input_set, execution_context)` — each returning `NodeFnResult | None` and taking the handful of dependencies as explicit params (pass a small frozen `_DeployInterceptContext` dataclass to avoid long arg lists). `_intercept` becomes a short dispatch that tries each in turn and returns the first non-None. This mirrors the registry pattern the executor already uses (_builders._register).
item.behavior_preservation: Pure code-move: the first-match-wins ordering of the branches is preserved by calling the helpers in the same order; closures keep capturing the same values now passed as parameters. No branch condition changes, so the same override (or fall-through None) is produced for every node.
item.est_reduction: _intercept body to ~25 lines; cx27 -> ~8 (rest distributed, each helper cx <=6)

verdict.evidence:
Re-read _intercept in full (src/haute/deploy/_scorer.py:469-733) plus the NodeBuildHooks/wrap_builder contract (_node_builder.py:38-63) and NodeType enum (_types.py:25-50).

COMPLEXITY IS INCIDENTAL (mechanically removable). The body is six top-level `if node_type == X` blocks. The six intercepted types (apiInput/externalFile/optimiserApply/modelScore/dataSource) are DISTINCT StrEnum members with distinct string values, so they are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE: for any single node at most one top-level block's `node_type` guard can be true. Therefore:
- There is NO cross-branch fall-through. When a node matches block A's type but fails its inner guard (e.g. API_INPUT node with nid not in input_set; externalFile with no remap or remapped_path None; optimiserApply with non-file/non-run/registered sourceType; modelScore with neither remapped_path nor bundled_contract_path; dataSource in input_set or no remap), no later `if node_type == B` (B != A) can fire, so control necessarily reaches `return None`. Splitting into per-type helpers called in dispatch order, returning the first non-None, is exactly equivalent. The proposal's emphasis on "first-match-wins ordering" is actually a non-issue here (mutual exclusivity makes ordering irrelevant) — the proposal is more robust than it claims.

BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING (build-time side-effect surface verified). Grepped model_score_temp_paths / retained_lazy_frames across the file: inside _intercept (469-733) there are ZERO mutations of shared mutable state. model_score_temp_paths is only passed by reference into model_score_fn's closure (line 667) and appended at SCORE time inside _run_score_pipeline, never at build time; retained_lazy_frames is captured nowhere in _intercept (appended only at line 826, outside the closures). Every branch's eager work (_remap_artifact lookups, _declared_categorical_levels_for_model_score, projection.model_score_required_output_columns, _bundled_contract_path) is pure computation feeding closure default-args. Hence the per-node helpers — each early-returning None when node_type does not match so the other helpers' eager work never runs for a non-matching node — produce byte-identical NodeFnResult (func_name, callable, is_source) or None for every node. Defensive snapshots (MappingProxyType(dict(config)), list(source_names), list(source_ids)) are preserved by a pure code-move. Null/empty/error paths preserved: external_passthrough (dfs empty -> pl.LazyFrame()), model_score_missing_artifact's RuntimeError raise, contract-mismatch raises in _assert_runtime_contract_matches — all live inside the moved closures, unchanged.

CONSISTENCY: the dispatch-by-node-type pattern already exists in _builders._register (@_register(NodeType.X, ...), confirmed _builders.py:314/464/512), so the extraction matches an established codebase convention as the proposal claims.

CAVEAT (implementation, not soundness): two branches read build_kwargs — modelScore (line 628 build_kwargs.get("required_output_columns")) and dataSource (line 714). The proposal's listed signature for the dataSource helper, `_intercept_static_data_source(node, remap, input_set, execution_context)`, OMITS required_output_columns/build_kwargs. A faithful implementation MUST still forward it (via the _DeployInterceptContext or an explicit param), otherwise source_scan_projection pushdown for static data sources is silently disabled — a real regression. This is description-level imprecision, easily fixed, and is exactly the kind of subtlety a careful dev/reviewer pair must catch.
verdict.est_reduction: _intercept body ~265L -> ~25L dispatch; cx27 -> ~8, each helper cx <=6 (matches proposal). Net file size roughly unchanged (logic redistributed to 5 module-level helpers + a small frozen context dataclass).
verdict.repro_path: N/A (read-only audit). To validate the move: each helper must (a) guard on its node_type first and return None immediately otherwise, and (b) receive the same captured deps including build_kwargs/required_output_columns for the modelScore and dataSource helpers. Existing deploy-scoring tests (apiInput injection, externalFile remap+code/passthrough, optimiserApply file+mlflow, modelScore remapped/contract-only-missing-artifact, static dataSource projection) should pass unchanged and would catch any dropped capture.
verdict.recommended_action: PROCEED with the extraction. It is a provably behavior-preserving pure code-move (mutually-exclusive type guards, no cross-branch fall-through, no build-time shared-state mutation) that mirrors the existing _builders._register convention. REQUIRE in review: (1) each helper early-returns None for non-matching node_type; (2) the dataSource and modelScore helpers still receive build_kwargs/required_output_columns (the proposal's dataSource signature omits it); (3) defensive snapshots MappingProxyType(dict(config)) / list(source_names) / list(source_ids) preserved verbatim; (4) func_name still threaded into every returned tuple.
