item.what_it_does: Re-reads a static dataSource from its remapped bundled path, applying the same projection pushdown as normal execution.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The deploy `static_source` closure is a near-verbatim copy of the base builder's `plain_source_fn`: both call `projection.source_scan_projection(config, required)` then `read_data_source({**config,'path':...}, profile=..., columns=..., validate_columns=...)`. The ONLY difference is that the path is the remapped local path. The base builder already reads `config['path']`, so the override exists solely to substitute the path.
item.current_metrics: ~25-line closure duplicating a 14-line base closure
item.proposal: Instead of reimplementing the read, rewrite the dataSource node's `config['path']` to the remapped value during the existing pre-pass (`_resolve_runtime_graph_paths` / a new `_attach_remapped_source_paths`) and return None from the interceptor so the base `_build_data_source` builder runs unchanged. This removes the duplicated projection+read body entirely and keeps a single source-of-truth for source reading.
item.behavior_preservation: read_data_source and source_scan_projection are the same functions; feeding them the same config with only `path` swapped yields identical frames. The base builder's extra `_allow_empty_source_path` guard is a strict superset of the interceptor (which never hits empty paths because remap implies a concrete path), so behaviour for the remapped case is identical.
item.est_reduction: ~20 LOC

verdict.evidence:
Re-read both sites in full plus the supporting machinery (projection.source_scan_projection @projection.py:420; _builders._source_scan_projection @_builders.py:61-68; _allow_empty_source_path @_builders.py:71-72; _remap_artifact @_scorer.py:270-287; _resolve_runtime_graph_paths @_scorer.py:212-236; bundler @_bundler.py:113-124; deploy validator @_validators.py:264-273; hook semantics @_node_builder.py:38-63, confirmed by tests/test_coverage_gaps.py:275-293 that returning None falls through to base).

The duplication IS incidental for the common path, and the pre-pass+return-None mechanism is mechanically valid. But the proposal's behavior-preservation claim is INCOMPLETE and the change is NOT strictly behaviour-preserving. The interceptor at _scorer.py:707 fires for ANY DATA_SOURCE with a remapped path, with NO check on config['code'] or sourceType, whereas base _build_data_source (_builders.py:512-601) has THREE distinct paths: plain_source_fn (no code), _databricks_source, and source_fn+source_with_code (code present, runs _exec_user_code @_builders.py:597-599). Trace by case:

CASE A (static source, no code): current interceptor = projection.source_scan_projection(config, required) + read_data_source({**config,'path':remapped}, profile, cols, validate). Proposed base plain_source_fn: empty-path guard is False (deploy profile is DEPLOY_LIVE/DEPLOY_BATCH per _scorer.py:143-147, never None/PREVIEW_EAGER, and remap implies concrete path); _source_scan_projection falls through to projection.source_scan_projection(config, columns) for non-preview profiles; read_data_source with config['path'] pre-rewritten. IDENTICAL. Behaviour-preserving here.

CASE B (databricks): rejected by deploy validator (_validators.py:266-273) and carries no 'path' so never remapped — interceptor never fires today, base never reached. No change.

CASE C (static source WITH non-empty path AND user code): REACHABLE — no validator rejects code on a static dataSource, and the bundler bundles its file unconditionally on non-empty path (_bundler.py:113-124, no code filter). Current interceptor reads the file and DROPS the user code (no _exec_user_code) — a latent bug, inconsistent with the executor and with the sibling externalFile interceptor which DOES run code (_scorer.py:498-513). Proposed (return None -> base source_with_code) WOULD run the code. This is a real OUTPUT DIFFERENCE between current and proposed. The proposal would silently fix this bug, which is desirable, but per audit rules a simplification that changes any observable behaviour (even a buggy edge case) is not "provably behaviour-preserving"; it must be landed test-first (CLAUDE.md mandates a failing test before a bugfix). The proposal text omits CASE C entirely and asserts the interceptor is a near-verbatim copy of plain_source_fn, which is false. No existing test covers a code-bearing static dataSource in deploy.

Net: incidental complexity confirmed and the architectural direction (single source-of-truth path rewrite via a new _attach_remapped_source_paths pre-pass keyed by node_id__basename, available from the remap dict) is correct, but the change alters behaviour for code-bearing static sources and the stated preservation argument is wrong, so it is not a clean drop-in simplification.
verdict.est_reduction: ~20 LOC removed from _scorer.py (the static_source closure), offset by a small new pre-pass; net ~12-18 LOC
verdict.repro_path: Deploy a pipeline containing a non-input static dataSource node with a non-empty 'path' AND non-empty 'code' (e.g. code that renames/filters a column). Bundle + score: current interceptor returns the raw file frame WITHOUT applying the user code; after the proposal the code would run. No test exercises this today (grep for code+DATA_SOURCE in deploy tests: none).
verdict.recommended_action: Do NOT land as a pure "simplification". Treat as a behaviour-changing refactor: (1) first add a failing test for a code-bearing static dataSource in deploy proving the user code is currently dropped; (2) add a _attach_remapped_source_paths pre-pass (or extend _resolve_runtime_graph_paths) that rewrites config['path'] to the remapped value for DATA_SOURCE nodes (key {node_id}__{Path(path).name} via the existing remap dict), and make the interceptor return None for the dataSource branch so the base _build_data_source builder (including source_with_code / projection code_preserves_projection logic) runs unchanged; (3) confirm Case A regression tests (projection pushdown + path swap) still pass and databricks remains validator-rejected. This both removes the duplication and fixes the latent code-drop. If the team instead wants strictly no behaviour change, the proposal is unsound as written because it would alter Case C.

item.what_it_does: Walks backwards from the training node to determine the column COUNT at that node.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. `_resolve_target_columns` is an entire second BFS walker (deque, visited set, prune_live_switch_edges, build_parents_of) whose only output is an int column count. The richer `_resolve_target_columns_detail` already computes the actual column NAMES via the same backward walk (and is also called in estimate_safe_training_rows). The int-returning walker is a strictly weaker duplicate of the name-returning one.
item.current_metrics: _resolve_target_columns 48L cx ~9; _resolve_target_columns_detail 58L cx ~14 — overlapping walks
item.proposal: Delete `_resolve_target_columns` and define `n_columns = (lambda names: len(names) if names else None)(_resolve_target_column_names(graph, target, source))` at the single call site (estimate_safe_training_rows:882). `_resolve_target_column_names` already wraps `_resolve_target_columns_detail`.
item.behavior_preservation: Needs verification that the two walkers agree on count for every shape (selected_columns short-circuit, edgeJoin, source metadata). _detail returns names for exactly the same terminating conditions the int walker uses (`selected_columns` len, source metadata cols), plus it correctly expands edgeJoin outputs — so `len(names)` is at least as accurate. The one divergence to check: _resolve_target_columns returns the FIRST node's source col count on a plain source, while _detail dedupes columns; for a source node both equal the parquet column_count. Pin with a property test over existing graph fixtures before removing.
item.est_reduction: ~48 LOC, one whole function + its imports

verdict.evidence:
The premise "the int walker is a strictly weaker duplicate of the name walker" is false; the two walkers terminate on DIFFERENT nodes and the int result is load-bearing in two branches that the proposal would break.

Call site (src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:879-930): n_columns = _resolve_target_columns(...) [882] is used (A) as the guard `if not n_columns: return schema_unavailable` [884], and (B) in the ELSE branch [927-928] `n_columns = max(n_columns - len(excluded...), 1)` which runs ONLY when _resolve_target_columns_detail(...) returns None [912-913]. In the IF branch [913-926] the int value is discarded and n_columns is recomputed from the detail names. So the int walker matters precisely when the detail walker yields None.

DIVERGENCE 1 (silent-wrongness, pinned): non-string selected_columns. Int walker [511-513] does NOT type-check elements: `if sel and isinstance(sel,list) and len(sel)>0: return len(sel)` -> returns 2 for ["premium",1]. Detail walker uses _selected_column_names [606-612] which returns None for non-str entries, and [699] then ABORTS the whole walk returning None. Test test_invalid_selected_columns_are_rejected (tests/test_ram_estimate.py:1024-1029) pins detail->None here. Current code: n_columns=2, detail=None -> ELSE branch -> a real estimate. Proposal `len(_resolve_target_column_names(...))` -> None -> guard fires -> early-return schema_unavailable with probe_columns=0. A real RAM estimate silently becomes a no-op.

DIVERGENCE 2 (the ELSE branch goes dead): under the proposal n_columns is DERIVED from the detail names, so target_columns is None ⟺ n_columns is None ⟹ guard fires; the ELSE branch [927-928] becomes unreachable. Test at tests/test_ram_estimate.py:569-576 patches _resolve_target_columns->4 while _resolve_target_columns_detail->None and asserts probe_columns==2 and bytes_per_row==2*8*3.0 — i.e. it explicitly exercises this branch and treats the two functions as independent. The proposal eliminates the only path to that code and breaks the modeled production scenario (detail unresolvable but source/selected count still resolvable).

DIVERGENCE 3 (edgeJoin count, proposal self-admits): int walker has no edgeJoin handling, so it BFS-descends into both join parents and returns a single source's parquet column_count (e.g. base=3), whereas detail returns the joined width (e.g. 4). The proposal note concedes len(names) "correctly expands edgeJoin outputs" / is "at least as accurate" — i.e. it admits the counts differ. (Observable result for the happy edgeJoin path is unchanged only because the int value is discarded in the IF branch, but Divergences 1-2 still break.)

The guard-equivalence point the proposal would need (None/0 handling) is preserved by the lambda, but that does not rescue Divergences 1-2. Net: the change is NOT behaviour-preserving; it turns valid estimates into schema_unavailable no-ops in at least two cases that existing tests pin. The "property test over fixtures before removing" the proposal itself flags as a prerequisite would fail. The duplication is real but the second walker encodes a deliberately weaker (count-only, edgeJoin-agnostic, type-lax) terminating policy that is intentionally distinct — essential, not incidental.
verdict.est_reduction: ~48 LOC if it were sound; not realizable without changing behaviour (would also require deleting/rewriting the 3 tests at tests/test_ram_estimate.py:569-576, 1024-1029, 2294-2313 and the TestResolveTargetColumns class at 2144-2229).
verdict.recommended_action: REJECT as written. If de-duplication is still desired, it must be a behaviour-changing refactor done deliberately, not a "simplification": (1) decide the intended semantics for non-string selected_columns (currently int=count, detail=reject) and for edgeJoin counts, (2) collapse the ELSE branch into the detail path so n_columns always derives from names, (3) update/replace the pinned tests at 569-576, 1024-1029, 2294-2313 and TestResolveTargetColumns. Absent that, keep _resolve_target_columns; at most add a comment documenting that it is an intentionally weaker count-only fallback feeding the ELSE branch, not dead duplication.
verdict.repro_path: Graph with target modelling node config {"selected_columns": ["premium", 1]} over a known source: current estimate_safe_training_rows yields probe_columns>0 / non-zero bytes_per_row; proposed form yields schema_unavailable (probe_columns=0, bytes_per_row=0). item.what_it_does: Counts physical lines in a file (CSV minus a header line; JSONL as-is).
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The two functions are byte-for-byte identical except `_csv_row_count` returns `max(count-1, 0)`. The shared line-counting loop is duplicated.
item.current_metrics: 2x ~6-line functions
item.proposal: Extract `_count_lines(path) -> int` and define `_csv_row_count = lambda p: max(_count_lines(p) - 1, 0)` and `_jsonl_row_count = _count_lines` (or inline `_count_lines(path) - has_header`).
item.behavior_preservation: Identical iteration over the same binary file handle; only the post-decrement differs and is preserved.
item.est_reduction: ~6 LOC

verdict.evidence:
Re-read src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:329-342. The two functions are byte-for-byte identical except `_csv_row_count` returns `max(count-1, 0)` vs `_jsonl_row_count` returns `count`. The shared loop (open(path,"rb"); for _ in f: count+=1) is genuinely INCIDENTAL duplication, safely extractable as `_count_lines(path)->int`.

Behavior-preservation, every case traced and confirmed identical:
- Binary-mode iteration: both use "rb", so line splitting is on \n (0x0A) only; extracting the loop keeps the same handle/mode/iteration -> same count for any bytes.
- CSV header-only ("a,b,c\n"): 1 line -> max(1-1,0)=0 (test_header_only).
- CSV empty (b""): 0 lines -> max(0-1,0)=max(-1,0)=0. The max(...,0) clamp is the load-bearing edge case and is preserved verbatim by the proposal (test_empty_file, line 1395).
- CSV single data row ("a,b\n1,2\n"): 2 -> max(2-1,0)=1 (test_single_data_row).
- CSV N+1 lines -> 123 (test line 205) preserved.
- JSONL: `_jsonl_row_count = _count_lines` returns the raw count: multiple=3, empty=0, single=1 (TestJsonlRowCount lines 1409-1423) all preserved.
- No-trailing-newline files iterate identically (same loop), unchanged.
- Error paths: neither function has an internal try/except; both callers (lines 261, 278) wrap in the outer try/except Exception (lines 253/280). open() raising FileNotFoundError/OSError propagates identically whether inline or inside _count_lines -> no swallowing, no change.
- Import sites (tests lines 18/24) need callables; both a module-level lambda and the `= _count_lines` alias remain importable callables, so existing tests still resolve and pass.

All edge cases are pinned by existing tests (TestCsvRowCountEdgeCases, TestJsonlRowCount), so any accidental regression would fail CI. Minor stylistic caveat: prefer a named `def _csv_row_count(p): return max(_count_lines(p)-1, 0)` over a bare lambda for greppability/tracebacks; the `_jsonl_row_count = _count_lines` alias is fine.
verdict.est_reduction: ~6 LOC
verdict.recommended_action: Apply. Extract `_count_lines(path: str) -> int` containing the open("rb")/iterate/count loop. Define `_jsonl_row_count = _count_lines` and a named `def _csv_row_count(path): return max(_count_lines(path) - 1, 0)` (prefer def over lambda for traceback/greppability). Existing tests (TestCsvRowCountEdgeCases, TestJsonlRowCount, line 205) fully pin behavior including the empty-file max(...,0) clamp; run test_ram_estimate.py to confirm green.
verdict.repro_path: n/a

verdict.evidence:

INCIDENTAL complexity confirmed: both encode the same dispatch ladder (apiInput: json/jsonl special-case else parquet; dataSource: skip databricks else parquet[/csv]) with the same path-exists guards and the same try/except→log→None wrapper. Verified against TestCountSourceRowsForNode and TestSourceMetadataForNode (129 tests in file) — every leg is covered and would still pass.

TWO CAVEATS make it not behavior-neutral / not clearly worthwhile:
(1) OBSERVABILITY REGRESSION: on a parquet read that raises (corrupt file; or test_exception_returns_none line 1893 mocking Path.exists→RuntimeError), the current row-counter catches it and logs structured event "source_row_count_failed" (line 281). Under delegation the exception is caught INSIDE _detailed_source_metadata_for_node and logged as "source_metadata_failed" (line 323); the caller's own except never fires for parquet errors. The None return is preserved (no test asserts the event name — grep shows both event strings appear ONLY at their definition sites), but the emitted log-event name changes for that path. Given CLAUDE.md's "fail loudly so we can fix errors", silently renaming the diagnostic event is a minor regression, not a value-neutral refactor.
(2) FIDDLY CONTROL FLOW: the "keep only csv/jsonl legs, delegate parquet" framing requires interleaving — the apiInput .jsonl leg lives inside the json/jsonl block and must run before any fallback; the dataSource .csv leg only fires when path exists AND not .parquet. Delegating the whole node to _detailed_source_metadata_for_node(node).row_count preserves the apiInput no-extension-guard asymmetry correctly, but the unique-leg interleaving means the result is not dramatically simpler. A naive "drop everything non-csv/jsonl" implementation would risk dropping the apiInput exists→parquet (no ext guard) leg.

No case DROPS a return value, so it is not outright unsound; but the log-event rename is a behavioral delta and the readability win is modest for two short, fully-tested functions.
verdict.est_reduction: ~15-20 LOC, cx -6 across the pair (as proposed; plausible)
verdict.repro_path: Trace _count_source_rows_for_node vs _detailed_source_metadata_for_node for: apiInput corrupt/erroring .parquet (log event changes source_row_count_failed→source_metadata_failed); apiInput existing no-extension path (must still read as parquet — preserved only if delegating whole node, not if filtering to csv/jsonl only).
verdict.recommended_action: Accept only if implemented as full-node delegation: caller runs the two UNIQUE legs first (apiInput .jsonl+exists → _jsonl_row_count; dataSource .csv+exists → _csv_row_count) then returns _detailed_source_metadata_for_node(node).row_count for everything else (this preserves the apiInput no-extension-guard parquet leg). To keep behavior fully neutral, ALSO preserve the observability contract — either keep both log events distinct by catching the delegate's None-vs-raise separately, or consciously accept/standardize on the single "source_metadata_failed" event and note it. If observability fidelity matters, prefer the table-driven {NodeType: handler} variant that lets the row-only caller and metadata caller share one ladder while each keeps its own except/log wrapper. Given two short, exhaustively-tested functions and a small payoff, this is low-priority; defer unless batching with other _ram_estimate dedup.

item.what_it_does: Returns available RAM bytes by trying /proc/meminfo, then sysconf, then Windows GlobalMemoryStatusEx, else a 4 GiB fallback.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The function threads SIX mutable locals (proc_meminfo_error, sysconf_error, sysconf_pages, sysconf_page_size, windows_attempted, windows_error) across three try-blocks purely so one warning log at the end can name which probes failed. The happy path returns early from each block, so the error bookkeeping is dead on success and dominates the line count.
item.current_metrics: 76L, multiple try/except with shared error state
item.proposal: Extract three small probe helpers, each returning `int | None` (and logging its own debug-level failure reason): `_ram_from_proc_meminfo()`, `_ram_from_sysconf()`, `_ram_from_windows()`. Body becomes `for probe in (...): v = probe(); if v: return v` then a single fallback warning. The per-probe failure detail moves into the probe (or a returned reason tuple), removing the six-variable accumulator.
item.behavior_preservation: Same probe order, same early-return semantics, same 4 GiB fallback value and warning emission. Only the plumbing of diagnostic strings changes (still logged, just sourced per-probe). No change to returned bytes for any platform.
item.est_reduction: ~25 LOC; nesting/locals materially reduced

verdict.evidence:
Re-read src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:51-126 in full and traced every path. The six locals (proc_meminfo_error, sysconf_error, sysconf_pages, sysconf_page_size, windows_attempted, windows_error) are NOT pure scaffolding for a free-form message — they are a TESTED structured contract on the single final `logger.warning("available_ram_fallback_4gib", ...)` event. Two tests lock this in:

(1) tests/test_ram_estimate.py:165-184 test_ultimate_fallback_logs_structured_warning asserts the ONE fallback warning event carries fields proc_meminfo_error ("proc unavailable"), sysconf_error ("no sysconf"), windows_attempted is False, plus fallback_bytes and platform.
(2) tests/test_ram_estimate.py:1721-1750 test_windows_ctypes_exception_falls_to_default asserts the same warning event carries windows_attempted is True and windows_error ("ctypes unavailable").
capture_logs (structlog.testing, imported at line 11) captures all levels and the tests filter for event=="available_ram_fallback_4gib".

CASE TRACE vs proposal:
- Happy paths (proc MemAvailable found -> *1024; sysconf>0 -> pages*page_size; win32 GlobalMemoryStatusEx true -> ullAvailPhys): all early-return before any bookkeeping is read. The proposed `for probe: v=probe(); if v: return v` preserves order and these returns. OK. (Covered: lines 1650-1679, 128-155.)
- Fallback path: the proposal AS LITERALLY WRITTEN says each probe logs "its own debug-level failure reason" and the body emits "a single fallback warning". That moves the per-probe reasons OFF the final warning event into separate debug logs, so fallback_logs[0]["proc_meminfo_error"], ["sysconf_error"], ["windows_attempted"], ["windows_error"] would KeyError/fail. This BREAKS both tests above -> NOT behaviour-preserving as described.
- The proposal's alternative ("or a returned reason tuple") CAN preserve behaviour, but then it does not remove the accumulator: each int|None probe must become (int|None, reason); the body must re-thread all reasons into logger.warning with the exact same 6 keys. Additionally windows_attempted is a PLATFORM flag (True only when sys.platform=="win32"; stays False and windows_error None on non-win32, e.g. freebsd13 test) that is distinct from a probe failure reason, so a plain int|None probe cannot convey it — extra plumbing is required. sysconf_pages/sysconf_page_size are also logged individually (None unless the non-positive branch at line 83 is hit) and must be preserved.

So: behaviour preservation is only achievable in the tuple-returning variant, which is relocation rather than removal of the six-variable state; the headline "remove the six-variable accumulator / ~25 LOC" overstates the gain. The debug-log variant is an outright regression against existing tests.
verdict.repro_path: cd C:\Users\prici\haute; python -m pytest tests/test_ram_estimate.py::TestAvailableRam::test_ultimate_fallback_logs_structured_warning tests/test_ram_estimate.py::TestAvailableRamPlatformPaths::test_windows_ctypes_exception_falls_to_default -q  (both assert per-probe reasons ON the single available_ram_fallback_4gib warning event; the debug-log variant of the proposal fails these)
verdict.est_reduction: Realistic ~8-12 LOC net in the behaviour-preserving (reason-tuple) form, not ~25. The ~25 LOC figure is only reachable by dropping the structured warning fields, which is a test-breaking behaviour change.
verdict.recommended_action: Do NOT adopt the literal "per-probe debug-log + single bare warning" form — it regresses tests/test_ram_estimate.py:165-184 and 1721-1750. If pursued, ONLY the variant where each helper returns (bytes|None, reason) and the body re-assembles the SAME six structured keys (proc_meminfo_error, sysconf_error, sysconf_pages, sysconf_page_size, windows_attempted, windows_error) into the unchanged logger.warning("available_ram_fallback_4gib", ...) is acceptable; windows_attempted must remain driven by sys.platform=="win32" (not by the probe's None). Run the full TestAvailableRam and TestAvailableRamPlatformPaths classes after. Given the modest, contract-constrained payoff and the active concurrent edits to the RAM-detection contract noted in review/02-findings (cgroup/4GiB fallback remediation, _execution_admission consumers), churn here is low priority; recommend defer/skip unless bundled with that remediation.

item.current_metrics: 27-line single-expression assignment inside a 419L/cx46 function

item.what_it_does: Reads parquet footer metadata into a _DetailedSourceMetadata and (separately) re-keys its width columns per node.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. `_detailed_parquet_metadata` computes `column_width_keys={str(c): str(c) for c in columns}` (identity mapping), but every caller immediately passes the result through `_source_scoped_metadata`, which OVERWRITES column_width_keys with `{c: f'{node_id}\0{c}'}`. The identity-map construction is therefore always thrown away.
item.current_metrics: redundant dict-comprehension over all columns on every source read
item.proposal: Drop the `column_width_keys=` initialisation in `_detailed_parquet_metadata` (default to `{}` or to the identity inline only if a non-scoped caller exists). Confirm via grep that every call path goes through `_source_scoped_metadata`; if so the field is only ever the scoped form.
item.behavior_preservation: Since `_source_scoped_metadata` replaces the field for all observed callers, removing the discarded initial value changes nothing downstream. Verify no caller uses _detailed_parquet_metadata's result without scoping.
item.est_reduction: ~2 LOC + one O(ncols) comprehension per source read

verdict.evidence:
Re-read _ram_estimate.py:195-245 plus all consumers. The complexity is genuinely INCIDENTAL and the simplification (replace the identity dict-comprehension with {}) is behavior-preserving.

CALL-PATH TRACE (grep-confirmed, src + tests):
_detailed_parquet_metadata has exactly 3 callers:
  (1) _parquet_metadata (line 219) -> immediately unpacks only `.row_count, .column_count` (line 220). NEVER reads column_width_keys. This is the only NON-scoped path; columns 264/275 reach it via _count_source_rows_for_node and also discard everything but row_count.
  (2,3) _detailed_source_metadata_for_node lines 313 & 320 -> ALWAYS wrapped in _source_scoped_metadata(...), which does meta._replace(column_width_keys={column: f"{node_id}\0{column}" ...}) (line 243-245), unconditionally overwriting the field. The identity map built at line 230 is thrown away on every scoped read.

CONSUMERS of column_width_keys are exactly two (lines 571, 808), BOTH using `meta.column_width_keys.get(column, column)` (fallback to the column name). The `sources` tuple they read (built at line 378-388 in _detailed_ancestor_source_metadata) is populated solely from _detailed_source_metadata_for_node, i.e. always the SCOPED form. So a column_width_keys reader never sees a non-scoped meta in any src path.

BEHAVIOR PRESERVATION: For the scoped path, _source_scoped_metadata replaces the field -> identical regardless of init (identity-map vs {}). For the non-scoped _parquet_metadata path, the field is never read -> identical. Critically, because BOTH readers use `.get(column, column)`, even a hypothetical non-scoped reader would be observationally identical between {} and the identity map: get("c","c")=="c" either way. The only way to distinguish {} from the identity map is direct iteration/len/membership of column_width_keys on a non-scoped meta — and no such caller exists (only lines 571 & 808, both `.get`). Tests at test_ram_estimate.py:1258 & 1281 construct _DetailedSourceMetadata manually with explicit scoped keys and never call _detailed_parquet_metadata, so they are unaffected.

CAVEAT (why I flag the wording, not the soundness): _DetailedSourceMetadata is a NamedTuple (lines 195-201) with NO field defaults, so column_width_keys is REQUIRED. The proposal's headline 'Drop the column_width_keys= initialisation' is literally wrong — dropping the kwarg outright raises TypeError at construction. The correct edit is to set it to {} (which the proposal does list as the option). An implementer must use the {} form, not delete the kwarg, and not add a NamedTuple-level default (which would silently weaken the manual test constructions). With that {} form the change is provably behavior-preserving.

Net: incidental complexity (always-discarded identity map), provably equivalent {} replacement, real but small saving.
verdict.est_reduction: ~1-2 LOC net; eliminates one O(n_columns) dict-comprehension per scoped source read (line 230). Saving is real but minor — the read is I/O-dominated by read_parquet_metadata, and the comprehension only runs on the scoped path where the result is immediately overwritten.
verdict.recommended_action: Apply, but implement as column_width_keys={} at line 230 (do NOT literally delete the kwarg — the field is required on the NamedTuple, so deletion raises TypeError; and do NOT add a NamedTuple default, which would dilute the explicit test constructions at test_ram_estimate.py:1258/1285). Both consumers (lines 571, 808) already use .get(column, column), making {} observationally identical to the discarded identity map. Optionally add a one-line comment at line 230 noting that scoped callers overwrite this field, so {} is the unscoped default. No test changes needed; existing _detailed_source_metadata_for_node / _source_column_base_widths tests already cover the scoped path end-to-end.
verdict.repro_path: grep '_detailed_parquet_metadata' src/haute/_ram_estimate.py confirms 3 callers; only _parquet_metadata (line 219, reads row/col only) is non-scoped, lines 313/320 scope via _source_scoped_metadata. grep '.column_width_keys' shows only readers at lines 571 & 808, both `.get(column, column)`. No reader iterates the dict, so {} == identity-map observationally.

item.what_it_does: Rejects pickle globals not on the allowlist with an identical error message.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The exact same 5-line `raise pickle.UnpicklingError(f"Blocked unpickling of {module}.{name} ... _ALLOWED_PICKLE_PREFIXES ...")` message is written twice (class method + joblib monkeypatch).
item.current_metrics: two identical ~7-line allow-or-raise blocks
item.proposal: Extract `_resolve_allowed_global(orig_find_class, self, module, name)` (or a `_blocked_pickle_error(module, name) -> UnpicklingError` factory) and call it from both find_class implementations.
item.behavior_preservation: Same allowlist check (`_pickle_global_is_allowed`), same delegation to the original find_class on match, same error type and text on miss.
item.est_reduction: ~8 LOC

verdict.evidence:
Re-read both blocks in full. _RestrictedUnpickler.find_class (405-413) and the _restricted_joblib_find_class monkeypatch (454-463) each do: `if _pickle_global_is_allowed(module, name): <delegate>; raise pickle.UnpicklingError(<message>)`. I whitespace-normalized and diffed the two raise blocks — they are byte-for-byte identical, including the em-dash, the f-string `{module}.{name}` interpolation, the wording, and the UnpicklingError type (PowerShell compare returned IDENTICAL: True). This is genuinely INCIDENTAL duplication (a verbatim copy-paste), not essential complexity.

Behavior-preservation, tracing every case for the recommended factory form `_blocked_pickle_error(module, name) -> UnpicklingError` (call sites become `raise _blocked_pickle_error(module, name)`):
- MATCH path: Block A keeps `return super().find_class(module, name)`; Block B keeps `return original_find_class(self, module, name)`. The factory touches only the raise lines, so both delegation targets are preserved exactly (this matters — they delegate to DIFFERENT originals: unbound super vs the captured pre-patch NumpyUnpickler.find_class).
- MISS path: identical UnpicklingError text/type produced; tests at tests/test_sandbox.py:151, 207, 224 assert `match="not in.*allowlist"`, and the message still contains "class not in the allowlist" — still passes.
- joblib ImportError fallback (447-450), the _joblib_lock + monkeypatch restore in the finally (465-472), and validate_project_path are all untouched; test_safe_load_does_not_break_subsequent_loads (237/264-268) still holds.
No null/empty/ordering/side-effect case changes.

Caveat on the alternative form: the proposal's option (b) `_resolve_allowed_global(orig_find_class, self, module, name)` folds in the control flow too, but the two sites call different originals with different arities (`super().find_class(m, n)` 2-arg bound vs `original_find_class(self, m, n)` 3-arg). A combined helper must receive the right callable (e.g. pass `super().find_class` as a bound method); doable but more error-prone. Prefer the `_blocked_pickle_error` factory, which is unambiguously behavior-preserving.
verdict.est_reduction: ~6-8 LOC (the 4 duplicated message lines collapse to one shared definition; net ~6)
verdict.repro_path: tests/test_sandbox.py:151 (safe_unpickle blocked), :207 and :224 (safe_joblib_load blocked, match="not in.*allowlist"), :237/264-268 (restore-after-error) all exercise both raise sites and the match path.
verdict.recommended_action: Adopt the `_blocked_pickle_error(module, name) -> pickle.UnpicklingError` factory (option a) and call `raise _blocked_pickle_error(module, name)` from both find_class implementations, leaving the allowlist check and the two distinct delegation lines untouched. Do NOT fold in the control flow via `_resolve_allowed_global` (option b) — the super() vs captured-original asymmetry makes it more error-prone for negligible extra savings. Run tests/test_sandbox.py to confirm green.

item.what_it_does: Compares a numeric actual/expected within a percent tolerance (and formats the mismatch message).
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. Both functions independently recompute `actual_decimal=_to_decimal(actual)`, `expected_decimal=_to_decimal(expected)`, `allowed=abs(expected_decimal)*Decimal(str(tolerance_pct))`. item.title: haute deploy scores every test-quote file TWICE (validate_deploy internally + handle_deploy again), running the full pipeline + model loads redundantly
item.location: src/haute/cli/_deploy.py:157 (validate_deploy) and :173 (score_test_quotes); src/haute/deploy/_validators.py:312 (validate_deploy itself calls score_test_quotes)
item.failure_scenario: `handle_deploy` calls `validate_deploy(resolved_deploy)` at line 157. `validate_deploy` already runs the full scoring pass `score_test_quotes(resolved, tq_dir)` at _validators.py:312 (to surface runtime errors). `handle_deploy` then calls `score_test_quotes(resolved_deploy)` AGAIN at line 173 to print per-file status. So for every `.json` in test_quotes/, the entire pruned pipeline is executed twice — including model artifact loads, optimiser artifact loads, and full Polars collects. On a real pricing pipeline this doubles deploy/CI validation latency for no functional gain, and any non-deterministic cost (MLflow download) is paid twice. There is also a subtle divergence risk: if scoring is flaky, the printed pass (run 2) can disagree with the gate that already passed (run 1).

verdict.evidence: Code trace: handle_deploy (_deploy.py:157) calls validate_deploy(resolved_deploy); validate_deploy internally runs the full scoring pass score_test_quotes(resolved, tq_dir) at _validators.py:312, which calls score_graph at _validators.py:375. handle_deploy THEN calls score_test_quotes(resolved_deploy) again at _deploy.py:173 for the per-file status print -> a second score_graph per .json file. score_graph (_scorer.py:844) -> score_graph_lazy executes the full pruned pipeline incl. model load _load_local_model_cached (_scorer.py:656) and streaming_collect (_scorer.py:870). No guard prevents the 2nd run; for 1-row quotes the dataframe execution cache is None (DEPLOY_LIVE branch, _scorer.py:803), so the lazy graph is rebuilt and re-collected both times (only artifact DISK reads are stat-gated-cached, not the graph build/collect). EXECUTED REPRO (review/03-simplification/repro/platform__BUG-1.py, `uv run python`): one test-quote file on disk, monkeypatched counting score_graph -> output "score_graph calls during validate : 1", "score_graph calls TOTAL : 2", with both invocations byte-identical ([{'rows_in':1,'output_node_id':'out'},{'rows_in':1,'output_node_id':'out'}]); `validation_passed` log confirms the full structural gate ran (faithful reproduction, not a setup short-circuit). Asserts calls_after_validate==1 and total_calls==2 both passed. NOT already catalogued: nearest neighbor is finding #7 (catalog.md:92), which is a distinct CORRECTNESS bug (validate-time scoring uses artifact_paths=None, loading an unpinned model and skipping the contract check) — it concerns what the single scoring path does, not the duplication of the scoring path. No catalog entry (findings 1-69 or refuted section) describes the double execution.
verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\platform__BUG-1.py
verdict.recommended_action: Eliminate the redundant scoring pass. validate_deploy already runs score_test_quotes (to surface runtime errors) and discards the per-file results; have it return those results (or expose them via the raised/returned value) so handle_deploy reuses them for the per-file status print at _deploy.py:173 instead of calling score_test_quotes a second time. This preserves both the validation gate and the printed status while running the full pruned pipeline (model/optimiser loads + Polars collect) exactly once per test-quote file, and also removes the flaky-scoring divergence risk (printed pass can no longer disagree with the gate that already passed). Add a regression test that monkeypatches score_graph with a counter and asserts exactly ONE call per .json file across handle_deploy. Note: the planned fix for finding #7 (threading resolved.artifacts into score_test_quotes) is orthogonal and complementary — apply both, scoring once WITH artifact_paths.
verdict.est_reduction: ~50% of `haute deploy`/CI validation-phase latency in the common case (validate gate + status print currently each run the full pruned pipeline once per test-quote file; de-duplication leaves a single run). Savings scale with test_quotes/ file count and per-file pipeline cost (model/optimiser artifact loads + Polars collects); for 1-row smoke quotes the DEPLOY_LIVE dataframe cache is disabled so the second collect is full, not cached. No correctness change.

item.title: _csv_row_count counts physical lines, not CSV records: quoted fields containing newlines (and trailing blank lines) inflate the row estimate, driving over-aggressive training downsampling
item.location: src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:329-334 (_csv_row_count) consumed by estimate_source_rows:406 and ultimately estimate_safe_training_rows
item.failure_scenario: `_csv_row_count` returns `max(line_count - 1, 0)` where line_count is raw `for _ in f` over the binary handle. A CSV with RFC-4180 quoted fields that embed newlines (common in free-text insurance fields like address/notes) reports MORE lines than data rows, and a file with a trailing blank line also over-counts. Polars' own CSV reader (used at execution time) parses records correctly, so the RAM estimator's `total_rows` is larger than the real row count. Because total_rows feeds `peak_bytes` and the `safe_row_limit = usable_ram / peak_per_row` decision, an over-count makes the estimator believe the dataset is bigger than it is and downsample training MORE aggressively than necessary (prices then derive from a needlessly truncated sample). This is the opposite/independent failure from catalog #31 (which is about available-RAM detection, not row counting) and is not catalogued. Direction is conservative w.r.t. OOM, but it silently corrupts the training row budget; the module's own docstring claims metadata is 'always accurate'.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\platform__BUG-2.py
verdict.evidence: Executed review/03-simplification/repro/platform__BUG-2.py (uv run, polars 1.39.2, EXIT=0; git status -- src tests rating clean). CORE CLAIM (mode A) REAL: _csv_row_count (src/haute/_ram_estimate.py:329-334) returns max(physical_line_count-1,0) over a raw binary `for _ in f` iterator (counts physical lines). For a CSV whose quoted 'notes' field embeds a newline (1 header + 2 records), _csv_row_count returned 3 while pl.scan_csv AND pl.read_csv (the execution-time reader, src/haute/_io.py:509,514) returned 2 -> genuine over-count vs the reader the pipeline actually uses. Control plain 50-row CSV: estimator==polars==50 (no harness off-by-one). SUB-CLAIM (trailing blank line) REFUTED: estimator=4 and pl.scan_csv=4 (Polars also parses the trailing blank as a null record; B3 two-blanks: both =5) -> no divergence vs the real reader, so 'trailing blank lines inflate the estimate relative to the reader' is FALSE. NOT CATALOGUED: catalog entries 1-69 contain no CSV record-vs-line finding; #31 (lines 341-348) is exclusively available-RAM detection (cgroup-blindness + fixed 4 GiB fallback), independent as the claim asserts. The csv/newline grep hits at catalog lines 199/337/339/665/666/668 are unrelated (banding keys, .csv path-traversal example, CRLF request-id injection).
verdict.est_reduction: n/a (read-only audit; no code change made)
verdict.recommended_action: Keep as a low-severity finding, narrowed to the embedded-newline mode only (drop the refuted trailing-blank sub-claim) and correct the impact framing. Severity downgraded from the claim's 'low' framing of training-downsample corruption to a genuinely-low correctness defect because the stated path does NOT reach training downsampling: estimate_safe_training_rows derives total_rows from _detailed_ancestor_source_metadata -> _detailed_source_metadata_for_node, which handles only .parquet for DATA_SOURCE (line 319) and returns None for .csv (=> total_rows None => no downsampling). _csv_row_count is reachable only via estimate_source_rows/_count_source_rows_for_node, and neither has any production caller in src/ outside _ram_estimate.py (only tests exercise estimate_source_rows). So today the over-count corrupts no live training budget; the real defect is that _csv_row_count is record-inaccurate for quoted embedded newlines, contradicting the module docstring 'Metadata is ... always accurate' (line 17). Fix (TDD per repo): replace the physical-line count with a true CSV record count consistent with the execution reader -- e.g. pl.scan_csv(path).select(pl.len()).collect().item() (matches executor.py:1574's own pattern) or csv.reader -- and add a failing-then-passing test for an embedded-newline quoted field (assert 2, not 3). Existing tests at tests/test_ram_estimate.py:201,1386-1400 only cover plain/header-only/empty CSVs and miss this case.

item.title: infer_output_schema swallows ALL cache-write exceptions with a bare `except: pass`, masking real bugs (e.g. a non-serialisable schema or permission error) against the project fail-loud mandate
item.failure_scenario: After the dry-run, `infer_output_schema` writes `{fingerprint, schema}` to `.haute_cache/output_schema.json` inside `try/except Exception: pass`. Any error here (schema containing a non-JSON-serialisable dtype string, a read-only/oversized cache dir, an interrupted write producing a torn file) is silently discarded with no log at all. The immediate effect is benign (cache simply not written), but two real problems hide here: (1) a programming error that makes the schema unserialisable is never surfaced, violating CLAUDE.md's no-silent-fallback rule; (2) a partially-written file from a crash mid-write is left on disk and is later read by the cache-hit branch (lines 99-106) which only catches read/parse errors, not semantic mismatch — compounding catalog #29's stale-cache concern. At minimum this swallow should be narrowed (OSError) and logged like the sibling `corrupt_schema_cache` warning at line 106, not an unconditional `pass`.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\platform__BUG-3.py
verdict.evidence: Direct read of src\haute\deploy\_schema.py:144-148 confirms `try: cache_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); cache_path.write_text(_json.dumps(...)) except Exception: pass  # non-critical` — a bare swallow with NO logging, asymmetric with the sibling cache-READ path at line 105-106 which logs `logger.warning("corrupt_schema_cache", ...)`. Executed repro (exit 0) drove the REAL infer_output_schema (score_graph patched to a synthetic 1-row frame, all I/O in a tempdir, CWD chdir'd because the cache path is CWD-relative). It placed a regular FILE at `.haute_cache` so line 145 `mkdir` raises a genuine OSError; a standalone probe confirmed `FileExistsError: [WinError 183] ... '.haute_cache'` (OSError subclass). Captured the real structlog stream via structlog.testing.capture_logs: the ONLY event during the call was `graph_fingerprint_computed` — zero warning/error and zero failure-named event ('corrupt'/'cache_write'/'schema_cache') — while the function returned {'premium':'Float64'} normally. This proves a real cache-write OSError (read-only / wrong-type cache dir, permission error) is silently discarded against CLAUDE.md's no-silent-fallback / fail-loud mandate.
verdict.est_reduction: N/A (bug item, not a simplification)
verdict.recommended_action: FIX (small). Narrow the swallow to `except OSError as exc:` and log it like the sibling read path, e.g. `logger.warning("schema_cache_write_failed", path=str(cache_path), error=str(exc))` instead of unconditional `pass`. This keeps the deliberate non-blocking behavior (deploy still proceeds and recomputes next run) while surfacing a persistently failing cache (e.g. read-only .haute_cache) per the fail-loud mandate. No test pins the swallow-without-log behavior (only unrelated PermissionError tests at tests/test_deploy_internals.py:3070/3079), so the change is non-breaking; add a TDD regression test asserting a warning event is emitted when the write raises OSError. NOTE for the writer: this is NOT a duplicate of catalog #8 (same line range, but #8 is the distinct cache-KEY/stale-schema defect). Two of the claim's sub-scenarios are OVERSTATED and should not inflate severity: (1) a 'non-JSON-serialisable schema' is effectively unreachable because line 141 builds schema with str() keys AND str() values, so _json.dumps cannot raise a serialization TypeError here — the realistic masked error is an OSError, not a programming bug; (2) the 'torn file silently mis-read, compounding #29/stale cache' framing is incorrect — a truncated/torn JSON file is caught by the read-path `except Exception` at 105-106 (json.loads fails) and logged+recomputed, so it does not silently feed a wrong read. Keep severity low: the immediate effect is benign (cache simply not written); the only genuine harm is diagnosability of a persistently failing write.

item.title: _detect_ci_env treats CI markers as truthy unless EXACTLY in a small falsy set, so providers that set e.g. CI=' false ' (whitespace) or CI='off' are misread as in-CI, allowing a real deploy locally
item.failure_scenario: `_detect_ci_env` returns True when any marker var's value is not in `{'', '0', 'false', 'False', 'FALSE', 'no', 'No', 'NO'}`. The value is matched verbatim with no `.strip()`/`.lower()`, so `CI=' false '`, `CI=off`, `CI=disabled`, or `GITHUB_ACTIONS=n` are all considered truthy → `is_ci=True`. The gate at line 111 (`if not config.dry_run and not is_ci: refuse`) is the ONLY guard preventing a real production deploy from a developer machine. A user who exports a leftover/typo CI variable (or a shell that injects `CI=` with trailing space) bypasses the 'Deploys must go through CI/CD' block and deploys straight to production from local. The whitelist of falsy spellings is brittle; the safe form is `value.strip().lower() not in {'', '0', 'false', 'no', 'off'}` and the gate should fail closed.

verdict.evidence: Ran `uv run python review/03-simplification/repro/platform__BUG-4.py` (EXIT=0, bug reproduced). _detect_ci_env (src/haute/cli/_deploy.py:47-52) builds falsy={"","0","false","False","FALSE","no","No","NO"} and returns True when `value is not None and value not in falsy` — raw compare, no .strip()/.lower(). Repro output: CI=' false ' -> is_ci=True; CI='off' -> True; CI='disabled' -> True; GITHUB_ACTIONS='n' -> True; CI='FaLsE' -> True; CI='No ' -> True. Controls correct: CI='true'->True, CI='false'/'0'/''->False, absent->False. Grep confirms _detect_ci_env/is_ci is used in exactly ONE place — the gate at _deploy.py:110-111 `is_ci=_detect_ci_env(os.environ); if not config.dry_run and not is_ci: raise SystemExit(1)` ("Deploys must go through CI/CD."). No other CI guard in src/; deploy backend _mlflow.py:329-376 only reads DATABRICKS_RATING_HOST/TOKEN, so a spurious is_ci=True + non-dry-run + valid pipeline proceeds to a real production deploy (deploy_resolved at _deploy.py:200) from a local machine. Not in catalog: Grep of review/02-findings/catalog.md for _detect_ci_env|is_ci|CI/CD|falsy|deploy gate found no matching finding (routes__BUG-4.py is an unrelated _friendly_error bug). Existing tests (tests/test_cli_deploy.py:49-62 cleared-env block; tests/test_cli_fail_loudly.py:373 truthy markers) cover only canonical truthy/absent values — the falsy-but-misread spellings are untested, so a normaliser fix breaks no existing test.
verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\platform__BUG-4.py
verdict.est_reduction: Closes the only fail-open path on the sole production-deploy gate: prevents an unintended real prod deploy from a developer machine when a stray/typo CI var (CI=off/disabled/no, mixed-case, or whitespace-padded ' false ') is present.
verdict.recommended_action: Confirm and fix (fail closed). Normalise before comparing in _detect_ci_env: `v = (env.get(var) or "").strip().lower(); if v not in {"", "0", "false", "no", "off"}: return True`. Per CLAUDE.md TDD, first add a failing parametrized test (extend tests/test_cli_deploy.py / test_cli_fail_loudly.py) asserting CI=' false ', CI='off', CI='disabled', GITHUB_ACTIONS='n', CI='FaLsE', CI='No ' all still BLOCK a non-dry-run deploy, plus a regression test that absent/CI='true' behave unchanged. Keep severity low: trigger is a self-inflicted atypical local env state, no remote vector, but blast radius (production deploy) justifies the cheap fix.

item.function: the solve / train / explore job-lifecycle action families
item.what_it_does: Maintains three parallel async-job caches (active job map + completed-result map) with start/progress/complete/fail transitions and entry-count LRU trimming.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The three families are structurally identical: startX writes `{...s.Xjobs,[nodeId]:{...}}`; updateXProgress is a verbatim `if(!job)return s; {...job,progress}`; completeX/failX each repeat the same 5-step ritual — pull job, destructure it out of Xjobs, touchCachedResult(XRecency), build nextCached, trimCacheByRecency(..., MAX_CACHED_X, pinned), then return {Xjobs:remaining, Xresults:bounded.records}. updateSolveProgress/updateTrainProgress/updateExploreProgress are byte-for-byte identical except the field name. Only the nextCached *shape* genuinely differs per family; everything around it is boilerplate.
item.current_metrics: len ~405 lines for the three families; updateXProgress x3 are ~7 lines each, 100% duplicated; complete/fail x3 share ~25-line skeletons
item.proposal: Extract two generic helpers parameterised on the slice name: (1) `updateJobProgress(set, slice, nodeId, progress)` collapsing the three identical updateXProgress bodies into one call site each; (2) `commitJobResult({set, jobSlice, resultSlice, recency, max, pinned, nodeId, buildCached, onEvict})` that performs the pull-job / destructure / touch / trim / return dance, taking a per-family `buildCached(job, prevResult)` closure for the only varying part. solve/train keep their extra derived-cache eviction via the `onEvict` hook. This removes ~150 LOC and makes the three caches provably consistent.
item.behavior_preservation: Each helper reproduces the exact same set() return shape (same keys, same `job?remaining:slice` guard used by completeTrainJob's direct-completion path, same trim order). The varying nextCached is supplied verbatim by buildCached, so frontier-extraction, error defaults, and structuralVersion fields are unchanged. No null/empty path changes: the `if(!job)return s` early-out and the `?? ""` fallbacks move inside the helper unchanged.
item.est_reduction: ~150 LOC; removes 3 fully-duplicated functions

verdict.evidence:
Re-read useNodeResultsStore.ts:681-1086 in full plus the helpers (trimCacheByRecency 509-539, cache* 246-507) and call sites (ModellingConfig.tsx:145-155 direct-completion; test 296-340, 1841-1887).

PART A — updateXProgress helper (SOUND). The three bodies (solve 689-696, train 922-929, explore 1017-1024) are structurally identical: `const job=s.Xjobs[nodeId]; if(!job) return s; return {Xjobs:{...s.Xjobs,[nodeId]:{...job,progress}}}`. A single `updateJobProgress(set, slice, nodeId, progress)` reproduces this exactly. This part is genuinely incidental and behaviour-preserving. ~12 LOC saved.

PART B — commitJobResult helper (the bulk of the claimed ~150 LOC): the proposal MISDESCRIBES the code; a single generic helper is NOT behaviour-preserving as specified.

1. The proposal asserts "the `if(!job) return s` early-out … move[s] inside the helper unchanged." FALSE for completeTrainJob (931-965): it deliberately has NO early-out. It destructures the job out unconditionally, uses `job?.jobId ?? ""` / `job?.configHash ?? ""`, and returns `trainJobs: job ? remainingJobs : s.trainJobs`. This is the documented direct-completion path used by ModellingConfig for sync/error results (call sites 145/148/152) and is pinned by tests "completeTrainJob works even without an active job" (310) and "falls back to 'Model'" (1880). completeSolveJob (701) and completeExploreJob (1029) DO early-out on `!job`. So the single `?? ""` fallback the proposal mentions exists ONLY in train; solve/fail-train/explore read `job.jobId` directly (no `??`). One helper cannot both early-out-on-null AND tolerate-null; it would need a per-family flag, eroding the saving and the "provably consistent" claim.

2. completeSolveJob is NOT a single-closure buildCached. It is a two-phase build (717-733): construct nextCached, compute initialPointIndex from a 12-line frontier-extraction block (703-715), then conditionally RE-spread `result: deriveSolveResultForFrontierPoint(nextCached, initialPointIndex)` referencing the half-built object. The frontier-extraction + initialPointIndex logic is unique and cannot live in a uniform "ritual."

3. The onEvict side effects are three DIFFERENT shapes, not a uniform hook: solve complete/fail (743-746, 782-785) delete `_optimiserPreviewCache[evicted]` then re-`cacheOptimiserPreview` the survivor; train complete (953-960) has a THREE-way branch keyed on `bounded.records[nodeId]?.result.status === "error"` (delete vs cacheModellingPreview), train fail (988-991) UNCONDITIONALLY deletes `_modellingPreviewCache[nodeId]`; explore complete/fail (1041-1053, 1073-1085) have NO side effects. The train-complete branch depends on result CONTENT, not just the evicted set, so `onEvict(evictedIds)` is insufficient — it needs the survivor + status too.

4. The three failX nextCached are not just "different shape" — they have different SOURCES: failSolve spreads from `s.solveResults[nodeId] ?? {error-default}` (759-763, preserving prior originalResult), failTrain hardcodes a fresh error TrainResult (974), failExplore preserves `previous?.result ?? null` (1062-1064). Each is its own buildCached, but combined with #1/#3 the per-family parameters (buildCached, source, early-out flag, bespoke onEvict) dominate the boilerplate that remains.

Conclusion: PART A is a clean dedup. PART B can be partially extracted (the trimCacheByRecency call + remaining-jobs return is already routed through the shared trimCacheByRecency helper), but the asymmetries — train's missing early-out, solve's two-phase frontier build, and three distinct content-dependent eviction side effects — mean a faithful commitJobResult carries so many per-family hooks that the realistic net saving is well under the advertised ~150 LOC and the "provably consistent" benefit is largely illusory. Worthwhile only if scoped to PART A plus a modest helper for the literal trim+return tail; the full generic merge as written is unsound (drops the train direct-completion semantics).
verdict.est_reduction: Realistic ~30-50 LOC (updateXProgress dedup ~12 LOC + a thin trim/return tail helper), NOT the claimed ~150 LOC. The complete/fail bodies stay largely intact due to per-family early-out, frontier, and eviction asymmetries.
verdict.recommended_action: Adopt PART A only: extract `updateJobProgress(set, slice, nodeId, progress)` to collapse the three byte-identical updateXProgress functions (sound, behaviour-preserving, S effort). Reject PART B as specified: a single commitJobResult that moves the `if(!job) return s` early-out inside the helper would break completeTrainJob's direct-completion path (tests at lines 310, 1880; call sites ModellingConfig.tsx:145-155). If consolidation of complete/fail is still desired, scope it to a narrow `trimAndReturn({records, recency, max, pinned, jobSlice, resultSlice, remainingJobs, keepJobs})` tail helper that does ONLY the trimCacheByRecency-call + return-shape, leaving each family's bespoke nextCached build, frontier extraction, null-guard policy, and eviction side effects in place — and require a full dev/reviewer pair given the silent-wrongness risk around the train null path. Verify no regression via the existing LRU/pinned/direct-completion/preview-cache tests in useNodeResultsStore.test.ts.
verdict.repro_path: frontend/src/stores/useNodeResultsStore.ts:931-965 (completeTrainJob no-early-out + 3-way eviction) vs :698-751 (completeSolveJob two-phase frontier build) vs :1026-1054 (completeExploreJob no side effects); tests frontend/src/__tests__/stores/useNodeResultsStore.test.ts:310,1880; call sites frontend/src/panels/ModellingConfig.tsx:145-155

item.what_it_does: After every graph mutation, recomputes persistedFingerprint/structuralFingerprint/panelContextFingerprint and conditionally bumps the matching version counters + dirty flag.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The block `const nextFingerprint = computeStructuralFingerprint(...); ...(nextFingerprint === state.structuralFingerprint ? {} : {structuralFingerprint: nextFingerprint, structuralVersion: state.structuralVersion + 1})` is copied 8 times verbatim. The dirty patch `dirty: computeDirty(state.lastSavedSnapshot, state.savedPersistedFingerprint, nextPersistedFingerprint)` is copied 7 times. setNodes/setEdges additionally use an IIFE-inside-spread pattern (`...(() => {...})()`) purely to compute these derived fields, which is harder to read than a named helper.
item.current_metrics: 6 mutators + undo/redo; ~190 lines; the structural-version ternary duplicated 8x, the dirty patch 7x, panelContext patch already extracted (good precedent)
item.proposal: Mirror the existing `computePanelContextPatch` helper with two siblings: `computeStructuralPatch(state, nodes, edges, preamble)` returning `{}` or `{structuralFingerprint, structuralVersion: +1}`, and `computePersistedPatch(state, nodes, edges, preamble)` returning `{persistedFingerprint, dirty}`. Each mutator becomes `set(state => ({ ...historyPart, [field]: value, ...computePersistedPatch(...), ...computePanelContextPatch(...), ...computeStructuralPatch(...) }))`, deleting the IIFEs. undo/redo similarly call the patches instead of inlining the ternary.
item.behavior_preservation: The helpers return the identical object shapes the inline code produces, computed from the same args; spread order preserves the same precedence (later keys win, but no key overlaps). The 'fingerprint unchanged ⇒ omit key ⇒ version preserved' semantics are reproduced exactly by the `=== ? {} : {...}` inside the helper. Raw mutators keep their early hasOnly* short-circuits before calling the patches, so position/UI-only fast paths are untouched.
item.est_reduction: ~60-80 LOC; eliminates 2 IIFEs and 13 duplicated ternary/patch blocks

verdict.est_reduction:
~55-75 LOC realistic (item's 60-80 is slightly optimistic once two ~12-15 line helpers + call-site spreads are added back). Removes 2 IIFEs (setNodes L445-465, setEdges L473-493) and collapses 8 structural ternaries + 8 persisted {persistedFingerprint, dirty:computeDirty(...)} blocks.</est_reduction>
<parameter name="effort">M
verdict.evidence:
Complexity is INCIDENTAL and the refactor is state-equivalent, but the proposal's written behavior-preservation rationale is imprecise in two spots that are exactly where a careless impl would regress, so marginal not sound.

TRACE (frontend/src/stores/useGraphStore.ts):
- Structural ternary `...(nextFingerprint===state.structuralFingerprint ? {} : {structuralFingerprint, structuralVersion:+1})` appears at L458-463 (setNodes), L486-491 (setEdges), L511-516 (setPreamble), L559-564 (setNodesRaw), L599-604 (setEdgesRaw), L621-626 (setPreambleRaw) = 6 in the `?{}:{...}` form; undo L657-660 and redo L688-691 use the DIFFERENT `structuralFingerprint:next; structuralVersion: next===cur?cur:cur+1` form (8 total).
- Persisted `{persistedFingerprint:next, dirty:computeDirty(state.lastSavedSnapshot, state.savedPersistedFingerprint, next)}` at L452-457, L480-485, L505-510, L541-548, L582-589, L651-656 (undo), L682-687 (redo) = 8 (item says 7).
- computePanelContextPatch (L393-405) returning {} | {panelContextFingerprint,panelContextVersion:+1} is in-file precedent — extraction is established and matches CLAUDE.md "share functionality already built".

WHY STATE-EQUIVALENT (all observable behavior is final state; both test files — structuralVersion.test.ts and consolidation.test.ts — assert only via getState(), never patch-object identity):
1. History mutators: proposed computeStructuralPatch(state,nodes,edges,preamble) and computePersistedPatch(state,nodes,edges,preamble) compute from the same args the inline code uses (mutated value + other two from state) and read lastSavedSnapshot/savedPersistedFingerprint from state — identical result. computeDirty args identical at every site. ✓
2. undo/redo: current code ALWAYS assigns structuralFingerprint=next (even when next===current, a no-op since strings are primitives) and bumps version only on change. A {}-returning computeStructuralPatch OMITS both keys when unchanged. Different PATCH OBJECT, but identical POST-MERGE STATE (untouched vs reassigned-to-same-value). Same for panelContext. So the item's claim 'helpers return the identical object shapes the inline code produces' is FALSE for the unchanged-undo/redo case — only state-equivalence holds. Reviewer/implementer must verify final state, not object shape.

THE TWO LANDMINES the proposal under-specifies:
A. setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw have a MID-FUNCTION `if (sameStructural) return {...persistedPatch,...panelContextPatch}` (L550-552, L590-592) that gates computeStructuralFingerprint. The item only names the early `hasOnly*` guards ('keep their early hasOnly* short-circuits'); it does NOT mention sameStructural. computeStructuralPatch must be invoked ONLY in the non-sameStructural branch, else it eagerly calls computeStructuralFingerprint and breaks the throwing-toJSON guards at structuralVersion.test.ts L211-260 ('does not recompute the structural fingerprint for visual-only raw node changes').
B. The position-only path (setNodesRaw L530-535) returns {nodes, dirty:computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes(state,nodes)} — it deliberately OMITS persistedFingerprint and uses a DIFFERENT dirty function. It must NOT be replaced by computePersistedPatch. The item correctly says 'position/UI-only fast paths are untouched', so this one is covered — but it's the same hazard class as (A).

No external consumer (usePipelineAPI, useNodeResultsStore, usePanelGraphContext, useGraphCanvasState, etc.) reads patch objects — they subscribe to final state fields — so nothing else is sensitive. TypeScript: helpers return Partial<Pick<...>> exactly as computePanelContextPatch does; trivial.
verdict.repro_path: cd frontend && npx vitest run src/stores/__tests__/useGraphStore.structuralVersion.test.ts src/stores/__tests__/useGraphStore.consolidation.test.ts — establish green baseline, then re-run after refactor; both suites assert only final getState() values so they pin the state-equivalence that matters. Pay special attention to structuralVersion.test.ts:211 (visual-only no structural recompute), :86 (panelContext not bumped on position/selection), and consolidation.test.ts:630/680/747 (throwing-toJSON on visual/position-only) — these break if computeStructuralPatch/computePersistedFingerprint is called before the hasOnly*/sameStructural short-circuits.
verdict.recommended_action: PROCEED with two corrections to the plan. (1) Mirror computePanelContextPatch exactly: add computeStructuralPatch(state,nodes,edges,preamble) returning {} | {structuralFingerprint,structuralVersion:+1}, and computePersistedPatch(state,nodes,edges,preamble) returning {persistedFingerprint,dirty}. (2) In setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw, preserve BOTH the early hasOnly* returns AND the mid-function `if (sameStructural)` return, invoking computeStructuralPatch only in the non-sameStructural branch; do NOT touch the computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes path. For undo/redo, replacing the inline ternary with the {}-returning helpers is fine because final state is unchanged — but the implementer must validate via state assertions, not object-shape, since the patch object legitimately differs. Per CLAUDE.md TDD: run the two suites green first, refactor, re-run; no test changes needed (they already pin final state). Worthwhile but classified marginal due to the imprecise 'identical object shapes' rationale and the unstated sameStructural guard, both of which are silent-regression traps for the perf-sensitive throwing-toJSON tests.

item.function: parse a raw frontier-point record into a typed SolveResult
item.what_it_does: Validates and projects an untyped frontier-row object (constraints, lambdas, scenario stats/histogram, factor tables, history) into the strongly-typed SolveResult shown in the panel.
item.why_complex: PARTLY INCIDENTAL. `deriveSolveResultForFrontierPoint` (lines 413-477) and the fallback object inside `updateFrontierAfterSelect` (lines 860-893) independently assemble the same SolveResult fields (iterations, cd_iterations, clamp_rate, history, scenario_value_stats/histogram, factor_tables, frontier_error) with subtly different defaulting, which is exactly the kind of drift the catalog flags elsewhere. The flat-vs-nested scenario_value_stats branch (282-328) lists all 11 percentile fields twice (once for nested, once for the `sv_*` flat aliases).
item.current_metrics: deriveSolveResultForFrontierPoint len 64, the two stat branches ~46 lines duplicated field-by-field; the select fallback re-lists 8 of the same fields
item.proposal: (1) Drive scenario_value_stats from a single `{field: [nestedKey, flatKey]}` table and a loop, instead of two hand-written object literals. (2) Have `updateFrontierAfterSelect`'s no-frontier fallback call a shared `emptyPointResult(originalResult)` builder that `deriveSolveResultForFrontierPoint` also uses for its non-overridden fields, so the two paths can never diverge on which fields reset to undefined/null.
item.behavior_preservation: The table-driven stats loop reads the same keys in the same order and throws via the same numericFrontierValue on the same non-finite inputs, so valid/invalid/absent rows behave identically. The shared empty-result builder reproduces the current literal field-for-field (verified against lines 862-872), so the select path's output is unchanged.
item.est_reduction: ~40-60 LOC; removes one duplicated 11-field literal and one duplicated fallback literal

verdict.evidence:
Re-read useNodeResultsStore.ts:255-477 and 814-903 in full, plus OptimiserSolveResult (api/types.ts:643-663) and the store tests.

PART (1) table-driven scenario_value_stats (282-328) — SOUND. The duplication is genuinely incidental: the flat branch ALREADY declares the exact field->key table (flatStats, lines 300-312). The nested branch (283-298) reads stats.<field> and labels errors "scenario_value_stats.<field>"; I verified nestedKey === field for all 11 fields (mean/std/min/max/p5/p25/p50/p75/p95/pct_increase/pct_decrease). The flat branch reads row[svKey] and labels with the flat key (note the only non-obvious mapping p50->sv_median). A single loop over an 11-entry {field: flatKey} table drives BOTH branches with identical throw-ordering (first non-finite field, in array order) and identical labels (nested: `scenario_value_stats.${field}`; flat: the flat key). numericFrontierValue is the same throw source. The presence-guard (line 313: `Object.values(flatStats).some(field => row[field] !== undefined)`) and the nested-vs-flat dispatch (line 283 `row.scenario_value_stats != null`) are unchanged. Tests at lines 1297-1309 assert the full 11-field flat projection including sv_median->p50, so a regression in this loop would be caught. ~20-25 LOC of duplicated numericFrontierValue calls removed.

PART (2) shared emptyPointResult builder — MARGINAL (behavior-preserving but over-justified, low value). The no-frontier fallback (862-872) is literally `{...originalResult, iterations:undefined, cd_iterations:undefined, clamp_rate:undefined, history:null, scenario_value_stats:undefined, scenario_value_histogram:undefined, factor_tables:undefined, frontier_error:undefined}` — exactly 8 resets, and the proposal's "verified against 862-872" matches. A helper reproducing it is behavior-identical: those defaults ARE observable because the final result (877-893) uses `selectResult.X ?? pointResult.X` (iterations/cd_iterations/scenario stats/histogram/factor_tables), `=== undefined ? pointResult.X` (clamp_rate/history), and frontier_error is NOT in the override list so it passes through from pointResult.

HOWEVER the dedup rationale is overstated. deriveSolveResultForFrontierPoint (457-476) overrides ALL 8 of those fields with parsed row values (iterations/cd_iterations via optionalFrontierInteger, clamp_rate, history via optionalHistory, scenario_value_stats/histogram, factor_tables, frontier_error:undefined). If derive started from emptyPointResult(original), every blank would be fully SHADOWED — it cannot shorten derive at all and contributes nothing to derive's correctness. The proposal's claim "the two paths can never diverge on which fields reset to undefined/null" is misleading: the paths legitimately DO differ — derive sets `warning: converged ? undefined : NON_CONVERGED_WARNING` (line 474, load-bearing at the direct call sites 731 and 799), while the fallback intentionally does NOT touch warning (harmless: line 892 overwrites warning in the final result regardless). So the only real saving from part (2) is collapsing the ~9-line fallback literal to one call (~7 LOC); it creates no genuine anti-drift guarantee.

LOC: realistic ~25-30 LOC (part1 ~20-25 + part2 ~7), below the proposal's "40-60" which inflates the figure by treating derive's self-overridden fields as dedupable.

NO behavior would break in either part as proposed; the verdict is marginal (not sound) because the bundled item carries an inflated est_reduction and a misleading "can never diverge" justification for a part-2 change that delivers little, at risk:medium.
verdict.est_reduction: ~25-30 LOC realistically (part1 table-driven stats ~20-25; part2 fallback-literal collapse ~7). The proposal's "40-60" is inflated — it double-counts deriveSolveResultForFrontierPoint's 8 fields as dedupable, but they are fully shadowed by derive's own overrides.

(1263-1310) covers the stats projection incl. sv_median->p50; "selectFrontierPoint uses a point-specific warning..." (1312-1340) and "updateFrontierAfterSelect uses the backend non-convergence warning..." (1477-1497) guard the warning divergence; "updateFrontierAfterSelect updates result metrics" (1446-1475) exercises the no-frontier fallback path (but does NOT assert the 8 reset fields, so part-2 reset semantics are not directly covered).
verdict.recommended_action: Split the item. ACCEPT part (1): replace the two hand-written 11-field stat literals with one loop over the existing flatStats-shaped table, keeping the per-branch label convention (nested: `scenario_value_stats.${field}`; flat: the flat key) — clear, safe win. DOWNGRADE/OPTIONAL part (2): if done, limit it to factoring ONLY the no-frontier fallback literal (862-872) into emptyPointResult(originalResult); do NOT route deriveSolveResultForFrontierPoint through it (its 8 fields are fully shadowed, so it neither shortens derive nor prevents drift) and drop the inaccurate "can never diverge" justification. Add a test asserting the fallback resets (iterations/cd_iterations/clamp_rate/history/scenario_value_stats/histogram/factor_tables/frontier_error) when selectResult omits them, to lock in part-2 behavior before refactoring.
