item.function: project edges to trace / hover / zoom visual states with a per-edge cache
item.what_it_does: Returns edges restyled for whichever mode is active (trace > hover > zoom > none), reusing a projection cache and pruning it.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. Four branches (trace, hover, zoom, default) each open with `const seenIds = new Set(); const next = edges.map(e => { seenIds.add(e.id); ...projectEdgeWithCache(...) }); pruneEdgeProjectionCache(edgeProjectionCache, seenIds); return next`. Only the per-edge `(visualState, visuals)` decision differs; the iterate+seen+prune scaffold is written four times.
item.current_metrics: len ~107; the seenIds/map/prune skeleton duplicated 4x (~6 lines of pure boilerplate each)
item.proposal: Extract `projectEdges(edges, classify)` where `classify(edge) => {visualState, visuals}` is the only per-mode input, and have it own the seenIds accumulation + final pruneEdgeProjectionCache call. The three active branches become a one-line `return projectEdges(edges, e => traceConnectedEdgeIds.has(e.id) ? {...} : {...})`. The default branch keeps its `if(cache.size>0)cache.clear(); return edges` fast path.
item.behavior_preservation: projectEdges calls projectEdgeWithCache with identical (edge, endpoints, visualState, visuals) tuples and prunes against the same seenIds set, so cache hits/misses and the returned array identity are unchanged. The endpoints lookup `endpointsByEdgeId.get(e.id)!` stays inside the loop. Branch priority (trace before hover before zoom) is preserved by call order.

verdict.evidence:
Re-read useTracing.ts:426-533 (edgesWithTrace) plus helpers projectEdgeWithCache (123-142) and pruneEdgeProjectionCache (144-149). Complexity is INCIDENTAL: the three active branches (trace 428-468, hover 471-509, zoom 512-529) are byte-identical in scaffold — `const seenIds=new Set(); const next=edges.map(e=>{seenIds.add(e.id); const endpoints=edgeAdjacency.endpointsByEdgeId.get(e.id)!; return projectEdgeWithCache(edgeProjectionCache,e,endpoints,visualState,visuals)}); pruneEdgeProjectionCache(edgeProjectionCache,seenIds); return next` — differing ONLY in the per-edge (visualState,visuals) decision (and hover's one-time suppressHoverMarkers setup at 472-475). Extracting projectEdges(edges,classify) that owns seenIds + the single prune call is behavior-preserving:
1) Cache hits/misses unchanged — projectEdgeWithCache receives identical (cache,edge,endpoints,visualState,visuals) tuples; its hit test (cached.source===edge && cached.visualState===visualState) ignores the freshly-allocated visuals literal in both old and new code.
2) Array identity preserved — each active branch already returns a fresh .map array; projectEdges returns a fresh mapped array. CRITICAL: the default branch (531-532) `if(cache.size>0)cache.clear(); return edges` returns the ORIGINAL edges reference and CLEARS (not prunes) the cache. Proposal correctly keeps it OUT of projectEdges. This asymmetry is pinned by an existing test — useTracing.test.ts:442 `expect(edgesWithTrace).toBe(params.edges)` (referential toBe) — which would fail if anyone routed the default case through the helper.
3) Prune timing identical — projectEdges accumulates seenIds over the same edges it maps and calls pruneEdgeProjectionCache once at end.
4) endpointsByEdgeId.get(e.id)! stays inside the loop; the `!` is compile-time only so missing-entry behavior (passing undefined) is unchanged.
5) Branch priority trace>hover>zoom>default is in the surrounding if-chain, untouched.
6) Empty edges: []→[], prune no-op. Identical.
The existing test suite (useTracing.test.ts) already pins per-mode styling (332-348, 364-417: trace-active/lite/dimmed filter+animated+className), default array identity (442), cache reuse without endpoint re-reads (459-481), and trace-over-hover priority (515-537) — so any regression in styling/identity/ordering/caching is caught. No external callers: projectEdgeWithCache/pruneEdgeProjectionCache are module-private and used only here. Honest deductions (do not affect behavior): the proposal's "becomes a one-line return" is over-stated for the hover branch, which must retain its 2 setup lines (hoveredNode/suppressHoverMarkers) captured by the classify closure; and the classify indirection adds a small layer. The one real footgun — never call projectEdges for the default branch — is explicitly acknowledged by the proposal.
verdict.est_reduction: ~25-35 LOC (3 active branches shed ~5 lines of seenIds/map/prune scaffold each; hover branch keeps its 2 setup lines, so realistic net is slightly below the proposal's 30-40)
verdict.repro_path: frontend/src/hooks/useTracing.ts:426-533; helpers at 123-149; regression net at frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useTracing.test.ts (lines 332-348, 364-417, 439-442, 459-481, 515-537)
verdict.recommended_action: Accept. Define projectEdges(edges, classify) inside the hook body (closing over edgeAdjacency + edgeProjectionCache, or taking them as params) that does: build seenIds, map each edge to projectEdgeWithCache(edgeProjectionCache, e, edgeAdjacency.endpointsByEdgeId.get(e.id)!, classify(e).visualState, classify(e).visuals) — calling classify ONCE per edge into a local — then call pruneEdgeProjectionCache once and return the array. Rewrite the trace/hover/zoom branches to delegate (hover branch keeps its suppressHoverMarkers setup and passes a closure). MUST leave the default branch (cache.clear(); return edges) exactly as-is and NOT route it through projectEdges — guarded by the existing toBe(params.edges) test at line 442. useMemo dependency arrays stay unchanged. Run frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/useTracing.test.ts to confirm green; per CLAUDE.md TDD, no new test required since the existing suite already pins identity, per-mode styling, ordering, and cache reuse.

item.function: render the inputs→result calculation 'well' (and its banding variant)
item.what_it_does: Draws the dark rounded box of ExpressionChainRows followed by a final accented result/band row with a positioned dot.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The two functions share ~50 lines verbatim: the identical outer `<div style={{background:'rgba(0,0,0,.12)',borderRadius:6,padding:'10px 12px',marginTop:8,...}}>`, the identical `entries.map(entry => <ExpressionChainRow .../>)` block (lines 256-269 ≡ 341-354), and the identical absolute-positioned dot `<div style={{position:'absolute',left:3,top:hasEntries?15:7,width:7,height:7,...}}/>` (277-282 ≡ 364-369). Only the final-row content (formula+sub+result vs input→band) differs.
item.current_metrics: renderUnifiedBox len 81, renderBandingBox len 71; ~50 shared lines including 14-line entries.map and 6-line dot, duplicated
item.proposal: Extract a `<CalculationWell entries={entries}>{finalRow}</CalculationWell>` component (or local render fn) that owns the outer box, the entries.map, and the dot+border chrome, taking the differing final row as children/prop. renderUnifiedBox and renderBandingBox each shrink to building their final-row JSX and delegating.
item.behavior_preservation: The extracted chrome emits byte-identical markup/styles (same hasEntries-driven borderTop/marginTop and dot top offset), and the entries.map keys on entry.column exactly as today, so the DOM and InputSourceTree nesting are unchanged. The banding `aria-label` and result `title` stay on their respective final rows.

verdict.evidence: Re-read CalculationHero.tsx:235-389 in full plus ExpressionChain.tsx and both test files. The complexity IS incidental (removable), not essential: renderUnifiedBox (235-316, ~82 LOC) and renderBandingBox (318-389, ~72 LOC) share verbatim chrome — outer box style is byte-identical (246-254 == 332-340); the entries.map -> ExpressionChainRow block with the same 5 props and the same subSources/InputSourceTree child guard is identical (256-269 == 341-354); the absolute-positioned dot div is identical (277-282 == 364-369); and the final-row wrapper STYLE object is identical (272-275 == 356-363). Both paths call the same buildUnifiedEntries() and derive hasEntries the same way, so nothing forces the duplication. Traced every case for behaviour-preservation: (1) !calculation -> both return renderCalculationMissing(); the proposal keeps callers building their own final row, so this guard stays — safe. (2) hasEntries false vs true drives borderTop/marginTop:6/paddingTop:8 AND dot top:7-vs-15; both boxes compute this from the same entries, so an extracted well that receives `entries` reproduces it byte-identically — safe. (3) subSources child conditional (Object.keys(...).length>0) and key={entry.column} are identical in both maps — safe to hoist. (4) result `title` / band `title` stay on inner content spans (children) — unaffected. THE ONE SHARP EDGE: in renderBandingBox the aria-label={`Banding: ${summary}`} sits ON the final-row wrapper div (356-363) — the exact div the proposal says CalculationWell should "own (... the dot+border chrome)". renderUnifiedBox's wrapper has NO aria-label. Test panels/__tests__/CalculationHero.test.tsx:376 asserts getByLabelText("Banding: driver_age=22 -> young"). So if the wrapper/dot chrome is hoisted into CalculationWell, the implementer MUST thread the aria-label through as a prop or the banding test breaks; the proposal's own text ("aria-label stays on the final row") is in tension with "owns the dot+border chrome" since the label lives on that chrome wrapper. Clean resolution: have CalculationWell own only the outer box + entries.map (the larger ~22 verbatim lines) and let each caller keep its own final-row wrapper (dot+border+content) — that removes the bulk of the duplication, leaves aria-label trivially in place, and is provably behaviour-preserving; only the 6-line dot stays duplicated. No snapshot tests exist (snapshot glob empty) and no test pins the dot top/borderTop, but the proposal's "byte-identical markup" bar is the stricter and is achievable under the outer-box-only split. Net: genuine, low-risk dedup with one named caveat (aria-label on the hoisted chrome) that must be respected to stay correct — hence marginal, not fully sound.
verdict.est_reduction: ~40-50 LOC (outer-box + entries.map dedup is the safe bulk; reaching ~55 requires also hoisting the dot+wrapper, which triggers the aria-label caveat)
verdict.repro_path: Existing tests cover the contract: panels/__tests__/CalculationHero.test.tsx:351-379 (banding: getByLabelText("Banding: driver_age=22 -> young") and Policies source row) pins the aria-label and the entries.map output for the banding box; trace/__tests__/calculationHero.errorUI.test.tsx case A pins the !calculation alert. No DOM-snapshot guard exists for the dot top/borderTop, so byte-identity of that chrome is on the implementer, not the test suite.
verdict.recommended_action: Accept with the constraint that CalculationWell owns ONLY the outer box + entries.map (and optionally the dot via an explicit prop), while each caller keeps/threads its own final-row wrapper so the banding aria-label stays on the labelled div — verify getByLabelText("Banding: ...") still passes. If the dot+wrapper are hoisted, pass the aria-label as a prop applied to that wrapper. Add a small DOM assertion (dot top offset and borderTop presence when entries exist vs not) so future edits can't silently drift the chrome, since no current test guards it.

item.function: choose the column set passed to the Modelling/Optimiser editors
item.what_it_does: For pass-through Modelling/Optimiser nodes, uses upstream columns when present else falls back to the node's own previewed _columns.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The exact block `const effectiveCols = upstreamColumns.length > 0 ? upstreamColumns : ((node.data as Record<string,unknown>)?._columns as {name:string;dtype:string}[] | undefined) || []` is duplicated verbatim in both the MODELLING and OPTIMISER switch arms, including the awkward double cast already computed once at line 880 (`currentColumns`).
item.current_metrics: ~6 lines duplicated across 2 arms; currentColumns already derives the same _columns cast at line 880
item.proposal: Hoist `const effectiveCols = upstreamColumns.length > 0 ? upstreamColumns : currentColumns` once (currentColumns already exists at line 880 — move it above renderEditor or compute a memo), and reference it in both arms. Removes the repeated inline cast.
item.behavior_preservation: currentColumns is defined as `((node.data...)._columns as {name;dtype}[]) || []` — the identical value the inline expression computes; the only behavioural input is `upstreamColumns.length > 0`, unchanged. Both editors receive the same array reference they do today.
item.est_reduction: ~8 LOC

verdict.evidence:
Re-read NodePanel.tsx lines 640-880 and 1036 in full. Complexity is INCIDENTAL: the effectiveCols computation is duplicated verbatim in the MODELLING arm (805-807) and OPTIMISER arm (818-820), and its fallback `((node.data as Record<string,unknown>)?._columns as {name;dtype}[]) || []` is ALREADY computed once at line 880 as `currentColumns`. The only input distinguishing arms is `upstreamColumns.length > 0`, which is shared, so there is no essential per-arm logic.

Behavior-preserving — traced every case of `upstreamColumns.length > 0 ? upstreamColumns : currentColumns` vs the inline form:
(1) upstream non-empty -> both return the same `upstreamColumns` memo reference (line 646 useMemo).
(2) upstream empty + `_columns` truthy -> inline returns `node.data._columns`; currentColumns (line 880) is also `node.data._columns || []` -> SAME object reference. node/node.data is a stable prop, never reassigned (only usage at 685) and never mutated, so currentColumns reflects the identical `_columns` the inline reads.
(3) upstream empty + `_columns` null/undefined -> inline yields a fresh `[]`; currentColumns yields a fresh `[]`. Sole difference: currentColumns is one shared `[]` across both arms, but only one switch arm executes per render (a node is MODELLING xor OPTIMISER), so unobservable. The `| undefined` in the inline cast annotation is type-only, zero runtime effect.

TDZ/ordering verified safe: currentColumns is declared at 880 AFTER renderEditor (677), but renderEditor is a closure invoked exactly once at line 1036 (grep confirmed no other call site), which runs after 880 initializes. So no Temporal Dead Zone at call time. Hoisting currentColumns above renderEditor (proposal's suggestion) is feasible since `node` is guarded non-null at line 661; either placement is behavior-preserving. `effectiveCols` is consumed exactly once per arm (only as the upstreamColumns prop). No frontend test references effectiveCols/currentColumns, so no test coupling to reference identity that the refactor could break.
verdict.est_reduction: ~6-8 LOC (removes duplicated double-cast across 2 switch arms; reuses existing currentColumns binding)
verdict.repro_path: N/A (read-only verification; no behavioral defect)
verdict.recommended_action: Apply. Hoist `const effectiveCols = upstreamColumns.length > 0 ? upstreamColumns : currentColumns` using the existing currentColumns (line 880). Preferred for cleanliness: move the `currentColumns` declaration (and optionally `availableColumns`) from line 880 to just above renderEditor (after the `if (!node) return null` guard at line 661, e.g. near line 675), then reference currentColumns in both arms. item.function: build cheap string signatures of upstream edges for useMemo dependency keys
item.what_it_does: Produces delimiter-joined strings keying inputSources/upstreamColumns/hasApiInputUpstream memos so unrelated nodeMap rebuilds don't churn them.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. Three of the four signature builders share the identical `edges.map(edge => \`${edge.source}\u00XX${lookup(nodeMap[edge.source])}\`).join(delim)` shape, differing only in which field of the source node they read (_columns sig, nodeType, label) and the delimiter chars. The hand-picked /// control chars are easy to mis-pair.
item.current_metrics: 4 functions, ~24 lines; 3 are the same map/join template with a different field accessor
item.proposal: Provide one `upstreamSignature(edges, nodeMap, project)` where `project(srcNode, edge) => string` is the only variant, and define the three signatures as thin wrappers (`upstreamNodeTypeSignature = (e,m) => upstreamSignature(e,m,(n)=>String(n?.data?.nodeType ?? ""))`). columnsSignature stays as the inner per-node serializer reused by the _columns projector.
item.behavior_preservation: Each wrapper emits the same concatenation (same fields, same delimiters preserved inside the project fn / fixed join char), so the memo keys are byte-identical and React's memo invalidation is unchanged. Pure functions, no null-path change (the `?? ""` defaults move into project).

verdict.evidence:
Re-read NodePanel.tsx:479-503 plus call sites 631/645/654 and types in editors/_shared.tsx:56-74. The proposal's core premise — "three of the four share the identical edges.map(edge => `${edge.source}\uXX${project(...)}`).join(delim) shape, differing only in which field they read" — is FALSE in two ways.

(1) Entry-template shape differs. upstreamColumnsSignature (483) entry = `${edge.source}${columnsSignature(srcCols)}` join . upstreamNodeTypeSignature (493) entry = `${edge.source}${nodeMap[edge.source]?.data?.nodeType ?? ""}` join . upstreamLabelSignature (499) entry = `${edge.id}${edge.source}${nodeMap[edge.source]?.data?.label ?? ""}` join . The label one is NOT `${edge.source}\uXX${value}`: it prefixes edge.id (with its own ) BEFORE edge.source, and uses TWO in-entry separators ( and ). This edge.id prefix is load-bearing — upstreamLabelSignature keys the inputSources memo (644) whose objects carry edgeId: e.id (638), so the key must vary on edge.id. The common template cannot reproduce this without putting edge.source after edge.id, breaking byte-identity.

(2) Delimiters vary (join  vs ; in-entry  vs  vs both). The proposed signature upstreamSignature(edges, nodeMap, project) has NO delimiter/prefix parameter, so as literally specified it would unify delimiters and drop the edge.id prefix — i.e. it CHANGES the bytes of all three signatures, contradicting the "byte-identical memo keys" guarantee. To truly preserve bytes the helper needs ~4 params (entry-prefix, in-entry sep, join char, projector), and the label wrapper must fold its whole entry into project — collapsing the abstraction's benefit.

Correctness note: delimiters only need per-signature collision-freedom (each signature keys a SEPARATE memo: upstreamSchemaSignature->upstreamColumns 646-653, upstreamTypesSignature->hasApiInputUpstream 655-659, upstreamSourceLabelSignature->inputSources 632-644), so cross-signature delimiter unification would not actually break invalidation. Behavioral memo-identity tests exist (NodePanel.test.tsx:1306, 1354) and would guard real regressions, but they do not assert byte content. So the dedup is not a correctness risk, but the proposal as written is NOT behavior-preserving for the label signature and overstates the shared shape (only columns+nodeType are genuinely the same template, and even they differ in delimiter). The "easy to mis-pair control chars" complexity is relocated into project/params, not removed.
verdict.est_reduction: ~4-6 LOC realistically (only upstreamColumnsSignature + upstreamNodeTypeSignature are dedup-able, with a join-delimiter param); the claimed 12-15 LOC assumes a 3-way unification that is not byte-preserving
verdict.repro_path: Code-trace only (no runtime repro needed). Compare entry templates at NodePanel.tsx:488 vs 495 vs 501; note 501 prefixes edge.id with  before edge.sourcevalue while 488/495 are edge.source<sep>value. Memo wiring at 631-659; identity tests at frontend/src/panels/__tests__/NodePanel.test.tsx:1306 and 1354.
verdict.recommended_action: Do NOT apply as written — the headline 3-way `upstreamSignature(edges,nodeMap,project)` would change the label signature's bytes (drops edge.id prefix, unifies delimiters), so it is not the byte-identical no-op claimed. If any dedup is wanted, restrict it to upstreamColumnsSignature + upstreamNodeTypeSignature only, add an explicit join-delimiter parameter, and leave upstreamLabelSignature untouched (its edge.id-prefixed dual-separator entry is a different shape). Given ~4-6 LOC payoff against added parameter surface and churn near memo-invalidation-critical code, lowest-risk call is to skip.

item.what_it_does: Runs up to DOWNSTREAM_PREVIEW_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT in-flight previewNode calls, refilling as each settles, until a work set is exhausted or the request is superseded/aborted.
item.why_complex: PARTLY INCIDENTAL. Both functions implement the same bounded worker pool: an `activeCount`/`activePreviewCount`, a drain loop `while(active<LIMIT && hasWork && requestStillCurrent())` that launches previewNode(...).then/catch/finally, with the same abort/superseded handling (`isAbortError||isPreviewSupersededError`) and the same `requestStillCurrent()` gate. previewStaleUpstream is essentially propagate's drain loop without the DAG dependency bookkeeping.
item.current_metrics: propagate len ~163 (cx high), previewStaleUpstream len ~52; the drain/launch/limit/abort skeleton (~30 lines) is shared
item.proposal: Extract a `runBoundedPreviewPool({items, limit, isCurrent, signal, runOne})` helper that owns active-count, the drain loop, and the standard then/catch(abort|superseded|toast)/finally wiring, returning a Promise that resolves when drained or cancelled. previewStaleUpstream becomes a direct call; propagate supplies `runOne` plus its DAG `settleNode` callback for refill ordering. This isolates the genuinely-essential DAG scheduling (pendingParents/hasChangedParent) from the boilerplate pool mechanics.
item.behavior_preservation: The helper reproduces the same concurrency cap, the same per-task terminal handling (abort/superseded swallow vs warning toast), and the same `requestStillCurrent()`/`signal.aborted` short-circuits, so cancellation timing and the toast set are unchanged. propagate keeps its exact settleNode/queueNodePreview logic — only the launch+limit plumbing is shared — so the cascade ordering and the columnsChanged propagation are byte-for-byte the same.
item.est_reduction: ~40-60 LOC and a sizeable cx drop on propagate

verdict.repro_path: frontend/src/hooks/usePipelineAPI.ts:331-494 (propagate), 674-726 (previewStaleUpstream); tests frontend/src/hooks/__tests__/usePipelineAPI.propagation.test.ts:656-710 and usePipelineAPI.test.ts:1452-1498 pin the concurrency cap but NOT abort/finish timing.
verdict.evidence: The two "pools" share only a superficial active-count + while(active<LIMIT && hasWork && current()) skeleton; their contracts diverge on every axis, so a single runBoundedPreviewPool({items,limit,...}) helper cannot be byte-for-byte behavior-preserving. (1) WORK-SET DISCOVERY: previewStaleUpstream drains a STATIC array via nextIndex++ (674-698). propagate's readyQueue is NOT a known work set — items enter only via queueNodePreview when pendingParents hits 0 AND hasChangedParent (415-419,485-490); the queue grows DURING draining as settleNode recursively releases children. The proposal's {items} param assumes an up-front work set that does not exist for propagate. (2) RE-ENTRANCY: drainReadyQueue calls settleNode(nodeId,false) for un-previewable nodes mid-while WITHOUT incrementing activeCount (440-442,continue), and settleNode recurses into the DAG → queueNodePreview → re-enters drainReadyQueue, pushing more onto readyQueue that the same while keeps draining. previewStaleUpstream has zero re-entrancy. A generic runOne:Promise cannot express synchronous settles that mutate the work queue re-entrantly. (3) TERMINAL PREDICATE: previewStaleUpstream finishes on a launched-task counter settledCount>=length (690). propagate finishes on the conjunction settledNodeIds.size>=reachableNodeIds.size && activePreviewCount===0 && readyQueue.length===0 (399-405) because reachable nodes get settled WITHOUT ever being previewed (else settleNode(childId,false) at 421; un-previewable at 441) — a launch counter would never complete. Different finish predicates, not one dressed two ways. (4) ABORT LIFECYCLE (the killer): propagate registers an EAGER controller.signal.addEventListener("abort",finishPropagation,{once:true}) (391), pre-checks signal.aborted (387-389), and tears the listener down in finishPropagation (379-382) — so on abort it RESOLVES IMMEDIATELY while tasks are still in flight. previewStaleUpstream has NO listener; it observes abort only lazily inside drain() reached via finishOne AFTER an in-flight task settles (685-687,721) — so on abort it waits for ≥ the current batch to settle. A shared helper must pick one: adopting propagate's eager listener changes when previewStaleUpstream().then(...) fires fetchPreviewImmediate and the previewBusy toggle (728-738); adopting the lazy poll strips propagate's eager-abort guarantee and listener cleanup. The item's claim that "cancellation timing... unchanged" is FALSE unless the helper carries BOTH strategies as a flag — i.e. a two-behavior superset, not a simplification. (5) MID-LOOP requestStillCurrent: propagate re-checks requestStillCurrent() INSIDE the while (435) to stop launching on a structuralVersion bump; previewStaleUpstream's while (694-697) checks only activeCount/nextIndex. Different short-circuit granularity. The complexity is ESSENTIAL: a faithful helper needs so many callbacks/flags (item-supplier, settle hook, finish predicate, abort mode, mid-loop gate) that it is LOC-neutral-to-negative and less readable; a "clean" helper silently alters previewStaleUpstream's cancellation/finish timing or breaks propagate's eager abort — a latent bug in a concurrency path the tests do not fully pin. The only genuinely shared, safe surface is the ~3-line error classifier (isAbortError||isPreviewSupersededError swallow + previewErrorDetail + warning toast at 466-475 vs 715-720), far below the claimed bounded-pool extraction.
verdict.est_reduction: Claimed ~40-60 LOC is not achievable safely. A faithful two-behavior helper is roughly LOC-neutral (≈0, possibly negative). The only sound extraction is a ~3-line error-classification/toast helper saving ~5-8 LOC total with no cx win on propagate.
verdict.recommended_action: REJECT the bounded-pool extraction as proposed — it is unsound: propagate's readyQueue is a DAG-released (not static) work set drained re-entrantly from settleNode, its finish predicate is a settled-set conjunction (not a launch counter), and its abort path uses an eager signal listener whereas previewStaleUpstream polls abort lazily after each batch — so a shared helper either changes previewStaleUpstream's cancellation/finish timing or loses propagate's eager-abort, neither behavior-preserving. If any cleanup is desired, limit it to extracting ONLY the shared error-classification+toast pattern (isAbortError||isPreviewSupersededError swallow → previewErrorDetail → addToast("warning",...)) into a tiny helper; leave the two pool/scheduler control flows intact. Before merging even that, add an abort-timing regression test (abort mid-flight, assert previewStaleUpstream resolves only after in-flight settles vs propagate resolves immediately) since current tests pin only the concurrency cap.

item.function: enumerate the input/dependency columns of an optimiserApply node detail
item.what_it_does: Lists objective/quote-id/scenario/constraint columns (online) or factor names (ratebook) referenced by an optimiserApply step.
item.why_complex: INCIDENTAL. The set of mode-keyed fields (objective_column, quote_id_column, scenario_index_column, scenario_value_column, constraints keys; ratebook factor.name) is hand-walked here and also rendered in OptimiserApplyDetail.tsx — two places that must agree on what an optimiserApply 'depends on'. A new field added to the detail type must be edited in both.
item.current_metrics: ~28-line mode branch; the same field list reappears in the detail renderer
item.proposal: Centralise an `optimiserApplyDependencyColumns(detail): string[]` in a shared trace helper (alongside modelScoreFeatureColumns / bandingRows, which already follow this pattern) and have both traceStoryView and the detail component consume it. Mirrors the existing single-source helpers for the other detail types.
item.behavior_preservation: The helper returns the same column names in the same conditions (guarded by isOptimiserApplyErrorDetail and mode checks), and the caller still feeds them into the same Set, so dependency-step highlighting is unchanged. Pure extraction, no control-flow change.
item.est_reduction: ~20 LOC and removes a cross-file drift risk

verdict.evidence:
Re-read traceStoryView.ts:165-193, OptimiserApplyDetail.tsx, NodeDetailBlock.tsx, the precedent helpers (modelScoreHelpers.ts:29 modelScoreFeatureColumns, bandingRows.ts:75 bandingRows), optimiserApplyHelpers.ts, and the type union (types/trace.ts:219-260).

COMPLEXITY IS INCIDENTAL (extractable): the optimiser_apply branch hand-walks one conceptual list ("columns this node depends on") that is mode-keyed. The codebase already establishes the exact extraction convention the proposal cites: modelScoreFeatureColumns(detail):string[] and bandingRows(detail) are shared helpers consumed by both targetStepDependencyColumns AND their *DetailBlock renderers. An optimiserApplyDependencyColumns(detail):string[] mirrors this. So extraction is sound on principle.

BEHAVIOR-PRESERVING — the traceStoryView side only. Traced every case the branch handles: (a) error variant skipped via isOptimiserApplyErrorDetail (the OptimiserApplyErrorNodeDetail has no column fields — correct to skip); (b) ratebook: guarded by Array.isArray(factors), adds factor.name only when truthy; (c) online: adds objective_column / quote_id_column / scenario_index_column / scenario_value_column each under its own truthiness guard, plus Object.keys(constraints ?? {}). A pure extraction returning string[] that the caller spreads into the existing Set is byte-for-byte identical (Set de-dup/insertion unchanged). The downstream consumers (targetStepDependencyColumns -> targetDependencyStepIds / defaultExpandedStepIds, asserted via trace-step-card-*/data-target-step in TracePanel.test.tsx incl. the online optimiser fixture at L749-825) stay green.

THE OVERSTATED PART (why not 'sound'): the proposal's stated end-state is "have BOTH traceStoryView and the detail component consume it" and that this "removes a cross-file drift risk." That is not a like-for-like substitution for the renderer. OptimiserOnlineDetail does NOT build a dependency-column list: it uses scenario_value_column/objective_column as LABELS (scenarioLabel/objectiveLabel), quote_id_column as a summary CHIP, and routes constraints through optimiserConstraintNames(), which is deliberately a SUPERSET (it unions detail.constraints keys with selected.constraints and every candidate's constraints + lambda_terms keys — optimiserApplyHelpers.ts:29-42) — a different computation than the dependency walk (detail.constraints keys only). OptimiserRatebookDetail uses factor.name to render a table, not to build a column list. So the two places "agree" only on the field NAMES existing, not on producing the same list; the renderer would still reference the individual fields for labels/chips regardless of the helper. Unlike the modelScore/banding precedents (where the helper IS the rendering data structure for both sides), the renderer here cannot cleanly consume the helper — making it consume it would be either a dead import or an artificial refactor of label/chip logic, and the cross-file drift mitigation is weaker than claimed.
verdict.est_reduction: ~12-18 LOC net (the ~28-line branch collapses to a short loop spreading a helper result). NOT the full ~20 LOC + bidirectional drift removal claimed — the renderer keeps its per-field label/chip references and its superset constraint union.
verdict.repro_path: Extract optimiserApplyDependencyColumns(detail: OptimiserApplyNodeDetail): string[] into optimiserApplyHelpers.ts (guarded by isOptimiserApplyErrorDetail + mode checks, returning the same names under the same truthiness conditions). Consume it from traceStoryView.targetStepDependencyColumns by spreading into dependencyColumns. Run frontend TracePanel.test.tsx (esp. the online optimiser fixture L749-853 and ratebook L855+) to confirm step-card highlighting/expansion is unchanged.
verdict.recommended_action: Accept a NARROWED version: extract optimiserApplyDependencyColumns(detail):string[] and consume it from traceStoryView ONLY (one-sided single-source, fully behavior-preserving, regression-covered, matches the modelScoreFeatureColumns/bandingRows convention). REJECT the proposal's bidirectional framing: do NOT force OptimiserApplyDetail.tsx to consume the helper — its fields are used for labels/chips and it relies on a deliberately broader optimiserConstraintNames() union, so the renderer is not the same computation and the 'two places must agree / removes cross-file drift' claim is overstated.

item.title: Direct synchronous train completion caches configHash="", making the result render as permanently stale (config-changed banner shown for a just-computed result)
item.location: frontend/src/stores/useNodeResultsStore.ts:931-943 (completeTrainJob: `configHash: job?.configHash ?? ""` when no active job) consumed by frontend/src/hooks/useStaleConfigEstimate.ts:60 (`isStale = !!cachedResult && cachedResult.configHash !== configHash`) and frontend/src/panels/ModellingConfig.tsx:87,230,289
item.failure_scenario: completeTrainJob's docstring (lines 934-935) states it 'also works for direct completion (no active job) used by ModellingConfig for sync/error results'. On that path `job` is undefined, so the cached result is stored with `configHash: ""`. useStaleConfigEstimate computes `isStale = cachedResult.configHash !== hashConfig(config)`; since hashConfig of any non-empty modelling config is never the empty string, isStale is true the instant the result lands. The ModellingConfig staleness banner (TrainingActionsAndResults isStale at :230/:289) therefore tells the user 'config changed since last run' for a result that was just computed for exactly the current config — undermining the entire staleness signal for synchronously-completed training results. Async (JobStore-backed) completions are unaffected because they carry the real job.configHash from startTrainJob.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\frontend__NEWBUG-01.py
verdict.est_reduction: n/a (correctness/UX defect, not a perf finding)
verdict.evidence: Chain confirmed by executed repro + code-trace; Python port validated against Node reference (identical digests: hashConfig({})='3horh', hashConfig(live)='d452x8'). (1) ModellingConfig.tsx:145 (immediate-error) and :148 (sync completion) call completeTrainJob(nodeId, result) WITHOUT a prior startTrainJob, so in completeTrainJob `job = s.trainJobs[nodeId]` is undefined. (2) useNodeResultsStore.ts:942 stores `configHash: job?.configHash ?? ""` -> "". (3) useStaleConfigEstimate.ts:59-60: `configHash = hashConfig(config)` (always non-empty; djb2 of "{}" = "3horh"), `isStale = !!cachedResult && cachedResult.configHash !== configHash` => "" !== nonEmpty => unconditionally true. (4) TrainingActionsAndResults.tsx:101-104 renders "Config changed since last training" whenever isStale, no post-train guard. (5) Async completions (useBackgroundJobs.ts:109) carry real job.configHash from startTrainJob (ModellingConfig.tsx:142) and are unaffected. Repro output: `isStale immediately after sync train = True (SHOULD be False)` while control `isStale after ASYNC train = False`. Existing test useNodeResultsStore.test.ts:310-321 asserts configHash=="" is stored but never the staleness consequence, so the bug is uncaught.
verdict.recommended_action: Confirm as a real low-severity cache/UX defect. NOT a duplicate of catalog #68 (that is djb2 hash-COLLISION making a changed config read as NOT stale; this is the opposite false-positive: a fresh sync result reads as stale due to stored configHash=""). Fix: thread currentConfigHash into the direct-completion calls in handleTrain (ModellingConfig.tsx:145,148,152) or extend completeTrainJob to accept an explicit configHash for the no-job path instead of defaulting to "". Add a behavioral test asserting a direct sync completion for config X yields isStale===false against X and true after a real config edit.

item.title: parseBranches mis-splits a conditional whose `then` value itself contains the word 'when' (or a nested when/then), dimming the wrong branch in the trace waterfall
item.location: frontend/src/trace/CalculationHero.tsx:73-102 (parseBranches regex `/when\s+(.+?)\s+then\s+(.+?)(?=\s+when\s|\s+otherwise\s|$)/gi`), consumed at :458-459 and the matched-branch dimming at :481-511
item.failure_scenario: The branch parser is a hand-rolled regex over the human-rendered `expression_text`/`substituted_text`. Its lookahead terminates a branch's `then` value at the next ` when ` / ` otherwise ` / end. If a branch result legitimately contains the token 'when' (e.g. a string literal, a column named like `flagged_when_high`, or a nested when/then expression that the backend rendered inline), the regex cuts the result early and/or starts a spurious extra branch, so the rendered conditional shows the wrong number of branches and `isBranchMatched`/`data-matched` may highlight the wrong arm. This is display-only (the trace waterfall is a post-hoc explanation, never the executed value), so it cannot mis-price, but it can show an actuary an incorrect 'taken branch' for non-trivial conditionals. Note the backend-provided `taken_branch_index` (when present, :460-463) overrides the regex match, so the failure is confined to conditionals where the backend did not supply an index and the branch text contains the delimiter tokens.

verdict.repro_path: C:\Users\prici\haute\review\03-simplification\repro\frontend__NEWBUG-02.py
verdict.evidence: parseBranches regex (CalculationHero.tsx:75-76) `/when\s+(.+?)\s+then\s+(.+?)(?=\s+when\s|\s+otherwise\s|$)/gi` is the only branch-splitter; no upstream guard. Repro (faithful port; ALSO validated against real V8: `node -e` on the verbatim regex returned identical split [["status = 'open'","'review"]]). Case A: input "when status = 'open' then 'review when overdue' otherwise 'no action'" -> branch[0].result == "'review" (truncated at inner ' when ', losing "when overdue'"). Case B (nested when/then, a real backend shape per _expression_parser.py:645-664 which renders nested conditionals inline into then_text): input "when region='EU' then when vat then 1.2 otherwise 1.0 otherwise 1.0" -> branch[0].result=="when vat then 1.2" (nested else lost) and otherwise=="1.0 otherwise 1.0" (garbled). Case C (wrong-arm dimming, backend supplied NO taken_branch_index): substituted "when tier='gold' then rate scaled when vip applies 0.8 otherwise 0.0" with result_value 0.8 -> isBranchMatched(0)==False (0.8 truncated away), full matched_flags computation (port of CalculationHero.tsx:481-486) == [False, True], i.e. data-matched='true' on the otherwise arm while the genuinely-taken gold arm is dimmed. All assertions pass, exit 0. NOT in catalog.md (grep NEWBUG-02/parseBranches/taken_branch_index/isBranchMatched/CalculationHero/conditional-display = no matches; items 10/11 are unrelated codegen).
verdict.est_reduction: n/a
verdict.recommended_action: Accept as a real low-severity display-only bug. Confirmed scope: (1) the rendered branch TEXT and branch COUNT corruption (Cases A & B) is UNCONDITIONAL — branches.map() at CalculationHero.tsx:481-511 renders parseBranches' condition/result verbatim regardless of taken_branch_index, so even a correct backend index does not fix the garbled arm text; (2) the wrong-ARM highlight (Case C) is additionally gated by absence/non-integer taken_branch_index (override at :460-463/:482-483), which the claim correctly concedes and which is reachable (_trace_enrichment.py:1527-1528 only sets it when non-None). No mis-pricing risk: trace waterfall is post-hoc enrichment over already-executed Polars values (_trace_enrichment.py:1515-1532). Fix: do not hand-roll a regex over the human-rendered text — have the backend emit a structured branch list (the parser already walks the when/then/otherwise AST and even tracks nested_branches/dimmed_branches, so the structured data exists) and consume that instead of re-parsing expression_text/substituted_text on the frontend. If a frontend parser must remain, it cannot be a flat regex; it needs token/paren-aware recursive parsing of nested when/then. Per CLAUDE.md TDD: add a failing CalculationHero render test for a conditional whose then-result contains ' when ' (string literal, column like flagged_when_high, and an inline nested when/then) asserting correct branch count, untruncated result text, and correct data-matched arm when taken_branch_index is absent.

item.title: failSolveJob with no prior result fabricates a converged=false/objective=0 SolveResult that getOptimiserPreview surfaces as a real (non-error-styled) result row
item.location: frontend/src/stores/useNodeResultsStore.ts:753-790 (failSolveJob: nextCached falls back to a synthetic `{status:'error', total_objective:0, baseline_objective:0, constraints:{}, lambdas:{}, converged:false}` when s.solveResults[nodeId] is absent) → getOptimiserPreview :1090-1096 → OptimiserPreview.tsx:140
item.failure_scenario: When a solve fails and there was NO previously cached result for the node, failSolveJob stores a placeholder SolveResult with all-zero objectives and converged=false, plus `error`. getOptimiserPreview returns this cached entry unconditionally (it only nulls on absence, not on `.error`), so OptimiserPreview receives a SolveResult that looks structurally like a completed solve (objective 0, empty constraints) carrying an error string. Depending on how the preview renders error vs result, an all-zero 'objective = 0 / no constraints' panel can be shown alongside the error rather than a pure error state. Because the optimiser is browser-only and never persists prices, this is a display/UX defect, not a mispricing — but a 0-objective result is a misleading thing to render for a failed solve. (Distinct from catalogued item #34's frontier-failure-on-completed case, which is about a *successful* solve whose frontier failed; this is the *failed*-solve placeholder path.)

verdict.evidence: failSolveJob (useNodeResultsStore.ts:760-762) writes synthetic {status:'error', total_objective:0, converged:false, constraints:{}, lambdas:{}} + error when solveResults[nodeId] is absent. buildOptimiserPreview (235-244) drops `error`; OptimiserPreviewData (OptimiserPreview.tsx:47-54) has no error field. getOptimiserPreview (1090-1096) returns null ONLY on absence, never on .error. App.tsx:613 `if (optPreview)` mounts <OptimiserPreview> with no .error check. OptimiserPreview.tsx:369,386 render subtitle 'Not converged' and collapsedMeta 'Not converged | Objective: 0'; the panel has NO branch on result.status==='error' or data.error (the only status==='error' checks at 642/801 are unrelated Export/rates async states). Repro exit 0 asserts statusSummary=='Not converged', collapsedMeta=='Not converged | Objective: 0', renderedResultStatus=='error'. Smoking gun asymmetry: the codebase already applies the correct guard at OptimiserConfig.tsx:228 (`cached.error ? null : cached.result`) and getModellingPreview at store.ts:1100 (`cached.result.status==='error' -> null`); only the optimiser-preview path omits it. Not in catalog (scanned items 1-56; #43 is the distinct successful-solve frontier-failure case).
